Create the initial Rust workspace and the four persistence crates prescribed by Level 2. Implement only the foundational identifier/value types needed by later storage work.

This task must leave the repository compiling and ready for the next implementation task.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read these documents before editing code:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. persistence crate boundaries.md
  3. design/level-2/002. canonical encoding and revision identity.md

Do not implement agents, Markdown, sessions, CLI commands, HTTP APIs, or web code.

docs.title: Files to create
docs.text:
Create:

Cargo.toml
crates/sr-core/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-core/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-core/src/ids.rs
crates/sr-core/src/encoding.rs
crates/sr-store/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store-memory/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store-memory/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store-sqlite/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/lib.rs

If a file already exists because another task ran first, preserve compatible work and modify only what is required.

docs.title: Workspace setup
docs.text:
The root Cargo.toml must declare a Cargo workspace containing the four crates.

Use the repository's selected Rust edition consistently. If none has already been selected, use the current stable edition supported by the local toolchain and record it only in Cargo metadata; do not create a design decision outside this task.

docs.title: sr-core requirements
docs.text:
Implement strongly typed wrappers for:

  • EntityId
  • RevisionId
  • SnapshotId
  • RootName
  • ObjectType
  • EncodingVersion

Requirements:

  • identifiers are not type aliases to String;
  • RevisionId and SnapshotId can hold a fixed BLAKE3 digest;
  • IDs implement the ordinary traits needed for map keys and tests: equality, ordering where sensible, hashing, clone/copy where sensible, and debug formatting;
  • textual display and parsing of digest IDs are deterministic and round-trip;
  • invalid textual IDs return an error instead of panicking;
  • RootName validates obvious invalid empty names;
  • backend-specific information must not appear in these types.

encoding.rs should define the EncodingVersion type and a placeholder/public boundary for canonical encoding used by the next task. Do not invent a full domain value model yet.

docs.title: Dependency rules
docs.text:
• sr-core depends on no Scriberig crate.
  • sr-store depends on sr-core.
  • sr-store-memory depends on sr-store and sr-core as needed.
  • sr-store-sqlite depends on sr-store and sr-core as needed.
  • No inverse dependency is allowed.

Add BLAKE3 only where needed for digest representation/testing. Do not add SQLite implementation dependencies yet unless required only to make the empty backend crate compile.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add unit tests for:

  • RevisionId display/parse round trip;
  • SnapshotId display/parse round trip;
  • invalid digest text is rejected;
  • two different digest bytes are different IDs;
  • empty RootName is rejected;
  • the workspace compiles with all four crates.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
Run at minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

If formatting fails, run cargo fmt, then rerun the checks.

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not create SQL tables.
  • Do not implement snapshots.
  • Do not implement an agent API.
  • Do not add CLI binaries.
  • Do not create semantic/domain types such as Paragraph or Function.
  • Do not make IDs depend on file paths or database row IDs.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Root Cargo workspace exists.
  • [x] All four persistence crates exist in the workspace and compile as empty crate shells.
  • [x] Dependency direction matches Level 2; scriberig-core has no Scriberig dependency, scriberig-store depends on core, and both backends depend on store and core.
  • [x] Core ID types are strongly typed.
  • [x] Digest IDs have deterministic text round-trips.
  • [x] Tests pass across the workspace.
  • [x] No higher-level product dependency was introduced by the four persistence crates.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Apply Licensing Metadata to Rust Crates
Objective
docs.text:
Apply the platform/product licensing split to every existing Rust crate without creating new crates or changing runtime behavior.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md
  2. design/level-2/001. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md
  3. the current Rust workspace/package-layout design, if present
  4. every Cargo.toml that will be modified

This task is metadata-only.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Run this task only after Rust crate manifests exist.

If the repository contains no Rust Cargo.toml package manifests yet:

  • do not create placeholder crates;
  • do not create empty manifests solely to satisfy this task;
  • report that the task is not yet applicable.

If a workspace root exists, distinguish the workspace manifest from package manifests.

docs.title: Files to Modify
docs.text:
Inspect all Rust manifests in the repository, including:

Cargo.toml
crates/*/Cargo.toml

and any other package manifests discovered by the workspace.

Modify only manifests that need explicit or inherited licensing metadata adjusted.

Do not edit Rust source files in this task.

docs.title: Classification Rule
docs.text:
Classify each crate by architectural responsibility.

Use this default:

Reusable platform crate -> Apache-2.0
Integrated product/runtime crate -> AGPL-3.0

Do not classify solely from the crate name.

Read the crate description, dependencies, public API, and controlling designs before deciding.

docs.title: Apache-2.0 Crates
docs.text:
A crate should normally be Apache-2.0 when its primary purpose is reusable infrastructure, including responsibilities such as:

  • core identity/value types;
  • immutable storage abstractions;
  • concrete reusable storage backends;
  • graph/schema libraries;
  • query libraries;
  • migration/change libraries;
  • projection infrastructure;
  • reusable domain adapters;
  • protocol definitions;
  • reusable client SDKs;
  • reusable agent-facing interfaces that do not execute the integrated Scriberig runtime.

The fact that an AGPL product depends on a crate does not make the reusable crate AGPL.

docs.title: AGPL-3.0 Crates
docs.text:
A crate should normally be AGPL-3.0 when its primary responsibility is operating the integrated Scriberig product, including:

  • the reference server application when it is the integrated Scriberig server;
  • integrated agent execution/orchestration;
  • product-specific workflows that coordinate the complete Scriberig runtime;
  • binaries whose purpose is to embed and operate that integrated runtime.

Do not mark a generic server protocol library AGPL merely because a server application uses it.

Do not mark reusable agent interfaces AGPL merely because the integrated agent runtime consumes them.

docs.title: CLI Classification
docs.text:
Do not assume all binaries are AGPL.

A CLI that primarily acts as a reusable client over public platform/server APIs should normally remain Apache-2.0.

A CLI or executable that embeds substantial integrated AGPL runtime/orchestration behavior should follow the AGPL product layer.

If a CLI mixes both responsibilities and the boundary cannot be determined from current designs, stop and report the ambiguity instead of guessing.

docs.title: Cargo Metadata
docs.text:
Each distributable crate must have a correct Cargo license declaration.

Use Cargo-supported SPDX license metadata corresponding to the license assigned by the controlling design.

Do not use a dual-license expression unless the design explicitly assigns two licenses to the same crate.

Do not use a repository-wide inherited value if doing so would make a mixed-license workspace inaccurate.

Workspace inheritance is acceptable only for groups of crates whose inherited value is correct.

If workspace package metadata currently defines one license for all members and the workspace contains both Apache and AGPL crates, refactor the metadata so each package resolves to the correct license without changing package behavior.

docs.title: Dependency-Direction Check
docs.text:
While classifying crates, inspect internal Scriberig dependencies.

Expected direction:

Apache reusable crate
        ^
        |
AGPL integrated product crate

AGPL product crates may depend on Apache platform crates.

An Apache reusable crate should not depend on an integrated AGPL product crate.

If such a reverse dependency exists:

  • do not hide it by changing the reusable crate's license just to make the graph look consistent;
  • do not move code during this metadata task;
  • record the dependency and report that an architectural refactor is required.

docs.title: Preserve Existing Package Information
docs.text:
Do not change:

  • package names;
  • versions;
  • descriptions except where needed to understand classification and separately requested;
  • dependency versions;
  • features;
  • targets;
  • workspace membership;
  • publish settings;
  • edition settings;
  • build scripts.

This task changes licensing metadata only.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After editing:

  • enumerate every Rust package in the workspace;
  • verify every distributable package resolves to a license;
  • verify reusable packages resolve to Apache-2.0;
  • verify integrated product/runtime packages resolve to AGPL-3.0;
  • verify no package accidentally declares both licenses unless a separate design explicitly requires dual licensing;
  • verify workspace inheritance does not erase the mixed-license boundary;
  • run Cargo metadata/workspace validation sufficient to prove the manifests still parse;
  • if the workspace already builds, run the normal lightweight manifest/build checks without changing code.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create new crates;
  • rename crates;
  • move source files;
  • change dependency versions;
  • add source-file license headers;
  • create a CLA or DCO;
  • add commercial licensing metadata;
  • mark every crate AGPL for simplicity;
  • mark the integrated runtime Apache for convenience;
  • resolve an architectural dependency violation by silently relicensing a reusable package.

docs.title: Completion Report
docs.text:
Produce a concise table containing:

crate | architectural role | assigned license | reason

Also report:

  1. manifests modified;
  2. any ambiguous crates left unchanged;
  3. any Apache -> AGPL reverse dependency discovered;
  4. validation commands run and their results.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: • [x] Complete — 2026-10-11. Current Rust package manifests declare the platform/product license split described by this task.

docs.title: Apply Licensing Metadata to Web Packages
Objective
docs.text:
Apply the platform/product licensing split to every existing TypeScript/JavaScript package and application manifest without changing application behavior.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md
  2. design/level-2/001. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md
  3. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md, if present
  4. every package.json that will be modified

This task is metadata-only.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Run this task only after web/package manifests exist.

If the repository contains no relevant package.json files yet:

  • do not create placeholder packages;
  • do not create an empty web workspace solely for licensing;
  • report that the task is not yet applicable.

Ignore package-manager cache directories and generated dependency trees such as node_modules.

docs.title: Files to Inspect
docs.text:
Inspect the web workspace root and all workspace package/application manifests, including patterns such as:

web/package.json
web/packages/*/package.json
web/apps/*/package.json

Also inspect any other first-party package manifests included by the workspace configuration.

Modify only first-party package manifests that need licensing metadata added or corrected.

Do not edit TypeScript/React source files in this task.

docs.title: Classification Rule
docs.text:
Use architectural responsibility, not framework or directory name, to classify each package.

Default rule:

Reusable package -> Apache-2.0
Complete integrated Scriberig product/application -> AGPL-3.0

Do not assume that every package under apps/ is AGPL or that every package under packages/ is Apache without checking its purpose.

docs.title: Apache-2.0 Web Packages
docs.text:
Reusable web/platform packages should normally be Apache-2.0.

This includes responsibilities such as:

  • protocol types;
  • transport clients;
  • client-side semantic models;
  • framework bindings;
  • headless editor/navigation controllers;
  • selection, command, history, diff, and editing behavior intended for reuse;
  • neutral reusable components;
  • reusable MUI-based component libraries;
  • reusable agent UI abstractions that do not embed the integrated Scriberig runtime.

MUI usage does not make a package AGPL.

React usage does not make a package AGPL.

Being consumed by the complete Scriberig editor does not make a reusable package AGPL.

docs.title: AGPL-3.0 Web Applications
docs.text:
The complete reference Scriberig editor application should normally be AGPL-3.0.

An application belongs on the AGPL side when its primary role is to operate the integrated Scriberig product rather than provide reusable UI infrastructure.

Product-specific workflows embedded only in the complete editor should follow the product license.

If product-specific behavior has been placed in a package presented as a reusable library, do not solve the architectural mistake by blindly relicensing the library. Report the boundary problem so the product-specific behavior can be separated later.

docs.title: Package Metadata
docs.text:
Every distributable first-party package must declare its license in package.json using the package ecosystem's normal license metadata.

Private first-party packages should also declare a license when doing so clarifies the product/platform boundary.

Do not use a dual-license expression unless a separate design explicitly assigns both licenses to that package.

Do not add publication configuration merely to expose license information.

Do not alter private, exports, files, type, scripts, or dependency fields unless another task requires it.

docs.title: Expected Reference Workspace Classification
docs.text:
If the workspace contains the reusable package structure described by the current web design, classify these responsibilities as Apache-2.0:

protocol
client
model
editor-core
react bindings
neutral components
components-mui

Classify the complete reference Scriberig editor application as AGPL-3.0.

Use actual package purpose as the final authority. Do not create missing packages merely because they are named in a design document.

docs.title: Dependency-Direction Check
docs.text:
While reviewing package metadata, inspect first-party package dependencies.

The expected direction is:

Apache reusable web libraries
             ^
             |
AGPL integrated editor application

The reference editor may depend on reusable Apache packages.

Reusable Apache packages must not depend on the complete AGPL editor application or product-only code.

If a reverse dependency exists:

  • do not hide it with a license change;
  • do not move source in this task;
  • report the architectural violation.

docs.title: Preserve Existing Package Behavior
docs.text:
Do not change:

  • package names;
  • versions;
  • dependencies;
  • peer dependencies;
  • workspace ranges;
  • build scripts;
  • test scripts;
  • TypeScript configuration;
  • bundler configuration;
  • package exports;
  • publication settings.

The only expected modification is license metadata, except for formatting needed to preserve valid JSON.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After editing:

  • enumerate all first-party web workspace packages/applications;
  • verify each applicable manifest has the intended license declaration;
  • verify reusable packages are Apache-2.0;
  • verify the complete reference editor is AGPL-3.0;
  • verify MUI reusable libraries remain Apache unless they contain integrated product behavior;
  • verify no reusable package depends on the integrated editor application;
  • run the package manager command needed to verify workspace/package manifests are valid;
  • if the existing web workspace has typecheck/build checks, run the lightweight normal checks to ensure metadata edits did not break package parsing.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create the web workspace;
  • create missing packages;
  • move source files;
  • add dependencies;
  • change package visibility;
  • add source-file SPDX headers;
  • mark all web code AGPL;
  • mark the complete editor Apache for convenience;
  • assume MUI is a product-only layer;
  • introduce a new component library;
  • publish packages;
  • add protocol or UI functionality.

docs.title: Completion Report
docs.text:
Produce a concise table:

package | architectural role | assigned license | reason

Also report:

  1. manifests modified;
  2. packages intentionally left unchanged and why;
  3. any reusable-package -> AGPL-application dependency discovered;
  4. validation commands run and their results.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: • [x] Complete — 2026-10-11. Current first-party web package manifests declare the platform/product license split described by this task.

docs.title: Document Contribution Licensing and Third-Party Notices
Objective
docs.text:
Create contributor-facing licensing guidance and preserve third-party attribution required by material that is actually present in distributed Scriberig components.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md
  2. design/level-2/001. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md
  3. LICENSING.md, if it already exists
  4. existing contributor documentation, if any
  5. existing dependency manifests and notice files relevant to distributed components

This task does not create a CLA, DCO, copyright assignment, or commercial licensing program.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Create or update:

CONTRIBUTING.md

Create or update this file only when there are third-party notices or attribution that should be surfaced centrally, or when the project intentionally wants an empty/initial notice registry:

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

Do not fabricate dependency entries merely to populate the notice file.

docs.title: Contributor Licensing Section
docs.text:
CONTRIBUTING.md must contain a clear section explaining how licensing follows the component being modified.

The content must preserve these rules:

  • contributions to Apache-licensed reusable platform components are contributed under terms compatible with Apache-2.0;
  • contributions to AGPL-covered integrated product components are contributed under terms compatible with AGPL-3.0;
  • contributors must preserve applicable licenses, notices, and attribution for third-party material they add;
  • contributors should check the target package's own metadata and LICENSING.md before assuming its license;
  • contribution to one side of the repository does not silently relicense code on the other side;
  • current contribution terms do not implicitly grant the project rights for future commercial relicensing beyond the rights actually provided by the component license and any explicit contributor terms in force.

Keep the language factual and tied to the repository design.

Do not present speculative legal interpretation as established policy.

docs.title: No Implicit CLA or DCO
docs.text:
Do not add statements such as:

By contributing you assign copyright...
By contributing you agree to a CLA...
All commits must carry a Signed-off-by line...
The project may relicense your contribution under any terms...

unless a separate approved design introduces that policy.

The Level 1 design explicitly leaves future commercial dual licensing as a possible later decision and warns against assuming relicensing rights that were never obtained.

If an existing CONTRIBUTING.md already contains a CLA, DCO, assignment, or relicensing statement, do not silently remove or rewrite it. Report the conflict for project-owner review.

docs.title: Third-Party Material Review
docs.text:
Inspect first-party distributable components and their dependency manifests that currently exist.

Relevant sources may include:

Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock
package.json / lockfiles
bundled assets
fonts
copied/generated source
parser grammars
embedded fixtures
vendored code

The purpose is not to produce a full legal opinion on every dependency.

The task is to identify notices or attribution that the repository must preserve or that existing third-party material already includes and requires to travel with distribution.

Do not assume that every dependency requires an entry in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Do not copy entire third-party licenses into the notice file unless their terms or existing distribution practice require it.

Preserve upstream notice files when they are required.

docs.title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md Structure
docs.text:
If the file is needed, use a simple structure such as:

# Third-Party Notices

This file records third-party notices and attribution that must accompany Scriberig distributions. Third-party components remain licensed under their own terms.

## <component or asset>

- component/version or source
- license
- required notice/attribution
- location of full third-party license or upstream notice when applicable

Only include verified entries for material actually present in or distributed with the repository/product.

If no current dependency requires a central notice but the project chooses to create the file as a registry, state that there are currently no centrally recorded notices and that dependency-specific obligations remain governed by their own licenses. Do not imply that no dependency has licensing obligations at all.

docs.title: Relationship to LICENSING.md
docs.text:
Do not duplicate the entire platform/product explanation in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Instead:

  • summarize the rule contributors need;
  • link to LICENSING.md for the complete repository licensing explanation;
  • link to the relevant files under LICENSES/ where useful.

LICENSING.md remains the main repository-level explanation of the split.

CONTRIBUTING.md explains what that split means for a contributor.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md records third-party notice obligations; it does not redefine Scriberig's own license.

docs.title: Package Boundary Check
docs.text:
While reviewing contributions and notices, verify that the repository's current packaging makes it possible to identify whether a target component is Apache or AGPL.

If a component's package metadata is missing or ambiguous:

  • do not guess in contributor documentation;
  • record the ambiguity;
  • point to the appropriate package-metadata implementation task.

Contributor policy must not become a substitute for missing package metadata.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Before completing the task:

  • verify CONTRIBUTING.md links to LICENSING.md if the latter exists;
  • verify it states the contribution-license rule for both Apache and AGPL components;
  • verify it does not create a CLA, DCO, assignment, or commercial relicensing grant;
  • verify it tells contributors to preserve third-party notices and attribution;
  • verify every entry in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, if present, corresponds to material actually present or distributed;
  • verify third-party notice entries do not claim Scriberig owns or relicenses the third-party component;
  • verify no repository dependency is being assigned an Scriberig license merely because Scriberig uses it.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a CLA;
  • require sign-off/DCO without a separate design;
  • claim copyright assignment;
  • promise commercial dual licensing;
  • add a commercial license;
  • fabricate third-party dependencies;
  • bulk-copy every dependency license into one file without need;
  • alter dependency versions;
  • alter package licenses in this task;
  • create source-file SPDX headers;
  • give legal conclusions beyond the controlling repository policy.

docs.title: Completion Report
docs.text:
Report:

  1. contributor documentation created or updated;
  2. whether THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md was created, updated, or intentionally deferred;
  3. every third-party notice/attribution source added and where it was verified;
  4. any existing contributor terms that conflict with the Level 1 design;
  5. any package whose license boundary remains ambiguous.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: • [x] Complete — 2026-10-11. CONTRIBUTING.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md implement the contributor and notice policy described by this task.

docs.title: Implement Derivation Events and Domain Registry
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the domain-independent event vocabulary and derivation registration mechanism required by the reusable derived-knowledge subsystem.

This task allows domain adapters to declare derivations without implementing their own private cache semantics, and allows higher product layers to observe derived-state activity without confusing it with canonical snapshot changes.

Do not implement HTTP/WebSocket transport, an async task scheduler, model execution, compiler execution, or any specific domain derivation in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. derived Level 3 tasks 001 through 004.

Inspect existing application/protocol/event conventions before naming event types.

If a generic event envelope already exists in a lower reusable layer, integrate cleanly rather than creating an unrelated event framework.

Do not make the derivation crate depend on transport or application crates merely to reuse an event envelope from a higher layer.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical derivation crate:

src/event.rs
src/registry.rs
src/lib.rs

If the profile module needs a very small extension to carry producer/version metadata or eager/lazy hints, modify it narrowly.

Do not edit server or protocol crates in this task.

docs.title: 1. Derived Event Semantics
docs.text:
In event.rs, define a reusable event enum or tagged structure for derived-state lifecycle events.

Support at least conceptual equivalents of:

DerivationStarted
DerivedResultAvailable
DerivationFailed
DerivedResultSelected
DerivedResultEvicted
DerivedResultInvalidatedForState
IndexUpdated

Each event should include the smallest useful exact references needed to correlate it with:

  • derivation profile/key;
  • result handle where one exists;
  • relevant subject/scope where available;
  • structured failure/explanation reason where relevant.

Do not require every event to carry full payload contents.

docs.title: 2. Canonical Events Are Not Derived Events
docs.text:
Do not define CanonicalSnapshotChanged as a derivation event.

Documentation must make the distinction explicit:

canonical event -> authoritative semantic state changed

derived event -> analysis/cache/index/selection availability changed

A derived event must never imply a canonical snapshot transition by itself.

The higher application/protocol layer may later combine both event streams.

docs.title: 3. Event Payload Stability
docs.text:
Events should use exact identifiers and structured reason/status types already defined by earlier tasks.

Do not embed arbitrary formatted prose where a machine-readable enum/type already exists.

Human-readable optional detail is acceptable in addition to structured fields.

Avoid transport-specific concepts such as:

websocket connection id
HTTP status
JSON field names
SSE event names

Those belong to protocol adapters.

docs.title: 4. Derivation Registry
docs.text:
In registry.rs, define a domain-independent registry of available derivation definitions.

A registration must describe at least:

exact derivation profile
input/subject compatibility descriptor
dependency discovery strategy descriptor
eager or lazy policy hint
freshness behavior descriptor/default
retention default
producer/implementation identity
optional cost hint

The registry defines what can be derived and how it should be treated by generic infrastructure.

It does not execute domain code in this task.

docs.title: 5. Extensible Input Compatibility
docs.text:
Do not hard-code domain types into a production enum.

A registration should be able to say conceptually:

profile X applies to entity type Y
profile Z applies to snapshot/scope kind Q

using existing universal type identifiers or opaque schema/type IDs.

Test-only fake domains are allowed.

Do not add variants such as:

RustFunction
MarkdownSection
PdfPage
SessionBranch

inside the universal registry.

docs.title: 6. Dependency Discovery Contract
docs.text:
The registry must describe how a derivation obtains its dependency set.

The first implementation may support strategies equivalent to:

DeclaredExactInputs
WholeSnapshot
ProducerSupplied

or another small extensible representation.

The goal is not to implement dependency analysis here.

The goal is to make the derivation contract explicit so later execution layers can construct a correct DerivationKey.

Do not hide dependencies behind an untyped closure if doing so makes them impossible to inspect or serialize conceptually.

If execution callbacks are added later, keep metadata separately inspectable.

docs.title: 7. Scheduling Hint
docs.text:
Reuse the existing eager/lazy profile scheduling hint.

The registry may override/default this per registration if needed.

Do not start background tasks.

The only requirement is that higher layers can discover whether a derivation is intended to be:

Lazy
Eager

without changing validity semantics.

docs.title: 8. Freshness and Retention Defaults
docs.text:
A registration may provide default freshness/retention behavior.

Examples:

local deterministic summary -> immutable freshness, reusable-expensive retention
external observation -> source freshness policy, historical/disposable retention depending on adapter
navigation index -> local freshness, disposable/eager retention

Do not encode those examples as production domain rules.

Reuse the generic policy types from task 003.

docs.title: 9. Registry Operations
docs.text:
Provide a small API conceptually supporting:

register definition
lookup exact profile
list profiles applicable to subject/type/scope
reject conflicting duplicate registration
inspect registration metadata

Registration order must not affect semantic identity.

If duplicate exact profiles are registered with conflicting metadata, return a structured error rather than silently selecting the last registration.

docs.title: 10. Event Emission Boundary
docs.text:
Do not bake a global event bus into the derivation crate.

Prefer event values that can be returned/emitted by higher execution services.

If an event-sink trait is necessary for existing project style, keep it tiny and optional.

The derivation crate must remain usable in an embedded application that simply calls functions synchronously and ignores events.

docs.title: 11. Public API
docs.text:
Expose equivalents of:

DerivationEvent
DerivationRegistration
DerivationRegistry
DependencyDiscovery
RegistrationError

Reuse existing profile, freshness, retention, status, and explanation types.

Do not duplicate them inside event/registry modules.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  1. every required derived-event kind can be constructed;
  2. derived events contain exact key/result handles where appropriate;
  3. no event type implies canonical snapshot advancement;
  4. registry accepts a custom test-domain profile;
  5. registry exact-profile lookup works;
  6. applicable-profile listing works using universal type IDs;
  7. conflicting duplicate exact profile registration fails structurally;
  8. identical duplicate registration behavior is deterministic;
  9. eager/lazy hint is inspectable;
  10. freshness and retention defaults are inspectable;
  11. dependency-discovery strategy is inspectable;
  12. registry contains no hard-coded production domain variants.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

Run clippy if already part of repository practice.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • add HTTP/WebSocket/SSE code;
  • add an async runtime merely for event dispatch;
  • execute domain derivations;
  • add a worker queue or task scheduler;
  • add model or compiler dependencies;
  • add agent tools;
  • add hard-coded domain variants;
  • treat derived events as canonical snapshot events.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] required derived event kinds exist;
  • [x] canonical and derived event semantics are documented separately;
  • [x] event payloads use structured exact identifiers;
  • [x] derivation registry exists;
  • [x] registrations are version/profile specific;
  • [x] input compatibility is domain-neutral;
  • [x] dependency-discovery metadata is explicit;
  • [x] eager/lazy hint is exposed without scheduler implementation;
  • [x] freshness and retention defaults reuse generic policies;
  • [x] duplicate registration conflicts are structured;
  • [x] no transport, agent, or domain-specific dependency was added.

docs.title: Add Derived Knowledge Conformance Tests and Documentation
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the first reusable derived-knowledge slice by adding one integration-style conformance suite and public documentation that prove the Level 1 invariants across the modules implemented by the earlier tasks.

This task should not add new architecture unless a test exposes a contradiction or missing prerequisite. Its purpose is to verify that the existing implementation behaves coherently as one subsystem.

Do not add a durable database backend, agent integration, server transport, domain adapters, or background scheduler in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. derived Level 3 tasks 001 through 005.

Inspect all current modules in the canonical derivation crate.

Do not rewrite APIs simply to make tests shorter. Tests should exercise the public contracts expected by downstream domain adapters and application layers.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical derivation crate:

tests/derived_knowledge.rs
src/lib.rs

Update module documentation in existing source files only where needed to make the public contract clear.

Update the root workspace manifest only if earlier tasks failed to register the crate correctly.

Do not create a new README unless the repository already uses per-crate README files as a convention.

docs.title: 1. Test Fixture Requirements
docs.text:
Build a small fake domain entirely inside the integration test.

Use generic/test identifiers such as:

Entity A
Entity B
Scope Q
Profile summary-v1
Profile render-v1
Style/config ST1

Do not depend on real Markdown, Rust, PDF, session, model, or compiler crates.

The fixture must use the real public derivation APIs and a small in-memory repository implementation suitable for the repository contract.

If task 002 already provided a reusable test-support repository module, use it.

Do not expose test support as public production API merely for convenience.

docs.title: 2. Conformance Scenario: Local Reuse
docs.text:
Create a local derived result:

Entity F @ Revision R1
+ summary profile P1
-> Result S1

Then simulate an unrelated entity changing:

Entity G @ Revision G1 -> G2

Assert:

  • the global test snapshot may differ;
  • the local derivation key for F@R1 does not change;
  • S1 remains reusable;
  • reuse explanation states that exact dependencies still match.

This is the primary proof of local reuse despite global change.

docs.title: 3. Conformance Scenario: Global Dependency
docs.text:
Create a derivation explicitly depending on Snapshot S1.

Change canonical state so the scope is represented by Snapshot S2.

Assert:

  • the derivation key changes;
  • the old result remains historically retrievable;
  • it does not satisfy the new snapshot-bound request;
  • explanation identifies the snapshot dependency change.

This proves that conservative whole-scope dependencies remain valid when deliberately chosen.

docs.title: 4. Conformance Scenario: Scope/Absence Dependency
docs.text:
Model:

query: all members matching condition Q
old positive members: A, B

Add a new matching member C without changing A or B.

Assert that the cached complete-result derivation is affected because the declared scope dependency changed.

This test must not rely on positive dependencies alone.

docs.title: 5. Conformance Scenario: Style-Only Change
docs.text:
Create:

semantic summary depends on Entity F@R1
render result depends on F@R1 + Style ST1

Change only style/configuration to ST2.

Assert:

  • semantic summary remains reusable;
  • old render result does not satisfy the ST2 request;
  • no semantic revision change is needed for this test;
  • explanation names the configuration/style dependency.

docs.title: 6. Conformance Scenario: Hierarchical Derived Reuse
docs.text:
Create:

F1@A -> Summary SF1
F2@B -> Summary SF2
SF1 + SF2 -> ModuleSummary M1

Change only F2@B to F2@C and create SF2C.

Assert:

  • SF1 is reused;
  • old SF2 remains historical;
  • the new module summary depends on SF1 + SF2C;
  • the old module summary remains historical and is not mutated;
  • reverse dependency traversal can identify the old module summary as affected for a new-state request.

docs.title: 7. Conformance Scenario: Fresh External Observation
docs.text:
Create an external-observation-like derived record with:

source X
observed at T1
fresh until T2

Assert:

  • before T2, freshness policy accepts it;
  • after T2, it no longer satisfies a current/fresh request;
  • the exact historical observation remains retrievable;
  • no canonical snapshot operation is performed by freshness evaluation.

Use a deterministic test clock or explicit timestamps passed into evaluation. Do not sleep in tests.

docs.title: 8. Conformance Scenario: Multiple Model-Like Results
docs.text:
Using a fake nondeterministic summary profile, store two different result artifacts for one exact derivation key.

Assert:

  • both immutable results remain present;
  • exact key lookup returns both;
  • selection policy can choose one according to a stated rule;
  • changing the preferred selection does not rewrite either artifact;
  • no canonical snapshot changes.

Do not invoke a real model.

docs.title: 9. Conformance Scenario: Failure Reuse Policy
docs.text:
Create:

  • one deterministic failure for immutable input;
  • one transient failure for the same or another request.

Assert:

  • deterministic failure may be recognized as reusable/inspectable according to explicit policy;
  • transient failure does not incorrectly block retry forever;
  • failure behavior is based on structured status, not error-message parsing.

docs.title: 10. Conformance Scenario: Retention Strength
docs.text:
Create one disposable result with weak dependencies and one pinned historical result with strong retention semantics.

Assert at the policy/model level:

  • disposable validity does not imply strong canonical retention;
  • pinned historical evidence can request strong retention;
  • validity and retention categories are independently inspectable.

Do not run canonical GC.

docs.title: 11. Conformance Scenario: Event Separation
docs.text:
Construct or capture derived lifecycle events for:

DerivationStarted
DerivedResultAvailable
DerivedResultSelected

Assert:

  • they carry derivation/result identifiers as designed;
  • none is a canonical snapshot event;
  • producing them does not invoke canonical snapshot mutation.

The test need not start an event bus.

docs.title: 12. Conformance Scenario: Domain Registration
docs.text:
Register a fake domain derivation using a test universal type ID.

Assert:

  • the registry accepts it;
  • its profile, scheduling hint, dependency-discovery strategy, freshness default, and retention default are inspectable;
  • the registry does not require a production enum variant;
  • a conflicting duplicate registration returns a structured error.

docs.title: 13. Public Documentation
docs.text: Update crate-level and module-level docs so a library user can understand the following without reading implementation source:

docs.title: Canonical vs derived
docs.text:
State clearly:

Derived results may share storage with canonical knowledge but do not participate in canonical snapshot identity unless explicitly promoted through the normal canonical change model.

docs.title: Exact reuse
docs.text:
State clearly:

Reuse is based on exact declared dependencies and derivation semantics, not EntityId alone and not filename timestamps.

docs.title: Global vs local
docs.text:
Document:

SnapshotId -> did anything canonical change in the scope?
DerivationKey/dependencies -> does this specific result still apply?

docs.title: Scope completeness
docs.text: Explain why queries claiming all, none, or completeness need scope dependencies.

docs.title: Freshness
docs.text: Explain that external observations may become stale for current-information requests while remaining exact historical observations.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Explain that retention and validity are independent.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: State that the crate has no agent dependency and is useful to ordinary library consumers.

docs.title: 14. API Hygiene Review
docs.text:
Before finishing, inspect public exports and remove accidental implementation details from the public API.

Check specifically for:

  • concrete map/hash-set types leaking unnecessarily;
  • backend row IDs;
  • SQL concepts;
  • mutable global current-profile concepts;
  • hard-coded domain enums;
  • transport types;
  • agent/model types.

Do not perform unrelated large refactors.

docs.title: 15. Workspace Validation
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If already standard in the repository:

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets

Fix warnings/errors caused by this derivation slice.

Do not fix unrelated pre-existing failures unless needed to run the tests; report them separately.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • add SQLite tables;
  • add distributed cache transport;
  • add server endpoints;
  • add React/web code;
  • add CLI commands;
  • add agent tools;
  • call a real model or compiler;
  • create real Markdown/Rust/PDF/session derivations;
  • add a scheduler;
  • change canonical identity rules;
  • silently promote derived results to canonical state.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] integration conformance test file exists;
  • [x] local reuse after unrelated global change is proven;
  • [x] explicit snapshot dependency invalidation is proven;
  • [x] scope/absence dependency invalidation is proven;
  • [x] style-only invalidation boundary is proven;
  • [x] hierarchical derived-result reuse is proven;
  • [x] external freshness semantics are proven without sleeping;
  • [x] multiple immutable results can coexist and be selected;
  • [x] failure policy is structured;
  • [x] retention and validity are independently tested;
  • [x] derived/canonical event separation is tested;
  • [x] domain registration remains generic;
  • [x] crate documentation explains all major Level 1 invariants;
  • [x] workspace format/check/tests pass;
  • [x] no higher-level product dependency was introduced.

docs.title: Implement: Bootstrap Projection Crates and Core Contracts
Objective
docs.text:
Create the three projection-related crates prescribed by Level 2 and establish the minimal domain-independent projection model in sr-projection.

This task is scaffolding plus core types only. Do not implement filesystem watching or Markdown parsing yet.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  3. design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
  4. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md

If persistence/change crates already exist, use their public ID/types instead of duplicating them.

docs.title: Files to create
docs.text:
Create or preserve-and-extend:

Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/model.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/capabilities.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/style.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/render.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/adapter.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection/tests/projection_conformance.rs

crates/sr-projection-fs/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs

crates/sr-markdown/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-markdown/src/lib.rs

If workspace crates from earlier tasks do not yet exist, do not reimplement their designs here. Add only dependencies that can compile against the repository state available to you.

docs.title: Workspace requirements
docs.text:
Add the three crates to the root Cargo workspace.

Dependency direction must be:

lower universal/store/change crates
          ↑
     sr-projection
       ↑        ↑
sr-projection-fs  sr-markdown

No dependency from sr-projection to either child crate is allowed.

No projection crate may depend on agent, CLI, server, TUI, or web crates.

docs.title: model.rs
docs.text:
Define strongly typed domain-independent concepts for:

  • ProjectionClass with ReadOnly, Editable, Ephemeral, Interactive;
  • ProjectionKind as an extensible typed identifier, not a closed enum of Markdown/Rust/etc.;
  • RendererVersion;
  • a projection reference/spec reference type using existing universal IDs where appropriate;
  • a semantic scope reference capable of identifying the entity/scope being projected;
  • ownership classification needed by the generic layer without filesystem-specific paths.

Do not encode file paths in generic projection identity.

docs.title: capabilities.rs
docs.text:
Define ProjectionCapabilities containing at least:

  • renderable;
  • parseable;
  • editable;
  • round-trip capable;
  • structure preserving;
  • style preserving.

Use a representation that can be extended compatibly.

Add constructor/helper methods that make invalid obvious combinations difficult, for example editable without parseable should be rejected or normalized explicitly.

docs.title: style.rs
docs.text:
Define only universal style references/identity needed by render contracts.

Do not put Markdown/Rust style fields here.

A render request must be able to refer to an exact immutable style revision or an exact style value supplied by an adapter.

docs.title: render.rs
docs.text:
Define request/result types sufficient to carry:

  • semantic scope;
  • base snapshot/exact semantic state reference;
  • projection kind;
  • style reference;
  • renderer version;
  • rendering context/extensions;
  • exact rendered bytes or text;
  • deterministic output hash metadata placeholder/boundary.

Do not implement filesystem writes here.

docs.title: adapter.rs
docs.text:
Define a domain-adapter trait boundary with separate methods/responsibilities for:

  • capabilities;
  • render;
  • parse external representation;
  • reconcile parsed candidate against semantic state;
  • validate result where adapter validation is required.

Use associated types or opaque adapter-owned candidate/diagnostic types if that keeps the generic layer free of domain enums.

Do not force one parser AST into the universal layer.

docs.title: reconcile.rs
docs.text:
Define a generic reconciliation outcome capable of distinguishing:

NoSemanticChange
MigrationProposal
Ambiguous
Conflict
InvalidExternalState

Reuse sr-change migration/conflict types if available. If a dependency is not implemented yet, create narrow adapter-facing placeholders only where needed to compile and clearly mark them for replacement; do not create a second full migration system.

docs.title: diagnostic.rs
docs.text:
Define structured stage information:

Render
Observe
Parse
Reconcile
Validate
Commit
Rerender

Projection diagnostics must carry stage plus structured domain detail/reference. A String message may be included for humans but cannot be the only information.

docs.title: state.rs
docs.text:
Define generic projection lifecycle/status concepts without filesystem paths:

Synchronized
ExternallyModified
Rendering
ImportPending
ImportFailed
Conflict
Missing

Filesystem-specific synchronization records are implemented later.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • editable projection capabilities require parseability;
  • read-only projection can be renderable without parseability;
  • projection kind is extensible without changing sr-projection;
  • reconciliation outcomes are distinguishable without parsing strings;
  • generic model types contain no filesystem or Markdown-specific dependency.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

Fix formatting and compilation issues before stopping.

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add a watcher library.
  • Do not parse Markdown.
  • Do not write files.
  • Do not create SQL tables.
  • Do not implement agent tools.
  • Do not define Rust/source-language ASTs.
  • Do not make projection identity depend on path or line number.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Three crates exist and are workspace members.
  • [ ] Dependency direction is correct.
  • [ ] Core projection classes/capabilities compile.
  • [ ] Render/adapter/reconcile contracts are separated.
  • [ ] No domain-specific syntax leaked into sr-projection.
  • [ ] Tests pass.

Stop when these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Add CLI commands/views for inspecting provenance, validation, policy decisions, conflicts, and capability denials through the shared application/protocol model.

The CLI is a product surface. It must not bypass application trust rules or read backend tables directly.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 30, 37–39, 41 and 53–54.
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  3. design/level-3/007. expose trust state through protocol and events.md.
  4. Existing CLI Level 2/3 designs and command conventions.

If the CLI/app operation boundary is not implemented, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Work only in the existing CLI crate and shared client/application abstractions. Typical files may include:

crates/scriberig-cli/src/commands/trust.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/src/commands/inspect.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/src/output/...

Adapt to actual structure. Do not create a second CLI framework.

docs.title: Commands / Views
docs.text:
Extend the existing inspect/history command model rather than inventing a disconnected security CLI. Provide ways to inspect:

object provenance
validation evidence
promotion/policy evaluation
approval evidence
projection conflicts
external-effect state/receipts

A compact default view should show summary information first, for example:

source: model_generated
validation: current / stale / failed / unknown
accepted via: promotion <id>

Then provide an explicit deeper view that follows handles to exact provenance and evidence objects.

docs.title: Denials
docs.text:
When a command is denied, print the structured denial with:

requested action
requested scope
reason
narrower alternatives if present
whether approval may grant it

Do not print hidden object content or secrets as part of the denial.

Use a distinct non-zero exit status for authorization denial according to the CLI's existing error conventions.

docs.title: Machine-Readable Output
docs.text:
If the CLI already supports JSON or another machine-readable mode, ensure trust/validation/denial results are available there using protocol/application types rather than scraping human output.

Do not create a new output format solely for this task.

docs.title: Event / Progress Output
docs.text:
For long-running validation/promotion/external-effect operations, use the common event stream if available. Show meaningful states such as validation started/completed, approval required, conflict detected, and promoted.

Do not infer success from process silence.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add CLI tests for:

  1. compact provenance summary;
  2. deep provenance inspection by handle;
  3. failed validation display;
  4. stale validation display;
  5. policy rejection vs capability denial remain distinct;
  6. conflict display includes resolvable IDs;
  7. denied operation returns expected exit status;
  8. JSON/machine-readable form preserves structured fields;
  9. no secret value is printed by receipt/denial fixtures.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run Rust workspace format/check/tests/lint plus any CLI snapshot tests already used by the repository.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not query SQLite tables directly. Do not add a CLI-only authorization bypass. Do not flatten provenance into unstructured log text. Do not expose credential material.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] trust information is inspectable from CLI;
  • [ ] compact and deep views exist;
  • [ ] denials are structured and distinguishable;
  • [ ] machine-readable output stays structured;
  • [ ] CLI uses shared application/protocol behavior;
  • [ ] tests cover failure and confidentiality cases.

docs.title: Expose Trust Inspection in Web Editor
Objective
docs.text:
Add reusable web-platform support and an integrated-editor view for provenance, validation, policy evaluation, conflicts, approvals, and capability denials.

The full editor must consume public web libraries. Do not implement trust inspection only as private application code.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 37–39, 52–54 and 62–63.
  2. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md.
  3. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md.
  4. design/level-3/007. expose trust state through protocol and events.md.
  5. Existing web workspace/bootstrap, client, model, React, component, and editor tasks.

If the public web packages have not been scaffolded, stop and report the prerequisite rather than adding a private one-off editor implementation.

docs.title: Expected Package Boundaries
docs.text:
Use the established packages, typically:

web/packages/client
web/packages/model
web/packages/react
web/packages/editor-core
web/packages/components
web/packages/components-mui
web/apps/editor

Do not require consumers to use MUI to inspect trust state.

docs.title: Client and Model
docs.text:
Add client/model operations that can:

load compact trust summary for an entity/revision
load provenance relations/details
load validation evidence
load policy/approval evidence
load conflict details
subscribe to trust-relevant events

Keep selection based on universal semantic IDs/snapshots. Trust panels should work for code, Markdown, PDF-derived objects, sessions, and future domains without separate navigation systems.

docs.title: Headless Editor Core
docs.text:
Provide headless controller/state suitable for third-party UIs. It should expose states such as:

loading
ready
restricted/denied
validation failed
validation stale
conflict unresolved
approval required

Expose handles/actions, not hard-coded presentation.

docs.title: React Bindings
docs.text:
Add hooks following existing package conventions, equivalent to:

useTrustSummary(selection)
useProvenance(selection)
useValidation(selection)
useTrustEvents(...)

Do not invent duplicate fetching/cache behavior outside the established web model/client layer.

docs.title: Reusable Components
docs.text:
Add neutral components for at least:

TrustSummary
ProvenanceInspector
ValidationList
PolicyEvaluationView
CapabilityDeniedNotice
ConflictSummary

Then provide MUI wrappers/compositions only if the MUI package already exists.

Components must distinguish authored/observed/generated knowledge and current/stale/failed validation without converting them into one trust score.

docs.title: Integrated Editor
docs.text:
Add a trust/provenance inspector that works from the editor's universal selection. It should support:

  • compact high-level status;
  • following exact provenance edges;
  • opening validation diagnostics;
  • inspecting policy/approval evidence;
  • opening conflicts;
  • navigating back to source evidence when source coordinates are available.

The raw graph/relation browser must still be able to inspect the same underlying objects.

docs.title: Denials and Confidentiality
docs.text: A denial is a normal UI state. Do not attempt alternative requests that widen scope automatically. Do not show hidden snippets, cached summaries, or relationship labels that reveal restricted data.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  1. authored vs model-generated badge/state;
  2. current vs stale validation;
  3. failed validation diagnostics;
  4. capability denial rendering without payload leak;
  5. conflict view with exact handles;
  6. universal selection drives trust inspector;
  7. neutral component works without MUI;
  8. MUI layer wraps public behavior rather than re-fetching privately;
  9. event update refreshes affected trust state;
  10. restricted derived summary is not rendered when subject access is denied.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run the repository's web lint, typecheck, unit/component tests, build, and any protocol conformance generation.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not add private API endpoints for the editor. Do not couple trust components to one domain. Do not compute authorization in React. Do not expose secret values.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] public web packages expose trust inspection;
  • [ ] headless behavior exists independently of MUI;
  • [ ] integrated editor uses public components/hooks;
  • [ ] universal selection links semantic object to provenance;
  • [ ] denial/conflict/stale states are explicit;
  • [ ] tests cover restricted and generated data.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the generic capability-discovery mechanism required by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md so clients can inspect an entity and learn what installed domain functionality is available without hard-coding every domain.

Capability discovery must be useful to CLI, API, browser, third-party libraries, and future agent tools. It must not depend on an agent runtime.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. current public APIs of scriberig-schema, scriberig-graph, scriberig-projection, and scriberig-app

Do not create a parallel plugin system if the repository already has a schema/domain registry. Extend the established registry instead.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Prefer implementing static domain/type capability metadata in scriberig-schema and runtime-installed capability aggregation in the lowest shared layer that already owns installed services.

Expected files are equivalent to:

crates/scriberig-schema/src/domain.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/src/capability.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/src/registry.rs
crates/scriberig-schema/src/lib.rs

If runtime capability providers already belong in another existing shared crate, place only the runtime aggregation there and keep schema/type declarations in scriberig-schema.

Add tests in the owning crate(s).

docs.title: Domain Descriptor
docs.text:
Provide a stable descriptor for an installed domain/schema.

It must expose at least:

domain identifier
human-readable name
schema version
entity types provided
relation types provided

Where the architecture already has equivalent identifiers, reuse them.

Do not make crate names or Rust TypeId values the public domain identity.

docs.title: Entity Capability Description
docs.text:
For an entity type in a given installed domain configuration, capability discovery should be able to advertise categories equivalent to:

available relations
available child/collection views
available descriptions/summaries
available projections
available semantic commands
available analyses
available validation capabilities

Not every capability needs an implementation in this task. The discovery model must support advertising only capabilities that are actually installed/available.

Do not claim a capability merely because a schema concept exists if no provider can execute it.

docs.title: Capability IDs
docs.text:
Use stable semantic IDs/names for capabilities.

Examples of the shape, not mandatory exact names:

projection.markdown
analysis.rust.references
command.markdown.rename_heading
validation.rust.compile
view.session.branch_tree

Capability IDs must be transport-safe and independent of Rust symbol names.

Avoid embedding implementation-specific version numbers into the semantic capability ID. Producer/version metadata belongs beside the capability/provider.

docs.title: Provider Metadata
docs.text:
When a capability is backed by a specific adapter/analyzer, discovery should be able to expose provider metadata where relevant:

provider/adapter identifier
provider version/profile
availability state
required configuration if known

Do not expose secret configuration values.

docs.title: Generic Inspection Integration
docs.text:
Integrate capability metadata with the existing generic inspect/schema APIs if such APIs exist.

A generic client inspecting a Function, PDFPage, Section, or Branch should be able to discover available operations without importing that domain crate directly.

The same mechanism must work for a deployment with only Markdown installed and a full deployment with many domains.

docs.title: Minimal Deployment Behavior
docs.text:
Test at least two registry configurations:

configuration A:
  universal store/schema + Markdown domain only

configuration B:
  Markdown + code/Rust + PDF + session capabilities

Configuration A must not advertise Rust/PDF capabilities.

The absence of an optional domain must not make generic inspection fail.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • domain descriptors are discoverable by stable ID;
  • entity types report only installed capabilities;
  • a Markdown-only registry does not expose Rust capabilities;
  • capability IDs are deterministic and transport-safe;
  • provider metadata is attached without leaking private implementation state;
  • generic clients can enumerate capability categories without linking agent crates;
  • duplicate capability/provider registration is rejected or deterministically resolved according to the established registry policy.

Run workspace formatting/tests/clippy for affected crates.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement agent tools.
  • Do not hard-code every domain into scriberig-core or scriberig-store.
  • Do not make optional domain crates mandatory dependencies of the universal store.
  • Do not advertise unavailable operations.
  • Do not expose Rust implementation type names as wire/public capability IDs.
  • Do not put credentials or secret configuration in capability metadata.
  • Do not create a second unrelated registry if one already exists.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Installed domains are discoverable generically.
  • [ ] Entity-level capabilities are enumerable.
  • [ ] Optional domains remain optional.
  • [ ] Capability IDs are stable and transport-safe.
  • [ ] Provider/version metadata can be represented.
  • [ ] Generic inspection works without agent dependencies.
  • [ ] Tests cover minimal and full-style registries.
  • [ ] Formatting, tests, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Add Trust Model End-to-End Conformance Tests
Objective
docs.text:
Create cross-surface integration tests that prove Scriberig's trust model is enforced consistently from semantic input through application operations, protocol/server, CLI/web-facing clients, validation, promotion, conflicts, and external-effect state.

This task should be implemented after the preceding trust tasks. It is a conformance suite, not another business-logic layer.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 30, 41, 54, 65 and 66.
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md.
  4. Level 3 trust tasks 001 through 010 in this series.
  5. Existing repository-wide protocol/conformance/end-to-end test conventions.

If the application layer, protocol/server, or trust primitives are incomplete, implement only tests for completed prerequisites and clearly mark remaining scenarios as blocked; do not fake passing behavior.

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
Use the repository's established integration/conformance test locations. The workspace design anticipates repository-level test areas; reuse those rather than burying all scenarios in one crate.

Possible locations, only if they exist in the implemented workspace:

tests/conformance/
tests/protocol/
tests/end-to-end/
web/... existing integration test area

Do not create a second test harness if one already exists.

docs.title: Canonical Scenario Fixture
docs.text:
Build one small semantic project fixture containing:

one public entity
one restricted entity
one generated summary derived from restricted content
one editable projection
one candidate branch
one validation policy
one fake external connector

Use deterministic IDs/test data where the implementation allows it.

The fixture must not contain real credentials or live external services.

docs.title: 1. Untrusted content cannot grant authority
docs.text: Store/import text containing an instruction equivalent to requesting broader authority. Run the normal application/agent-facing read path and prove the effective capability set is unchanged.

docs.title: 2. Restricted traversal does not leak
docs.text: Allow read access to a public entity linked to a restricted entity. Verify inspect, relation traversal, reverse lookup, search, summary access, and protocol responses do not expose restricted content.

docs.title: 3. Generated knowledge retains provenance
docs.text: Create or load a generated summary and prove a consumer can distinguish it from authored/observed evidence and follow provenance back to exact immutable inputs.

docs.title: 4. Validation is exact
docs.text:
Validate candidate S2, change a relevant dependency to produce S3, and prove the S2 validation is not accepted for S3.

Also change an unrelated entity while keeping declared dependencies identical and prove reusable evidence remains applicable where the dependency model permits it.

docs.title: 5. Promotion cannot be bypassed
docs.text:
Attempt canonical advancement through:

application operation
server/protocol path
CLI-facing path if testable in-process
web/client path if available

Prove each path requires the same promotion policy and exact evidence. There must be no product-surface storage bypass.

docs.title: 6. Stale proposal is explicit
docs.text: Create a proposal from base S1, advance canonical state independently, then attempt promotion. Verify stale/rebase/merge-needed result rather than silent overwrite.

docs.title: 7. Ambiguous projection edit becomes conflict
docs.text: Feed an intentionally ambiguous external edit. Prove the original observation is retained, conflict is first-class, canonical state is unchanged, and later resolution produces a normal migration.

docs.title: 8. Failed validation remains evidence
docs.text: Run a validator that fails. Prove the failure and diagnostics remain inspectable without making the candidate canonical.

docs.title: 9. Capability delegation cannot widen authority
docs.text: Create a narrow child/subagent capability from a parent and attempt to add a broader scope/action. Verify rejection.

docs.title: 10. External effect uncertainty is preserved
docs.text: Use a fake connector that accepts a request but simulates loss of the response. Verify the operation becomes Unknown, is not blindly retried, and can later be reconciled through an external observation.

docs.title: 11. Derived cache cannot bypass confidentiality
docs.text: Populate a cached summary while using a broad principal, then request it as a restricted principal. Verify cache hit is denied without deleting the reusable cache object.

docs.title: 12. Structured denial parity
docs.text: Trigger the same denied semantic operation through at least the direct application path and protocol/client path. Verify action, scope, reason, and approval-possible semantics agree.

docs.title: Audit Reconstruction Test
docs.text:
For one successful candidate, assert that a consumer can reconstruct this chain using semantic references rather than log scraping:

base snapshot
request/proposal
branch/workspace
migration
candidate snapshot
validation evidence
policy evaluation
approval if required
promotion
new canonical snapshot

Do not require private model reasoning traces.

docs.title: Failure-Mode Assertions
docs.text:
Add explicit regression names matching the Level 1 failure modes where practical:

model output is not automatically authoritative
web/imported text cannot grant capability
validation of A cannot promote B
external file edit cannot overwrite concurrent state silently
restricted cache/search cannot leak content
ambiguous reconciliation cannot create false lineage silently
local write cannot invoke unrelated external service
unknown external outcome is not retried as definite failure
stale validation is not presented as current
product surfaces cannot bypass application policy

docs.title: Test Quality Rules
docs.text:
• prefer semantic assertions over exact human-formatted strings;
  • verify IDs/references point to the exact expected revisions/snapshots;
  • never depend on network access;
  • use fake validators/connectors with deterministic behavior;
  • keep each scenario independently diagnosable;
  • do not mark blocked scenarios ignored without an issue/comment explaining the missing prerequisite according to repository conventions.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run the full Rust workspace tests, protocol conformance tests, and web tests/build required by the repository. The task is complete only when trust conformance tests are part of normal CI or the existing aggregate test command.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not introduce production bypass hooks solely for testing. Do not test authorization only at UI level. Do not rely on textual logs as proof of provenance. Do not use real secrets or real external side effects.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] one deterministic end-to-end trust fixture exists;
  • [ ] all ten Level 1 failure classes are covered by regression tests;
  • [ ] application and protocol paths agree;
  • [ ] provenance/audit chain is reconstructable;
  • [ ] ambiguous and failed states stay explicit;
  • [ ] cache/search confidentiality is tested;
  • [ ] external-effect uncertainty is tested;
  • [ ] conformance suite runs in normal project validation/CI.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first shared application-layer primitives in scriberig-app.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. the Level 1 identity/snapshot and change/migration documents that define the canonical ID and migration concepts already implemented by lower crates.

This task creates the reusable operation boundary. It does not implement HTTP, CLI parsing, agent model execution, or domain-specific editing.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The runtime crate scaffold must exist.

The foundational crates must already expose the real identifier and snapshot types required by this task.

Reuse those types. Do not create duplicate EntityId, RevisionId, SnapshotId, MigrationId, or branch identifiers inside scriberig-app.

If an upstream type is not yet implemented, implement only the portions that can compile without inventing a competing identity model.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Inside crates/scriberig-app/src/ create:

lib.rs
error.rs
context.rs
query.rs
command.rs
operation.rs
event.rs
capability.rs

Keep modules small and documented.

docs.title: context.rs
docs.text:
Define an application request context carrying the semantic base under which an operation runs.

It must be able to express:

  • exact snapshot when one is required;
  • caller/actor provenance in a generic form if the lower-level provenance model already exists;
  • capability/authorization context without embedding UI concepts;
  • a correlation/request identifier where useful.

Do not put HTTP headers, CLI arguments, or model prompts in this type.

Prefer explicit immutable values.

docs.title: error.rs
docs.text:
Define one structured application error enum with variants corresponding to these semantic classes:

NotFound
SchemaViolation
StaleBaseSnapshot
SemanticConflict
ValidationFailure
PermissionDenied
UnsupportedOperation
ProjectionOutOfSync
OperationCancelled
Internal

Use structured fields where existing lower-layer types make that useful.

Each error must implement normal Rust error/display behavior without requiring callers to parse its display string to discover the category.

Do not include HTTP status codes here.

docs.title: operation.rs
docs.text:
Define the application-level long-running operation model.

Required concepts:

OperationId
OperationKind
OperationStatus
OperationProgress
OperationResult reference/summary

Reuse a shared OperationId from scriberig-core if it already exists. If Level 2/3 identity work has not provided it, add it only in the canonical low-level crate, not locally in scriberig-app.

OperationStatus must represent at least:

Queued
Running
Completed
Failed
Cancelled

Ensure terminal states are distinguishable with a helper such as is_terminal().

Do not implement scheduling or threads in this task.

docs.title: event.rs
docs.text:
Define a transport-independent application event enum or equivalent typed model.

Include categories equivalent to:

SnapshotChanged
EntityChanged
ProjectionChanged
BranchChanged
MigrationCreated
OperationStarted
OperationProgressed
OperationCompleted
ValidationCompleted
AgentOutputProduced

Payloads should contain stable handles and concise metadata.

Do not copy full mutable entity state into events.

Do not use server/WebSocket types here.

docs.title: capability.rs
docs.text:
Define a small runtime capability vocabulary suitable for discovery.

The first implementation only needs to express:

  • a stable capability identifier/name;
  • short description;
  • whether it is available in the current application configuration;
  • optional domain/scope metadata if already supported cleanly.

Do not turn this into authorization policy or the repository capability matrix.

Those are separate concerns.

docs.title: query.rs
docs.text:
Define application-level read request/result forms for the first vertical capability: entity inspection.

Required semantic input:

entity
snapshot resolution mode
requested detail level if the existing graph API supports it

The result must identify:

  • the requested entity;
  • exact resolved revision;
  • exact snapshot used;
  • semantic type/summary information exposed by the graph layer.

Do not render terminal text here.

Do not serialize protocol DTOs here.

Use graph/query APIs already defined below the application layer.

If the lower graph API is not yet capable of inspection, keep request/result types and orchestration interfaces minimal rather than bypassing it.

docs.title: command.rs
docs.text:
Define command request boundaries, but do not implement broad mutations yet.

At minimum provide typed placeholders/interfaces for commands whose semantics already exist below the app layer, such as applying a migration against an explicit base snapshot.

Do not create an alternative mutation representation.

A command must delegate canonical change to scriberig-migration/snapshot infrastructure.

If those APIs are not ready, keep the module documented with only types that are justified by implemented lower layers.

docs.title: lib.rs
docs.text:
Re-export only stable application-facing types that callers actually need.

Do not glob-export internal implementation helpers.

Crate documentation should state clearly:

scriberig-app is the shared semantic operation boundary for CLI, server, TUI, clients, and agent adapters.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add unit tests for:

  • every application error category being inspectable without string parsing;
  • OperationStatus::is_terminal() or equivalent;
  • event payloads retaining stable IDs and not owning canonical state;
  • inspect request/result preserving snapshot identity;
  • application types not depending on transport-specific data.

Use compile-time dependencies and normal Rust tests; do not require a network.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add server routes.
  • Do not define protocol serialization here.
  • Do not add a CLI command.
  • Do not add a model provider.
  • Do not access SQLite directly.
  • Do not duplicate core identifiers.
  • Do not mutate canonical state outside shared migration APIs.
  • Do not implement a general job scheduler.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-app
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All prescribed source modules exist.
  • [ ] Semantic errors are structured and transport-neutral.
  • [ ] Operation lifecycle types exist with explicit terminal states.
  • [ ] Application events carry handles rather than copied canonical state.
  • [ ] Runtime capability discovery has a minimal typed model.
  • [ ] Entity inspection is represented through snapshot-aware request/result forms.
  • [ ] No transport, UI, agent-provider, or database-specific types leaked into the crate.
  • [ ] No canonical ID type was duplicated.
  • [ ] Tests and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Implement Protocol Contract and Schema Export
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first authoritative remote protocol contract in scriberig-protocol and provide a reproducible machine-readable schema export path.

Read first:

  1. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  2. design/level-2/011. application operations protocol and runtime boundaries.md
  3. design/level-3/012. implement application operation primitives.md
