App.tsx should render a minimal static shell such as the application name and a message that semantic views are not yet implemented.

The app may use MUI only through the normal MUI dependency or @scriberig/components-mui; do not implement actual Scriberig components in the app during this task.

docs.title: Vite Application
docs.text:
Configure web/apps/scriberig as a Vite React application.

The app must import reusable packages by package name, never by packages/.../src path.

Do not implement routes, panels, API connections, or agent commands yet.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
From web/, run the workspace-equivalent checks for:

pnpm install
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

If the root scripts use recursive pnpm commands, they must succeed even when packages currently have no tests.

The Vite app must produce a successful production build.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not edit Level 1 or Level 2 design documents.
  • Do not add server endpoint assumptions.
  • Do not define protocol wire types yet.
  • Do not implement a transport client.
  • Do not implement browser caches or stores.
  • Do not create selection or command APIs.
  • Do not create reusable visual components yet.
  • Do not implement the integrated editor views.
  • Do not add Redux, Zustand, MobX, or another state framework.
  • Do not add Storybook.
  • Do not add Electron or Tauri.
  • Do not add a browser E2E framework.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] web/ is a pnpm workspace.
  • [ ] All seven public packages exist with exact prescribed names.
  • [ ] The private @scriberig/app Vite application exists.
  • [ ] TypeScript strict checking is enabled through a shared base config.
  • [ ] React exists only in packages that need it.
  • [ ] MUI is not a dependency of protocol, client, model, editor-core, react, or neutral components.
  • [ ] No package imports another package through a private source path.
  • [ ] No speculative semantic APIs were introduced.
  • [ ] pnpm typecheck succeeds.
  • [ ] pnpm test succeeds.
  • [ ] pnpm build succeeds.
  • [ ] The lockfile is committed.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Create the initial Rust workspace and the sr-core identity types required by the identity/revision/snapshot design.

This task is intentionally narrow. Do not implement revisions, snapshot tries, stores, migrations, SQLite, agents, or domain models.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read these documents completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md

The Level 1 invariants are authoritative. The Level 2 document defines the concrete file layout for this implementation.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify only these files unless compilation requires a trivial adjacent change:

Cargo.toml
crates/sr-core/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-core/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-core/src/ids.rs

Do not create sr-store in this task.

docs.title: Required Result
docs.text:
Create a Cargo workspace containing crates/sr-core.

Implement these public opaque types:

EntityId
RevisionId
SnapshotId
TypeId
EncodingVersion

docs.title: EntityId
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Stored as exactly 16 bytes.
  • [ ] EntityId::new() creates a fresh non-content-derived identity.
  • [ ] Provide from_bytes([u8; 16]) and as_bytes().
  • [ ] Implement Clone, Copy, Eq, Ord, and Hash.
  • [ ] Implement deterministic Display and FromStr.
  • [ ] Display form starts with ent_.
  • [ ] Parsing rejects another identity prefix.
  • [ ] Do not expose the UUID crate's type in the public API.

Use UUID v4 generation internally unless the currently selected dependency makes another random 128-bit implementation materially simpler.

docs.title: RevisionId
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Stored as exactly 32 bytes.
  • [ ] Opaque newtype distinct from SnapshotId.
  • [ ] Provide byte construction/access needed by later hashing code.
  • [ ] Display form starts with rev_.
  • [ ] FromStr round-trips exact bytes.
  • [ ] Parsing rejects snp_ and ent_ values.

Do not compute revision hashes yet.

docs.title: SnapshotId
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Stored as exactly 32 bytes.
  • [ ] Opaque newtype distinct from RevisionId.
  • [ ] Provide byte construction/access needed by later hashing code.
  • [ ] Display form starts with snp_.
  • [ ] FromStr round-trips exact bytes.
  • [ ] Parsing rejects rev_ and ent_ values.

Do not implement snapshot hashing yet.

docs.title: TypeId
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Owns a UTF-8 string.
  • [ ] Constructor rejects an empty identifier.
  • [ ] Display returns the exact identifier.
  • [ ] Examples such as markdown.paragraph and rust.function must be valid.
  • [ ] Do not hard-code a registry of known type names.

docs.title: EncodingVersion
docs.text:
Requirements:

  • [ ] Small integer newtype.
  • [ ] Define public constant/version constructor for version 1.
  • [ ] Do not silently accept arithmetic overflow or use it as a mutable global.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Use one small typed parse/validation error for invalid textual identities and invalid TypeId construction. Do not use stringly typed errors in the public API if a compact enum is sufficient.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Keep dependencies minimal.

Allowed reasons for dependencies in this task:

  • random UUID generation;
  • optional serde support if it does not complicate the crate.

Do not add:

  • async runtime;
  • SQLite;
  • web framework;
  • parser framework;
  • agent SDK.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Unit tests may live inside ids.rs for this task.

Implement at least these tests:

  • [ ] two EntityId::new() calls produce different values;
  • [ ] EntityId display/parse round-trip;
  • [ ] RevisionId display/parse round-trip;
  • [ ] SnapshotId display/parse round-trip;
  • [ ] wrong prefixes are rejected;
  • [ ] RevisionId and SnapshotId cannot be accidentally parsed as each other;
  • [ ] empty TypeId is rejected;
  • [ ] valid TypeId round-trips through display.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
Before finishing, run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

Fix all failures and warnings introduced by this task.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not make EntityId content-addressed.
  • Do not alias RevisionId and SnapshotId to the same Rust type.
  • Do not include parent or position information in any identity type.
  • Do not create a global current snapshot.
  • Do not add application, CLI, server, or agent code.
  • Do not implement more of the Level 2 design than this task owns.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Workspace exists and builds.
  • [ ] sr-core is a reusable library crate.
  • [ ] All five required identity/configuration types exist.
  • [ ] Text identity prefixes are distinct and checked.
  • [ ] Tests pass.
  • [ ] Formatting and clippy checks pass.

docs.title: Create Repository License Texts and Licensing Guide
Objective
docs.text:
Create the repository-level licensing artifacts required by:

  1. design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md
  2. design/level-2/001. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md

This task is limited to the two complete license texts and the human-readable repository licensing guide.

Do not edit package manifests, contributor policy, source headers, or dependency notices in this task.

The controlling rule is:

Reusable infrastructure is Apache-2.0. The integrated Scriberig product and runtime are AGPL-3.0. The repository must make the boundary understandable without weakening either side.

docs.title: Files to Create
docs.text:
Create exactly these repository-level files if they do not already exist:

LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt
LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt
LICENSING.md

If one already exists, inspect it before changing it. Do not overwrite user-authored legal material blindly.

docs.title: Step 1 — Read the Controlling Designs
docs.text:
Before editing, read the full contents of:

design/level-1/014. extensibility ecosystem and licensing.md
design/level-2/001. licensing artifacts package metadata and notices.md

Do not infer a different licensing model from package names, README text, or personal preference.

The Level 1 document is authoritative for the architectural split. The Level 2 document is authoritative for the concrete repository artifacts created by this task.

docs.title: Step 2 — Obtain the Complete Apache-2.0 Text
docs.text:
Populate:

LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt

with the complete, unmodified Apache License 2.0 text from an authoritative source.

Requirements:

  • copy the legal text verbatim;
  • do not summarize it;
  • do not insert Scriberig-specific commentary into the license text;
  • do not remove the appendix;
  • preserve the license title and version;
  • do not add a copyright holder unless the official text itself contains placeholder/example text;
  • do not convert the text into a different license template.

If the agent cannot obtain or verify the authoritative full text, stop this task and report the missing prerequisite rather than generating legal text from memory.

docs.title: Step 3 — Obtain the Complete GNU AGPL Version 3 Text
docs.text:
Populate:

LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt

with the complete, unmodified GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text selected by the Level 1 design.

Requirements:

  • copy the legal text verbatim from an authoritative source;
  • do not summarize or rewrite clauses;
  • include all sections of the license;
  • do not insert project commentary into the license body;
  • do not silently switch to ordinary GPL;
  • do not silently choose a later-version clause or a different license variant on behalf of the project.

If the exact intended legal text cannot be verified, stop and report the ambiguity instead of inventing wording.

docs.title: Step 4 — Create LICENSING.md
docs.text:
LICENSING.md is explanatory documentation, not a replacement for the complete license texts.

Use a clear structure similar to:

# Licensing Scriberig

## Overview
## Apache-2.0 reusable platform
## AGPL-3.0 integrated product
## How to determine a package's license
## Agent and CLI boundary
## Third-party applications and extensions
## Third-party dependencies
## Source headers and SPDX metadata
## Contributions and future dual licensing
## License texts

The headings may vary slightly, but all required information below must be present.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Explain that the repository intentionally uses two licenses following the architectural platform/product boundary.

State the rule directly:

Reusable platform and building blocks: Apache-2.0
Integrated Scriberig product and runtime: AGPL-3.0

Do not describe the repository as wholly Apache or wholly AGPL.

docs.title: Apache reusable platform
docs.text:
Explain that reusable infrastructure is Apache-2.0 by default and give representative categories from the design:

  • identity/core types;
  • storage;
  • graph and schemas;
  • queries and migrations;
  • projections;
  • domain adapters;
  • protocol definitions;
  • Rust and TypeScript clients;
  • client-side models and framework bindings;
  • headless editor behavior;
  • neutral components;
  • reusable MUI components;
  • reusable agent interfaces that do not implement the integrated runtime.

Make clear that organizations may build proprietary applications using these Apache-licensed components subject to their applicable license terms.

docs.title: AGPL integrated product
docs.text:
Explain that the integrated product is AGPL-3.0 by default and give the representative categories from the design:

  • reference Scriberig server application;
  • integrated agent execution/orchestration runtime;
  • complete Scriberig editor application;
  • product-specific integrated workflows.

Do not claim that every server library, every binary, or every agent-related abstraction is automatically AGPL.

docs.title: Package-level decision
docs.text:
State that each distributable crate/package declares its own license in its package metadata and that this package declaration is the immediate indicator for that component.

Explain that architectural responsibility determines the classification.

A reusable CLI client may be Apache. A binary embedding the integrated AGPL runtime may be AGPL.

docs.title: Third-party applications
docs.text:
State that merely using Apache-licensed Scriberig platform libraries or interoperating with the public protocol does not turn an independent third-party application into the integrated Scriberig AGPL product.

Do not attempt to give legal advice about every possible combined work. Keep this section tied to the architectural intent expressed by the design.

docs.title: Third-party dependencies
docs.text:
State that third-party dependencies and assets retain their own licenses and that required attribution/notices must be preserved.

Do not list dependencies that are not actually present.

docs.title: SPDX/source headers
docs.text:
Explain that package metadata is required while repository-wide SPDX source headers are not currently mandated by this design.

Do not add a policy that every source file must contain a header.

docs.title: Contributions and future dual licensing
docs.text:
State that contributions follow the license of the component they modify.

State that commercial dual licensing of AGPL-covered components is only a possible future decision and is not promised or implicitly authorized by the current contribution terms.

Do not invent a CLA, DCO, assignment, or relicensing grant.

docs.title: License links
docs.text:
Link to:

LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt
LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt

using relative repository links.

docs.title: Content Quality Requirements
docs.text:
LICENSING.md must be understandable to a developer deciding whether to depend on a Scriberig package.

Prefer direct language over legal speculation.

Do not duplicate the full license texts inside LICENSING.md.

Do not claim that this guide overrides the actual licenses.

Do not add a copyright owner because the controlling designs do not specify one.

Do not add commercial contact information because the designs do not specify a commercial licensing program.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Before completing the task:

  • verify both files under LICENSES/ contain complete authoritative texts;
  • verify LICENSING.md names both licenses;
  • verify it distinguishes reusable platform from integrated product;
  • verify it says package metadata identifies each distributable component's license;
  • verify it does not imply reusable MUI libraries are AGPL merely because the reference app uses them;
  • verify it does not make all agent abstractions AGPL;
  • verify it does not promise commercial dual licensing;
  • verify all relative links resolve inside the repository.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
Do not:

  • edit Cargo.toml files;
  • edit package.json files;
  • create placeholder crates or web packages;
  • add source SPDX headers;
  • create a CLA or DCO;
  • add a copyright assignment;
  • create a plugin registry;
  • add a commercial license;
  • create protocol specifications;
  • paraphrase legal license text;
  • substitute GPL for AGPL;
  • label the entire monorepo with one license.

docs.title: Completion Report
docs.text:
Report:

  1. files created or updated;
  2. authoritative sources used to obtain each complete license text;
  3. any pre-existing legal text that required preservation or manual review;
  4. confirmation that LICENSING.md follows the platform/product boundary without introducing new licensing policy.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: • [x] Complete — 2026-10-11. Both complete license texts and the repository licensing guide are present and verified against the SPDX License List Data sources.

docs.title: Agent Task: Create the sr-change Crate Scaffold
Goal
docs.text:
Create the backend-independent Rust crate prescribed by design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md and wire it into the workspace without implementing domain behavior yet.

This task is complete only when the workspace compiles with the new crate and every prescribed module exists.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read these files in order:

  1. design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
  2. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  3. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md
  4. design/level-2/001. persistence crate boundaries.md
  5. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md

Do not reinterpret the identity model. EntityId, RevisionId, and SnapshotId come from sr-core.

docs.title: Prerequisite check
docs.text:
Before changing files, verify that the workspace and these crates exist:

Cargo.toml
crates/sr-core/
crates/sr-store/

If they do not exist, do not create replacement versions from this task. Stop and report that the persistence foundation must be implemented first from its own Level 3 tasks.

docs.title: Files to create
docs.text:
Create exactly these initial files if they do not exist:

crates/sr-change/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/src/migration.rs
crates/sr-change/src/operation.rs
crates/sr-change/src/provenance.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/branch.rs
crates/sr-change/src/workspace.rs
crates/sr-change/src/promotion.rs
crates/sr-change/src/diff.rs
crates/sr-change/src/conflict.rs
crates/sr-change/src/merge.rs
crates/sr-change/src/rebase.rs
crates/sr-change/src/query.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Also update the root Cargo.toml workspace members to include crates/sr-change.

docs.title: Cargo.toml
docs.text:
Use the repository's existing workspace package metadata and dependency style.

The crate must depend only on libraries needed for the backend-independent change model.

Required internal dependencies:

sr-core
sr-store

Do not add dependencies on:

  • sr-store-memory;
  • sr-store-sqlite;
  • agent crates;
  • CLI/server crates;
  • domain adapters.

Dev-dependencies may use sr-store-memory for conformance tests when that crate is available.

docs.title: lib.rs
docs.text:
Declare all prescribed modules.

Expose the main public types from their owning modules only when doing so follows the repository's existing public-API style. Avoid creating a large prelude in this task.

The crate-level documentation should state three rules:

  1. snapshots and revisions are immutable;
  2. change is represented as transitions between snapshots;
  3. the crate is backend- and domain-independent.

docs.title: Module responsibility comments
docs.text:
Each module should contain a short module-level documentation comment stating its responsibility:

  • migration: exact snapshot transitions and entity deltas;
  • operation: generic and domain-extensible semantic operations;
  • provenance: source and provenance metadata;
  • history: explicit change-history topology;
  • branch: branch metadata and branch references;
  • workspace: isolated speculative work;
  • promotion: optimistic named-root advancement;
  • diff: comparison of exact snapshots;
  • conflict: structured semantic conflicts;
  • merge: three-way merge orchestration;
  • rebase: replay against a new base;
  • query: history/change queries;
  • summary: compact structural summaries.

Do not implement algorithms in this scaffold task.

docs.title: Conformance test placeholder
docs.text:
tests/change_conformance.rs should compile and contain a module-level comment listing the cases prescribed by Level 2.

Do not add ignored failing tests merely to reserve names. Add real tests only when the relevant implementation task is completed.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Do not define duplicate EntityId, RevisionId, or SnapshotId types.
  • Do not issue SQL.
  • Do not depend on a concrete store backend from library code.
  • Do not add Markdown-, Rust-, PDF-, or session-specific change variants.
  • Do not create agent APIs.
  • Do not modify Level 1 or Level 2 documents.
  • Do not add speculative abstractions not needed by the prescribed module boundaries.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run the repository's normal formatter and checks. At minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If the repository uses additional standard checks, run them too.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] crates/sr-change exists.
  • [ ] Root workspace includes the crate.
  • [ ] sr-change depends on sr-core and sr-store, not concrete backends.
  • [ ] All 14 source modules exist.
  • [ ] change_conformance.rs exists.
  • [ ] Module responsibilities are documented.
  • [ ] No domain-specific behavior was introduced.
  • [ ] Workspace formatting, build, and tests pass.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text:
Report:

  • files created or modified;
  • dependency changes;
  • commands run and whether they passed;
  • any prerequisite mismatch discovered.

Do not claim later change-model tasks are implemented merely because the module files exist.

docs.title: Extend Shared Core with Knowledge Values and Provenance
Objective
docs.text:
Extend the existing shared core crate with the domain-independent value and provenance types required by the universal knowledge model.

Do not bootstrap a new workspace and do not create a second core crate.

This task is intentionally narrow: it adds universal property values, canonical/derived classification, and provenance. Identity generation, content addressing, canonical encoding, revision hashing, and snapshot storage are owned by other designs.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read these documents before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  3. the repository-wide workspace/package-layout Level 2 design;
  4. the identity/revision/snapshot Level 2 design that owns EntityId, RevisionId, and SnapshotId.

Inspect the root Cargo workspace before editing.

Use the core crate already registered there. The workspace design may call it scriberig-core; earlier identity work may have used another provisional name. Do not create another core crate to resolve a naming mismatch. Extend the canonical crate that actually exists in the workspace.

If no shared core crate exists yet, this task's prerequisite has not been implemented. Do not invent a competing workspace; report the unmet prerequisite.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the established shared core crate:

src/value.rs
src/provenance.rs
src/lib.rs
Cargo.toml            # only if a narrowly required dependency/feature is needed

If value.rs or provenance.rs already exists, extend it instead of creating a parallel module.

Do not modify identity-generation or canonical-encoding code unless a tiny public re-export is required to use the existing types.

docs.title: 1. Universal Property Value
docs.text:
Implement a public domain-neutral enum named KnowledgeValue or the equivalent name already chosen by the crate.

It must represent at least:

Null
Bool
SignedInteger
UnsignedInteger
Float
String
Bytes
List
Record

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text:
• List preserves element order.
  • Record uses string keys and should use deterministic iteration ordering where practical.
  • The type represents local property payloads, not semantic graph edges.
  • Do not add an EntityRef variant merely for convenience; semantic references belong in typed relations/collections.
  • Do not add domain-specific variants such as RustExpression, MarkdownParagraph, PdfPage, or SessionBranch.

docs.title: Traits
docs.text:
Provide sensible traits such as:

Clone
Debug
PartialEq

If floating-point values prevent honest total equality or hashing, do not invent misleading Eq/Hash semantics.

Provide only obvious small From conversions. Avoid a large conversion framework.

docs.title: 2. Canonical vs Derived Classification
docs.text:
Define one shared public classification enum, using a clear name such as KnowledgeClass:

Canonical
Derived

This type only classifies how a field/artifact participates in semantic state.

It does not decide whether a particular domain value is canonical. Schemas make that decision.

docs.title: 3. Provenance Inputs
docs.text:
Use the existing identity types from the shared core crate.

Define an exact dependency/reference structure if the core does not already have one, conceptually:

EntityRevisionRef {
    entity_id: EntityId,
    revision_id: RevisionId,
}

If another design already defines an equivalent exact reference type, reuse it.

Do not redefine EntityId or RevisionId.

docs.title: 4. Provenance Source
docs.text:
Define an extensible public source-kind representation capable of expressing at least:

User
AuthoritativeImport
Parser
Compiler
StaticAnalysis
Agent
ModelGenerated
System
ExternalTool
Migration
Custom(String)

The exact enum/type name may follow existing project naming.

The custom case is important so introducing a new producer category does not always require changing the core crate.

Provenance source records origin, not trust level.

Do not add trust scores, authorization decisions, or policy evaluation here.

docs.title: 5. Provenance Record
docs.text:
Implement a Provenance record containing enough data to answer:

  • what kind of source produced this knowledge?
  • what producer/tool/model produced it, if known?
  • which exact immutable entity revisions were inputs, if known?
  • which profile/configuration produced it, if relevant?
  • is there a short explanatory note?

Required conceptual fields:

source
producer              optional
inputs                zero or more exact entity/revision refs
profile/config        optional
note                  optional

Use an existing shared producer/profile identifier type if one already exists. Otherwise use a narrowly scoped string/newtype without inventing persistence semantics.

Do not include timestamps merely because provenance often has timestamps. Timestamps are not required by the Level 1 semantic model and may be added later by a history/audit design.

docs.title: 6. Public Exports
docs.text:
Update the shared core lib.rs so downstream schema/graph crates can import the new types from a stable public path.

Expose at least the equivalents of:

KnowledgeValue
KnowledgeClass
Provenance
ProvenanceSource
EntityRevisionRef      if newly defined here

Do not disturb existing public exports from identity/storage work.

docs.title: 7. Unit Tests
docs.text:
Add focused tests for:

  1. nested List values;
  2. nested Record values;
  3. list order preservation;
  4. deterministic record behavior where promised by the implementation;
  5. canonical vs derived classification;
  6. provenance with no inputs;
  7. provenance with multiple exact revision inputs;
  8. a custom provenance source;
  9. proof that semantic entity references are represented by provenance/reference types rather than encoded as arbitrary property-value variants.

Do not add database-backed tests.

  • semantic relationships are not encoded as arbitrary values;

Keep documentation concise and API-focused.

This task implements the authority vocabulary required by design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md. It does not implement authentication, secrets, policy evaluation, query filtering, or UI.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:

  2. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md.
  3. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  4. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md.
  5. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md.

Inspect the actual workspace before editing. Reuse existing crates and naming. If the Rust workspace or canonical core/application crates do not exist yet, stop and report the missing prerequisite instead of creating a competing layout.

docs.text:
Use the existing shared core crate only for small cross-cutting identity/value types that lower layers may need for attribution. Put capability semantics and enforcement-facing types in the shared application crate.

crates/scriberig-core/src/principal.rs

crates/scriberig-app/src/capability.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

docs.title: Principal Types
docs.text:
Define a stable PrincipalId newtype, or reuse an equivalent existing type. It identifies an actor for attribution; it does not imply permission.

Add a compact actor-kind vocabulary sufficient to distinguish at least:

Human
Agent
System
Service
Connector
Importer
Validator
ApiClient
Custom

Keep custom/extension support so new actor categories do not require changing the core crate.

Do not put credentials, authentication claims, roles, or capability lists inside PrincipalId.

docs.title: Capability Model
docs.text:
In the application layer, define an explicit capability value with three parts:

scope
actions
constraints

Support at least these actions:

Inspect
Query
Render
Propose
ModifyBranch
Validate
Promote
InvokeExternal

The scope model must be able to represent project, session, branch, entity, relation/projection, and external-destination scopes without encoding unrestricted filesystem paths as authority.

Constraints must be able to bind authority to an exact snapshot and, where applicable, a branch, domain, operation kind, lifetime, or external destination.

Prefer typed enums/newtypes over arbitrary strings for core actions. Allow extension points where future domains need additional actions.

docs.title: Least-Authority Semantics
docs.text:
Implement pure helper functions for checking whether one capability covers a requested operation and whether a delegated capability is no broader than its parent.

Required invariants:

  • absence of a capability means denial;
  • read authority does not imply write authority;
  • branch modification does not imply promotion;
  • local semantic modification does not imply external side effects;
  • a child/delegated capability may be equal to or narrower than its parent, never broader;
  • content stored in the graph cannot create or modify a capability value merely by being read.

Do not add ambient global capability state.

docs.title: Structured Denial
docs.text:
Define an application-level denial type containing at least:

principal
requested_action
requested_scope
reason
optional narrower alternatives
approval_possible flag or equivalent

Do not expose secrets or hidden object contents in the denial text.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add unit tests proving:

  1. inspect does not grant promote;
  2. modify-branch does not grant promote;
  3. project read can cover a descendant read when the scope rules explicitly allow it;
  4. entity-only access does not automatically cover arbitrary relation traversal;
  5. external invocation requires an external destination scope;
  6. delegated capability cannot widen scope;
  7. delegated capability cannot add an action absent from the parent;
  8. snapshot constraints are enforced;
  9. capability denial is a normal structured result;
  10. principal identity alone grants nothing.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not implement login, OAuth, password handling, cryptographic tokens, secret storage, HTTP middleware, model-specific rules, filesystem sandboxing, or project promotion. Do not add permission fields to ordinary domain entities.

  • [ ] read, branch modification, promotion, and external invocation are distinct;
  • [ ] delegation cannot increase authority;
  • [ ] structured denial exists;
  • [ ] no lower storage crate depends on application authorization;
  • [ ] focused tests pass.

Objective

  • derivation profile identity;

Do not implement result persistence, invalidation, selection, freshness, retention, events, domain execution, agents, or server integration in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read these documents before editing:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  4. the repository-wide workspace/package-layout Level 2 design;
  5. the identity/revision/snapshot implementation design.

Inspect the actual root Cargo.toml and existing crate directories.

The design uses the name scriberig-derive, but earlier designs may have standardized the workspace on sr-* crate names. Use the naming convention already established in the real workspace.

Do not create both scriberig-derive and sr-derive.

If a derivation crate already exists, extend it.

If the shared core identity crate or universal graph crate does not exist yet, this task has unmet prerequisites. Do not reimplement those prerequisites inside the derivation crate.

docs.title: 1. Crate Dependencies
docs.text:
Depend only on the lowest layers needed for exact identities and universal graph references.

Expected dependencies are conceptually:

shared core
universal graph

Do not add:

  • SQLite;
  • Tokio merely for future async work;
  • HTTP libraries;
  • model-provider SDKs;
  • CLI libraries;
  • UI libraries;
  • Markdown/Rust/PDF/session crates.

Keep dependencies minimal.

docs.title: 2. Derivation Profile
docs.text:
In profile.rs, define public types representing an exact derivation definition.

The model must distinguish:

human/domain kind
exact version/revision
optional producer/implementation identity
optional configuration identity
scheduling hint

Use existing strongly typed identifier/value conventions where available.

A simple initial representation is acceptable if it remains explicit and deterministic.

For example, an exact profile may conceptually contain:

kind: "function-summary"
version: "v1"
producer: optional exact producer identity
configuration: optional exact configuration identity
schedule: Lazy | Eager

Do not create a mutable global current profile.

If aliases are needed later, they belong outside exact profile identity.

docs.title: Required properties
docs.text:
• profiles are cloneable and debuggable;
  • equality means compatible derivation semantics;
  • fields participating in equality are deterministic;
  • domain names are represented by extensible identifiers/strings, not hard-coded production enums.

docs.title: 3. Dependency Types
docs.text:
In dependency.rs, define a domain-independent dependency enum or equivalent tagged representation.

It must support at least:

ExactRevision
Snapshot
ScopeOrCollection
Configuration
DerivedResult

docs.title: Exact revision dependency
docs.text:
Must reference an exact entity/revision pair using the existing shared type when available.

Do not represent an exact dependency as EntityId alone.

docs.title: Snapshot dependency
docs.text: References an exact SnapshotId when a derivation genuinely depends on a whole scope.

docs.title: Scope or collection dependency
docs.text:
Represents completeness/absence dependencies independently from positive result members.

The first implementation may use an opaque deterministic scope identity rather than designing every possible domain scope.

The important requirement is that scope dependency is a first-class variant.

docs.title: Configuration dependency
docs.text:
Represents exact semantic configuration such as style/toolchain/schema/adapter configuration.

Use an opaque exact identity/value rather than process-global mutable state.

docs.title: Derived-result dependency
docs.text:
References another immutable derived result identity or exact artifact handle using an existing appropriate type if one exists.

Do not invent domain-specific variants.

docs.title: 4. Dependency Set
docs.text:
Define DependencySet or an equivalent type.

It must:

  • contain zero or more dependencies;
  • produce deterministic equality/order/encoding behavior;
  • avoid treating incidental insertion order as semantic when dependencies are logically a set;
  • make duplicate dependencies harmless or reject them deterministically;
  • be easy to inspect for debugging.

Prefer a deterministic ordered set representation or explicit normalization.

Do not rely on nondeterministic hash-map iteration for cache-key identity.

docs.title: 5. Derivation Key
docs.text:
In key.rs, define DerivationKey.

It must include:

exact derivation profile
normalized dependency set

If the project already has a canonical encoding/hash abstraction appropriate for deterministic values, integrate with it.

If not, implement deterministic structural equality first and leave cryptographic/content hashing to the existing identity layer or later work. Do not invent a second hashing system.

The key must satisfy these invariants:

  1. same profile + same normalized dependencies => same key/equality;
  2. changing one RevisionId => different key;
  3. changing one scope/snapshot/config dependency => different key;
  4. changing dependency insertion order alone => same key;
  5. unrelated project changes are absent from a local key unless explicitly declared as dependencies.

Do not automatically insert the current SnapshotId into every key.

docs.title: 6. Public API
docs.text:
Update lib.rs to expose stable public equivalents of:

DerivationProfile
DerivationSchedule
Dependency
DependencySet
DerivationKey

Avoid broad glob re-exports if the repository style prefers explicit module paths.

Add crate-level documentation stating:

  • the crate models derived/cache semantics;
  • cache population does not alter canonical snapshots;
  • exact reuse is revision/dependency based;
  • the crate is usable without agents or a server.

docs.title: 7. Required Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • two equal profiles;
  • profile version change changes equality;
  • exact revision dependency uses both entity and revision;
  • dependency-set normalization ignores insertion order;
  • duplicate dependency normalization;
  • same profile/dependencies produce equal derivation keys;
  • one revision change changes key;
  • one configuration dependency change changes key;
  • one snapshot dependency change changes key;
  • a local key remains unchanged when an unrelated snapshot exists but is not a declared dependency;
  • scope dependency is representable without positive result members;
  • custom domain/profile names work without changing production enums.

Use fake/test IDs according to the existing core test helpers.
