docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Make the shared application layer enforce effective capability scope for inspection, traversal, search, reverse lookups, summaries, and derived views.

The generic graph/query libraries remain reusable below policy. Scriberig product surfaces must use the guarded application operations.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 8–13, 30–31, 52, 62–63.
  2. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md.
  3. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  4. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  5. Existing query/application Level 2 or Level 3 designs that own graph traversal and query APIs.

If the query crate or application-operation boundary is not implemented, stop and report that prerequisite rather than adding policy directly to storage.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Work primarily in the application layer. Typical files may include:

crates/scriberig-app/src/authorization.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/query.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/inspect.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

Adapt names to the actual repository. Do not move authorization into scriberig-store or make the reusable query engine agent-specific.

docs.title: Guarded Operations
docs.text:
Create or extend application operations for at least:

inspect entity
list/follow relations
reverse relation lookup
search/find
get description/summary
diff/history lookup where data exposure occurs

Every operation must receive or resolve an effective principal/capability context before returning semantic data.

docs.title: Traversal Rule
docs.text:
Authorization must be checked at each exposed result boundary, not only on the root object.

A caller permitted to inspect Function F must not automatically receive every entity reachable from F through arbitrary relations.

Search and reverse indexes must not reveal restricted entity names, descriptions, snippets, counts, or existence when the policy says those facts are confidential.

Choose one consistent behavior for hidden results through the existing application error/result conventions:

  • filtered from result sets; or
  • represented by an explicit redacted/denied result when the caller already knows the identifier.

Document that behavior in code comments and tests.

docs.title: Derived Views
docs.text:
Descriptions, summaries, cached semantic views, and convenience projections must be checked against the dependencies they expose. Do not treat them as public merely because they are derived.

This task does not implement cache partitioning; it must ensure the application path cannot fetch a derived artifact whose effective scope is broader than the principal's authority.

docs.title: Structured Denials
docs.text:
Use the denial type from the capability task. Do not convert a capability denial into NotFound unless an existing confidentiality policy explicitly requires non-disclosure of existence.

Do not include restricted content in error messages.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Build fixtures with at least two allowed entities and one restricted entity. Test:

  1. direct allowed inspection succeeds;
  2. direct restricted inspection is denied;
  3. allowed root traversal does not leak a restricted neighbor;
  4. reverse lookup does not leak a restricted source;
  5. global search omits restricted text/snippets;
  6. summary lookup respects the subject's access scope;
  7. a caller with broader capability sees the same hidden entity;
  8. denial does not disclose hidden payload text;
  9. lower-level query APIs remain callable without application policy for intentional embedded-library use;
  10. official application operations never bypass the guard.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. Add integration tests at the application boundary rather than only unit-testing helper predicates.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not add authorization checks to every storage read. Do not modify query semantics to contain agent-specific concepts. Do not create a second search implementation for authorized callers. Do not assume UI filtering is a security boundary.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] all application read/query paths use one capability guard;
  • [ ] relation traversal is scope-aware;
  • [ ] search/reverse indexes do not leak restricted content;
  • [ ] derived views respect source access;
  • [ ] low-level libraries remain usable below policy;
  • [ ] tests demonstrate both allowed and denied traversal.

docs.title: Implement: Canonical Encoding and Revision API
Objective
docs.text:
Implement deterministic canonical revision encoding and the backend-independent revision storage API.

This task must make exact revision identity executable without introducing any domain-specific schema.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. persistence crate boundaries.md
  3. design/level-2/002. canonical encoding and revision identity.md
  4. design/level-3/001. bootstrap persistence workspace and core ids.md

Assume the workspace and ID types from task 001 exist.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
Work primarily in:

crates/sr-core/src/encoding.rs
crates/sr-core/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/revision.rs
crates/sr-store/src/error.rs

Create test modules or integration tests where useful.

docs.title: Canonical encoding
docs.text:
Implement a small, versioned canonical encoding facility sufficient to encode storage-level revision envelopes.

A revision envelope contains:

encoding version
object type
canonical payload bytes

Requirements:

  • output is deterministic;
  • object type is included in identity;
  • encoding version is included in identity;
  • payload length/boundaries are unambiguous;
  • implementation does not depend on Rust struct memory layout;
  • malformed encoded input returns a typed error;
  • the byte format is documented in Rust module docs or comments near the encoder.

Do not build a universal domain serialization system in this task. Treat the canonical payload as bytes already prepared by the caller.

docs.title: Revision ID computation
docs.text:
Implement a function that computes RevisionId by hashing the complete canonical revision envelope with BLAKE3.

The same envelope must always produce the same ID.

Different ObjectType, encoding version, or canonical payload must produce a different encoded envelope and normally a different ID.

docs.title: Backend-independent revision record
docs.text:
In sr-store, define a logical immutable revision record containing at least:

  • RevisionId;
  • ObjectType;
  • EncodingVersion;
  • canonical payload bytes.

Provide construction that computes/validates identity rather than trusting an arbitrary caller-supplied ID.

docs.title: Revision store interface
docs.text:
Define a backend-independent trait or equivalent API with operations equivalent to:

put_revision(revision) -> RevisionId
get_revision(RevisionId) -> revision or not-found
has_revision(RevisionId) -> bool

Inserting the same exact revision more than once must be idempotent from the caller's perspective.

The API must not expose SQL, file paths, row IDs, or backend handles.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Add machine-readable storage errors for at least:

  • not found;
  • invalid canonical encoding;
  • revision identity mismatch;
  • invalid operation;
  • backend failure wrapper/category for future implementations.

Do not use string matching in tests to determine error categories.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • fixed fixture envelope produces fixed canonical bytes;
  • same envelope constructed twice produces identical bytes and ID;
  • different object type changes encoded bytes/ID;
  • different encoding version changes encoded bytes/ID;
  • changed payload changes ID;
  • malformed envelope decode fails cleanly if decode is implemented;
  • revision record construction rejects mismatched externally supplied identity if such constructor exists.

Use at least one golden fixture for canonical bytes so accidental encoding changes fail loudly.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not implement snapshots or roots.
  • Do not add SQLite tables.
  • Do not add semantic relations.
  • Do not invent paragraph/function schemas.
  • Do not add timestamps to canonical revision identity.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Canonical revision envelope format exists and is documented.
  • [ ] Revision IDs are derived from canonical envelope bytes.
  • [ ] Backend-neutral immutable revision record exists.
  • [ ] Backend-neutral revision-store interface exists.
  • [ ] Error categories are typed.
  • [ ] Golden deterministic-encoding tests pass.
  • [ ] Entire workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Implement Canonical Encoding and Revision Hashing
Mission
docs.text:
Implement deterministic canonical byte encoding in sr-core and the exact hashing rule used to produce RevisionId values.

This task must make revision hashing deterministic across runs, platforms, map insertion orders, and unrelated Rust implementation details.

Do not implement revision storage or snapshots yet.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/001. bootstrap workspace and identity types.md

Assume Level 3 task 001 has already been completed.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify:

crates/sr-core/src/canonical.rs
crates/sr-core/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-core/src/ids.rs
crates/sr-core/Cargo.toml

Modify ids.rs only where needed to expose safe constructors/accessors for hash-derived IDs. Do not redesign the identity types.

docs.title: Canonical Writer
docs.text:
Create a deterministic CanonicalWriter backed by Vec<u8>.

It must provide explicit methods for at least:

  • [ ] writing a fixed byte/domain tag;
  • [ ] u8;
  • [ ] u16;
  • [ ] u32;
  • [ ] u64;
  • [ ] booleans with fixed discriminants;
  • [ ] raw bytes with an explicit length prefix;
  • [ ] UTF-8 strings with byte-length prefix;
  • [ ] optional values with explicit present/absent discriminant;
  • [ ] sequence length before sequence contents.

Use one specified endian order for multi-byte integers. Use big-endian unless the Level 2 design is updated before implementation.

Lengths must use a fixed-width integer representation. Use u64 for encoded lengths unless there is a compelling implementation blocker.

Do not serialize usize directly because it is platform-sized.

docs.title: CanonicalEncode
docs.text:
Expose:

pub trait CanonicalEncode {
    fn encode_canonical(&self, out: &mut CanonicalWriter);
}

Implement it where useful for the primitive identity/configuration types, but do not create a blanket serde-based implementation.

The trait must make ordering an explicit caller responsibility for maps or sets.

Document that unordered containers must be sorted before encoding.

docs.title: Revision Hashing
docs.text:
Add BLAKE3 as a dependency.

Define one fixed revision-domain tag in code. Keep it private or crate-visible unless callers need it for conformance tests.

Provide one public helper with behavior equivalent to:

hash_revision(
  encoding_version,
  type_id,
  canonical_payload
) -> RevisionId

The hash input must be exactly the canonical encoding of:

revision domain tag
encoding version
type ID
canonical payload bytes

The EntityId must not participate in this hash.

No timestamps, pointers, process IDs, random values, insertion-order artifacts, or mutable aliases may participate.

docs.title: Encoding Version
docs.text:
Version 1 must be encoded into every revision hash.

Do not hard-code a raw integer in multiple places. Use the EncodingVersion type from task 001.

docs.title: Determinism Tests
docs.text:
Add focused tests proving:

  • [ ] the same inputs produce the same bytes;
  • [ ] the same revision inputs produce the same RevisionId;
  • [ ] changing payload changes RevisionId;
  • [ ] changing TypeId changes RevisionId;
  • [ ] changing EncodingVersion changes RevisionId;
  • [ ] EntityId is not an input to revision hashing;
  • [ ] encoding a fixed sequence produces an expected fixed byte vector;
  • [ ] strings use byte length, not character count;
  • [ ] the implementation does not depend on native endianness.

At least one canonical encoding test must assert exact bytes, not merely compare two runs of the same function.

docs.title: Public Documentation
docs.text:
Add rustdoc explaining:

  • why canonical encoding exists;
  • why general JSON serialization is not used for identity;
  • why map/set ordering must be canonicalized by callers;
  • why changing encoding rules requires a new encoding version.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not hash Debug output.
  • Do not hash serde JSON text.
  • Do not hash Rust memory layout.
  • Do not use HashMap iteration order.
  • Do not include EntityId in RevisionId.
  • Do not implement SnapshotId hashing in this task.
  • Do not create sr-store in this task.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] CanonicalWriter exists.
  • [ ] CanonicalEncode exists.
  • [ ] Revision hashing uses BLAKE3 and a domain tag.
  • [ ] Encoding version participates in the hash.
  • [ ] Exact-byte canonical tests pass.
  • [ ] Revision hashing determinism tests pass.
  • [ ] Workspace formatting, tests, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement Derived Result Records and Repository Contract
Objective
docs.text:
Implement immutable derived-result records and the backend-independent repository contract described by the derived-knowledge Level 2 design.

This task builds on the derivation profiles, dependencies, and keys created by the previous task.

It must make it possible to store, retrieve, and inspect immutable derived results without coupling the derivation layer to SQLite, an agent runtime, or a server.

Do not implement invalidation, selection policy, freshness policy, retention policy, events, or domain-specific derivation execution in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. design/level-3/001. scaffold derivation crate profiles dependencies and keys.md
  4. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md

Inspect the actual universal graph crate before editing.

The graph layer owns the generic DerivedArtifact model. Reuse that model or the canonical equivalent already implemented in the repository.

If the graph layer has not yet implemented a derived-artifact type, treat that as an unmet prerequisite rather than creating a competing artifact model inside the derivation crate.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical derivation crate:

src/result.rs
src/repository.rs
src/lib.rs

Tests may be module-local or added to the final integration test later.

Do not create a SQLite table or backend-specific crate in this task.

docs.title: 1. Derived Result Status
docs.text:
Define a small public status model for an immutable derivation attempt/result.

It must be able to represent at least conceptual equivalents of:

Succeeded
FailedDeterministic
FailedTransient
Cancelled

If cancellation is better represented as transient/non-cacheable metadata according to existing project conventions, preserve that distinction clearly.

The key requirement is that consumers can tell whether a failure may safely satisfy a later identical request or should normally be retried.

Do not infer retryability from a human-readable error string.

docs.title: 2. Derived Result Record
docs.text:
Define DerivedResultRecord or the canonical equivalent.

It must bind together:

DerivationKey
DerivedArtifact or exact artifact reference
status
provenance
optional failure metadata
optional observation/creation metadata when the existing shared types support it

Do not make the artifact canonical simply by wrapping it in this record.

Do not add a mutable is_current field.

Historical results must remain immutable.

Multiple records may exist for derivations that are nondeterministic or intentionally regenerated.

If the existing universal artifact already contains provenance, avoid duplicating contradictory provenance fields. Prefer one authoritative provenance structure and reference it from the result record.

docs.title: 3. Result Identity
docs.text:
Use existing content/identity abstractions if the project already provides them.

Do not invent a new unrelated hash format.

The repository contract must be able to return one or more stable result handles so later dependency records and selection logic can reference exact historical results.

If no dedicated DerivedResultId exists yet, use the narrowest existing immutable object/artifact identifier available and document that choice.

Do not use array indexes or database row numbers as public semantic identity.

docs.title: 4. Repository Trait
docs.text:
In repository.rs, define a backend-independent DerivedRepository trait or equivalent.

The first contract must support:

insert immutable result
get exact result by result handle
find all results for exact DerivationKey
find results associated with an entity/revision when indexed
record dependency metadata for a result
read dependency metadata for a result
lookup result handles by dependency
remove disposable derived records when explicitly requested

The trait may be synchronous unless the repository already has an established async abstraction at this layer.

Do not add Tokio merely to future-proof the trait.

The trait must describe semantic operations, not SQL.

docs.title: 5. Duplicate and Concurrent Insert Semantics
docs.text:
Document and implement deterministic semantics for inserting the same immutable result more than once.

At minimum:

  • inserting an identical immutable result must not corrupt storage;
  • repository implementations may deduplicate exact results;
  • multiple distinct results for one derivation key must be allowed;
  • no insertion operation may overwrite a previous historical result in place.

The repository abstraction should be compatible with two workers finishing the same derivation concurrently.

Do not require process-local locking in the public API.

docs.title: 6. Dependency Recording
docs.text:
A result must expose or allow repository lookup of the exact dependencies from its DerivationKey.

The repository must not require consumers to reverse-engineer dependencies from arbitrary payload bytes.

If dependency indexing is maintained separately from the result record, make that relationship explicit in the trait.

The final invalidation task will use this lookup.

Do not implement invalidation logic yet.

docs.title: 7. Entity/Revision Lookup
docs.text:
Provide a narrow lookup path that lets diagnostics and navigation discover derived results associated with an exact entity/revision.

This is not the validity mechanism.

Exact validity still comes from DerivationKey dependencies.

The entity/revision association is for discovery, history, and inspection.

Do not implement ambiguous implicit-current entity lookup.

docs.title: 8. In-Memory Test Repository
docs.text:
If no generic memory repository already exists for derived data, implement a minimal in-memory repository inside tests or a test-support module, not as a new production backend crate.

It should be sufficient to verify the repository contract.

Do not introduce a permanent memory backend API unless another design already establishes one.

Required behavior:

  • immutable insert;
  • exact lookup;
  • key lookup returning multiple results;
  • dependency lookup;
  • explicit removal of a disposable result;
  • old records remain unchanged after newer compatible results are inserted.

docs.title: 9. Public Exports
docs.text:
Update lib.rs to expose the intended public equivalents of:

DerivedResultRecord
DerivedResultStatus
DerivedRepository

Keep failure metadata types public only if clients need them to inspect results.

Avoid exposing test-support implementations as production API.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
Add focused tests for:

  1. successful result record creation;
  2. deterministic failure record;
  3. transient failure record;
  4. two distinct results for one exact derivation key coexist;
  5. reinserting an identical immutable result is safe;
  6. exact result lookup works;
  7. exact key lookup returns all matching records;
  8. dependency metadata can be retrieved without inspecting payload bytes;
  9. reverse dependency lookup returns the stored result handle;
  10. entity/revision discovery lookup does not replace exact key validity;
  11. explicit deletion/removal affects only derived storage and does not invoke any canonical snapshot operation.

Use fake universal artifacts and test profiles. Do not introduce production domain vocabulary.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

Run clippy if it is already part of repository practice.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • modify canonical snapshot state when inserting a result;
  • add SQLite;
  • add model/provider SDKs;
  • add server/protocol types;
  • add agent tools;
  • implement preferred-result selection;
  • implement freshness or retention;
  • implement invalidation;
  • hard-code domain derivation kinds;
  • duplicate DerivedArtifact from the graph layer.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] immutable derived result record exists;
  • [ ] success and failure statuses are structured;
  • [ ] exact result identity is reusable by later tasks;
  • [ ] repository trait is backend-independent;
  • [ ] multiple results per derivation key are supported;
  • [ ] exact dependencies are queryable;
  • [ ] reverse dependency lookup is possible;
  • [ ] entity/revision discovery lookup exists;
  • [ ] no canonical snapshot mutation occurs;
  • [ ] focused repository-contract tests pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the canonical Markdown domain vocabulary described by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md inside scriberig-domain-markdown.

This task defines what Markdown knowledge means after it is inside Scriberig. It does not implement filesystem watching, external-edit reconciliation orchestration, agent tools, or UI components.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/001. scaffold domain adapter crates.md
  4. the current public APIs of scriberig-core, scriberig-schema, and scriberig-graph

Do not create substitute schema or graph frameworks inside the Markdown crate. If required shared APIs are not implemented yet, stop and report the missing prerequisite.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/markdown/, create:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/types.rs
src/classification.rs

Add tests either as module tests or under:

tests/schema.rs

Do not create parser, renderer, or reconciliation modules in this task.

docs.title: Canonical Entity Vocabulary
docs.text:
Define the Markdown domain vocabulary needed for the first implementation slice:

MarkdownDocument
Section
Heading
Paragraph
List
ListItem
Table
TableRow
TableCell
CodeBlock
QuoteBlock
Link
ImageReference
InlineContent

Use the shared schema system rather than defining an unrelated local type registry.

The schema must make the following structural intent representable:

MarkdownDocument
  contains ordered top-level blocks/sections

Section
  has optional heading/title structure
  contains ordered blocks and nested sections

List
  contains ordered ListItem entities

Table
  contains ordered TableRow entities

TableRow
  contains ordered TableCell entities

Paragraph, Heading, CodeBlock, QuoteBlock, Link, ImageReference, and InlineContent must be independently addressable semantic entities where the shared model supports entity identity.

docs.title: Canonical, Derived, and Projection-Only Classification
docs.text:
Create an explicit Markdown-domain classification that communicates which information belongs to canonical state.

At minimum, encode or expose the following decisions:

Canonical:

section/block structure
paragraph text/content
list/item structure and order
table/row/cell structure and order
code block semantic content
links and image references
meaningful inline structure needed for faithful round-trip behavior

Projection-only by default:

indentation width
line wrapping
blank-line count used only for formatting
table column padding/alignment spacing
other whitespace with no Markdown semantic meaning

Derived by default:

summaries
topic labels
generated outlines
model-generated descriptions
search indexes

Do not mark a generated description canonical.

The concrete representation of this classification must use existing shared schema metadata if available. If no shared mechanism exists yet, expose a small Markdown-local function or constants that describe the classification without inventing a second persistence model.

docs.title: Relations and Collections
docs.text:
Use universal relations/collections rather than embedding opaque nested JSON when shared graph primitives exist.

The schema should support at least these semantic relations:

MarkdownDocument --contains--> Section/Block
Section --contains--> Section/Block
List --contains--> ListItem
Table --contains--> TableRow
TableRow --contains--> TableCell

Containment must be ordered where document order is meaningful.

Do not store reverse parent IDs as canonical child properties solely for navigation. Reverse traversal should use shared graph/index behavior.

docs.title: Navigation Expectations
docs.text:
The schema must support progressive disclosure:

Document
  -> top-level Section/Block
     -> nested Section/Block
        -> Paragraph/Table/List/etc.
           -> Row/Cell/Item/InlineContent

A future consumer must be able to inspect a document or section and learn child counts/types without loading the full document body.

This task does not implement the query surface, but the schema must not prevent that access pattern.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
Expose only the minimum public API necessary for other crates to obtain/register the Markdown schema and refer to Markdown domain type/relation identifiers.

Prefer a shape equivalent to:

markdown_schema()

or the established registration pattern already used by scriberig-schema.

Do not invent a parallel registration mechanism.

lib.rs should re-export the stable Markdown schema entry point and domain identifiers needed by later adapter tasks.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving at least:

  • every required Markdown entity type is present;
  • ordered containment is defined for lists, tables, rows, sections, and document blocks;
  • a paragraph can exist as an independently addressable entity;
  • canonical/projection-only/derived classification matches this task;
  • invalid obvious relations are rejected if the shared schema system supports endpoint validation;
  • schema registration is deterministic.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-markdown
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-markdown --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not parse Markdown text yet.
  • Do not render Markdown text yet.
  • Do not implement external-edit reconciliation.
  • Do not add summaries or model calls.
  • Do not add filesystem code.
  • Do not add SQL tables.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.
  • Do not treat source byte ranges as semantic identity.
  • Do not make formatting whitespace canonical unless required by Markdown semantics.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All required Markdown entity types exist in the shared schema system.
  • [ ] Ordered containment is modeled explicitly.
  • [ ] Paragraphs, rows, and cells are independently addressable.
  • [ ] Canonical, derived, and projection-only boundaries are explicit.
  • [ ] Schema registration is deterministic.
  • [ ] No parser/render/reconciliation behavior is included.
  • [ ] No private persistence model was introduced.
  • [ ] Tests pass.
  • [ ] Formatting, tests, and clippy checks pass.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Migration, Operations, and Provenance
Goal
docs.text:
Implement the universal migration data model in sr-change.

This task covers exact snapshot transitions, entity deltas, generic semantic operations, domain-extensible operations, and change provenance. It does not implement history traversal, branch logic, merge, rebase, or persistence backends.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 3 through 10 and 47 through 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Existing sr-core identifier types and public conventions.
  4. Existing sr-store error/result conventions if they are relevant to constructors.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
Primary files:

crates/sr-change/src/migration.rs
crates/sr-change/src/operation.rs
crates/sr-change/src/provenance.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs

Add unit tests beside the implementation or in a focused test module following repository convention.

Do not modify merge/rebase code in this task.

docs.title: Implement EntityDelta
docs.text:
Add a public universal entity transition type equivalent in meaning to:

EntityDelta {
    entity: EntityId,
    before: Option<RevisionId>,
    after: Option<RevisionId>,
}

Enforce the invariant that before == after is not a valid delta.

Provide clear helpers or predicates for:

is_created
is_removed
is_modified

Do not infer physical deletion from is_removed; it only means absence from the resulting canonical state.

docs.title: Implement Migration
docs.text:
A migration must contain at least:

base SnapshotId
result SnapshotId
entity deltas
source/provenance
semantic operations

Add parent/change references only if the current identifier model supports them cleanly. Do not invent storage-specific row IDs.

Construction must reject:

  • identical base/result snapshots when the migration claims canonical changes;
  • duplicate deltas for the same entity;
  • no-op entity deltas.

A representation-only operation is not a semantic migration and should not be modeled by manufacturing an empty canonical migration.

docs.title: Generic operations
docs.text:
Implement a universal enum or equivalent tagged model containing the Level 2 operations:

CreateEntity
ReplaceRevision
RemoveEntity
AddRelation
RemoveRelation
InsertCollectionMember
RemoveCollectionMember
MoveCollectionMember
ReplaceCollectionStructure

Use existing universal relation/collection identifiers from sr-core or adjacent generic crates if available.

If those identifiers do not exist yet, do not define domain-specific substitutes. Introduce only the smallest generic value type required and document why it belongs in sr-change versus sr-core.

Each operation must reference semantic entities and semantic positions/relations, never file offsets or line numbers.

docs.title: Domain-specific operation support
docs.text:
Add a representation that lets domain crates attach richer semantic intent without adding domain variants to the generic enum.

Requirements:

  • explicit domain/type identity;
  • opaque payload or typed reference whose encoding does not require sr-change to understand the domain;
  • safe round-trip through the generic model;
  • no dependency from sr-change to a domain crate.

Prefer the repository's canonical encoding/value conventions. Do not introduce JSON merely for convenience if the repository uses another generic value representation.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
Implement a source category model covering at least:

User
ExternalProjection
Agent
Cli
Api
WebEditor
Tui
Importer
Refactoring
Merge
Synchronization
System
Other

Add a provenance structure that can carry optional structured references such as:

  • actor/tool identifier;
  • branch/workspace entity;
  • projection entity;
  • validation result references;
  • parent migration/change references;
  • extension metadata.

Keep optional metadata generic. Do not make agent-specific fields mandatory.

docs.title: Ordering and determinism
docs.text:
Where migration identity or canonical encoding depends on ordering, normalize the representation deterministically.

Entity deltas should have a deterministic order independent of insertion order.

Do not silently reorder operations whose sequence is semantically meaningful.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Use typed errors for invalid migration construction.

At minimum distinguish:

NoOpDelta
DuplicateEntityDelta
InvalidSnapshotTransition
InvalidOperation

Fit these into existing repository error conventions rather than creating a parallel error framework.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • create delta is classified correctly;
  • remove delta is classified correctly;
  • modified delta is classified correctly;
  • no-op delta is rejected;
  • duplicate entity deltas are rejected;
  • migration preserves exact base/result snapshots;
  • generic operations round-trip through the chosen canonical representation if serialization exists;
  • domain-specific opaque operation does not require a domain dependency;
  • provenance supports each universal source category;
  • ordering is deterministic where required.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Never mutate a snapshot or revision.
  • Do not infer history from timestamps.
  • Do not add concrete backend code.
  • Do not add domain-specific operation variants.
  • Do not conflate diff with migration.
  • Do not treat formatting-only changes as semantic migrations.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Entity deltas are universal and validated.
  • [ ] Migration records exact base/result snapshots.
  • [ ] Generic operation vocabulary exists.
  • [ ] Domain-specific intent can be carried opaquely.
  • [ ] Provenance/source categories exist.
  • [ ] No domain/backend dependencies were added.
  • [ ] Determinism tests pass.
  • [ ] All focused tests pass.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the public types added, invariants enforced, tests added, and any generic identifier/value type that had to be introduced. Explicitly call out any unresolved dependency on sr-core or sr-store.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the TypeScript public protocol package in web/packages/protocol without inventing browser-only semantics.

This package is the stable TypeScript boundary for concepts exposed by the shared Scriberig protocol.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  4. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md

Prerequisite: the web workspace scaffold from Level 3 task 001 exists.

If a canonical runtime protocol schema already exists in the repository, use it as the authority. Do not create incompatible parallel definitions.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/protocol/src/ids.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/objects.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/query.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/changes.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/operations.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/sessions.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/projections.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/capabilities.ts
web/packages/protocol/src/errors.ts
web/packages/protocol/test/protocol-types.test.ts

Update:

web/packages/protocol/src/index.ts
web/packages/protocol/package.json

docs.title: Identity Types
docs.text:
Expose serializable protocol identities for at least:

EntityId
RevisionId
SnapshotId
MigrationId
OperationId
ProjectionId
SessionId or session entity reference if the canonical protocol models sessions as entities
BranchId or branch entity reference if applicable
TypeId
RelationTypeId

Use the representation prescribed by the canonical shared protocol.

If no encoded representation has yet been standardized, use opaque TypeScript aliases over string and do not attach parsing semantics beyond basic type separation.

Do not expose database row IDs.

docs.title: Object and Relation Shapes
docs.text:
Expose public shapes needed by the web layers for concepts supported by the design, including equivalents of:

EntityRef
RevisionRef
SnapshotRef
ObjectSummary
ObjectDescription
RelationSummary
CollectionPage
ProvenanceSummary

Keep summary forms separate from full-content forms where the protocol supports progressive disclosure.

Do not add fields only because they are convenient for one component.

docs.title: Query Types
docs.text:
Represent the shared query/operation vocabulary needed for:

inspect
list/follow relations
find/search
query/filter
history
diff

If the canonical runtime protocol already provides a query AST, mirror or generate that exact shape.

Do not design a second browser-specific query language.

docs.title: Change and Validation Types
docs.text:
Expose protocol shapes for:

MigrationSummary
MigrationDetail
MigrationProposal
SemanticDiff
ValidationResult
Conflict
StaleBase or equivalent stale-state condition

Keep accepted canonical state distinct from proposed/candidate state.

docs.title: Operation and Event Types
docs.text:
Expose the long-running operation lifecycle:

queued
running
completed
failed
cancelled

Represent events needed by the Level 1 design, including equivalents of:

snapshot advanced
entity changed
projection changed
branch/session changed
migration completed
validation completed
operation progress
agent output
operation failed
operation cancelled
connection/resume metadata where protocol supports it

Use discriminated unions so consumers can handle event types exhaustively.

docs.title: Session and Branch Types
docs.text:
Expose public session concepts required for navigation rather than a chat-only model.

At minimum support representations for:

  • session summary;
  • branch summary;
  • branch description/purpose/outcome when present;
  • goals;
  • decisions;
  • tasks;
  • tool/result references;
  • resulting migration/object references.

Reuse universal entity/revision references when the server models these as normal knowledge entities.

docs.title: Projection and Capability Types
docs.text:
Expose projection metadata sufficient for a web client to understand:

  • projection identity;
  • semantic source identity;
  • style or rendering identity where public;
  • snapshot/base state;
  • editable/read-only capability;
  • semantic location mappings when supported.

Expose capability descriptors used to determine available operations without hard-coding official-frontend privileges.

docs.title: Structured Errors
docs.text:
Define typed structured error shapes for conditions the UI must represent explicitly, such as:

  • authorization/capability denied;
  • not found;
  • stale snapshot/base;
  • migration conflict;
  • reconciliation ambiguity;
  • validation failure;
  • operation failure;
  • unsupported capability;
  • protocol incompatibility.

Do not collapse these into plain message strings.

docs.title: Public Exports
docs.text:
src/index.ts must export only supported public protocol types and helpers.

Avoid default exports.

Do not export generated/private implementation details if code generation is used.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add compile/runtime-light tests that verify:

  • discriminated unions narrow correctly;
  • representative protocol fixtures are assignable to exported shapes;
  • IDs remain opaque at API boundaries;
  • public exports do not require React, DOM, or MUI types.

If canonical JSON fixtures exist from the server protocol, use them directly.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
From web/ run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/protocol typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/protocol test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/protocol build

Also run the workspace typecheck to catch downstream breakage:

pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add HTTP behavior.
  • Do not add React types or hooks.
  • Do not add MUI.
  • Do not add browser caches.
  • Do not create UI-specific fields in protocol models.
  • Do not invent endpoint paths.
  • Do not mirror database tables directly.
  • Do not redefine canonical Rust/runtime protocol semantics when an authoritative schema already exists.
  • Do not add application layout state.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All prescribed protocol source modules exist.
  • [ ] IDs and references are opaque public values rather than database details.
  • [ ] Query/change/operation/session/projection concepts are represented.
  • [ ] Events use exhaustive discriminated unions.
  • [ ] Structured errors preserve stale/conflict/validation distinctions.
  • [ ] The package has no React or MUI dependency.
  • [ ] The package aligns with the canonical protocol source.
  • [ ] Protocol tests pass.
  • [ ] Workspace typecheck remains green.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the universal schema layer that lets domain crates define strongly typed semantic concepts without changing the storage architecture.

This task owns schema definitions and schema-level validation contracts only.

It must reuse the already-established shared core crate and must not create a second workspace, core, store, or graph implementation.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  3. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md
  4. the repository-wide workspace/package-layout design.

Inspect the actual workspace before editing.

Use the universal schema crate already established by the workspace if it exists. If it does not exist yet, create the crate at the canonical workspace path prescribed by the repository-wide layout rather than inventing an alternative prefix.

Do not create concrete Markdown, Rust, PDF, or session schemas in this task.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical universal schema crate:

Cargo.toml
src/lib.rs
src/entity.rs
src/property.rs
src/relation.rs
src/collection.rs
src/validation.rs

If these files already exist as skeletons, fill them in instead of duplicating modules.

The schema crate must depend on the shared core crate only for universal IDs/values/provenance needed by the schema model.

It must not depend on the universal graph crate, because graph records need to be able to implement schema validation without creating a dependency cycle.

docs.title: 1. Property Value Shapes
docs.text:
In property.rs, define a public ValueShape or equivalent type describing the accepted shape of the shared KnowledgeValue type.

Support at least:

Any
Null
Bool
SignedInteger
UnsignedInteger
Float
String
Bytes
List
Record

Recursive list/record shape constraints are desirable if they remain simple and deterministic.

Do not turn this into a general-purpose type language.

Define PropertySchema with at least:

key
name
description              optional
value_shape
required                  bool or equivalent
knowledge_class           Canonical / Derived

If the project already has a common cardinality/requiredness type, reuse it.

docs.title: 2. Cardinality
docs.text:
Define one reusable cardinality representation for relation and collection schemas.

It must express common cases:

zero or one
exactly one
zero or more
one or more
bounded min/max

A compact representation such as min plus optional max is acceptable if invariants are validated at construction time.

Do not encode cardinality only as documentation text.

docs.title: 3. Relation Schemas
docs.text:
In relation.rs, define RelationSchema or equivalent.

Required semantic fields:

relation type ID
human-readable name
optional description
permitted source entity types
permitted target entity types
knowledge class
cardinality
reverse-navigation expectation

The reverse-navigation setting should indicate whether reverse lookup is expected to be derived/index-backed.

Do not require reverse relations to be duplicated in canonical child state.

Use semantic entity-type IDs, not Rust TypeId, filenames, or module names unless an existing core type intentionally represents schema type identity.

docs.title: 4. Collection Schemas
docs.text:
In collection.rs, define CollectionSchema or equivalent.

Required semantic fields:

collection type ID
human-readable name
optional description
owner entity type
permitted member entity types
order semantics
cardinality
knowledge class

Represent order semantics explicitly, for example:

Ordered
Unordered

Do not collapse collections into generic relations: order/membership semantics are part of the Level 1 model.

docs.title: 5. Entity-Type and Domain Schemas
docs.text:
In entity.rs, define an EntityTypeSchema containing:

entity type ID
human-readable name
optional description
property definitions/references
relation definitions/references
collection definitions/references

Also define a top-level Schema/DomainSchema containing:

schema ID
schema version
human-readable name
optional description
registered entity types
relation definitions
collection definitions

Use deterministic map/set containers where practical.

The schema version can initially be a small explicit value/string. Do not design schema migrations in this task.

No production domain type may be hard-coded into these enums/structs.

docs.title: 6. Validation Subject Trait
docs.text:
In validation.rs, define a small trait such as ValidationSubject that exposes graph-shaped data using only shared core types.

It should allow schema validation to inspect, conceptually:

entity type
properties and values
relations and target entity IDs
collections and member entity IDs

If target/member entity types are needed, define a separate lightweight validation context/resolver trait that can answer:

entity ID -> entity type, within a caller-provided context

The schema crate must not depend on the graph or store crates.

Later the universal graph RevisionRecord will implement ValidationSubject.

docs.title: 7. Structured Validation Results
docs.text:
Define public equivalents of:

ValidationSeverity
ValidationLocation
ValidationIssue
ValidationReport

A validation issue must include:

severity
stable machine-readable code
human-readable message
optional semantic location

Semantic location must be able to identify at least:

whole subject/entity
property key
relation type
collection type

Do not make file path or line number mandatory for validation locations.

A ValidationReport must expose a direct has_errors()-style API so callers never need to parse message text.

docs.title: 8. Required Validation Behavior
docs.text:
Implement deterministic schema-level validation for at least:

  1. entity type is declared;
  2. required properties are present;
  3. property values match declared value shape;
  4. unknown properties are handled by one documented deterministic policy;
  5. relation types are valid for the source entity type;
  6. relation cardinality is valid;
  7. relation target types are valid when target-type context is available;
  8. collection type is valid for the owner;
  9. collection cardinality is valid;
  10. collection member types are valid when member-type context is available.

Ordinary invalid data must produce ValidationReport issues, not panics.

Use Rust errors only when validation cannot be performed because the schema/context itself is unusable.

docs.title: 9. Public Exports
docs.text:
lib.rs should expose the primary schema and validation types without forcing downstream crates through deep private paths.

Keep helper functions private unless they are genuinely part of the domain-adapter API.

The public API should make a clear distinction between:

schema definitions
runtime graph data
validation results

The schema crate should contain only the first and third categories.

docs.title: 10. Unit Tests
docs.text:
Add focused tests for:

  • required vs optional properties;
  • each relevant value-shape match/mismatch;
  • relation source/target restrictions;
  • relation cardinality;
  • ordered/unordered collection schema metadata;
  • collection cardinality;
  • structured validation locations;
  • stable machine-readable issue codes;
  • has_errors() behavior;
  • a custom test-only entity vocabulary proving production domains are not hard-coded.

Use test-local IDs such as test.document, test.section, and test.paragraph only inside test code.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Document these invariants:

  • schemas add domain meaning; they do not store project instances;
  • universal schemas remain domain-independent;
  • relations and collections are typed explicitly;
  • reverse navigation can be derived rather than canonically duplicated;
  • ordered and unordered collection semantics differ;
  • validation issues are semantic and machine-readable;
  • parser/compiler/product validity belongs to higher layers.

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If available:

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • create a new core crate;
  • depend on the graph crate;
  • add database access;
  • add parser/compiler validation;
  • add migrations;
  • add queries/search;
  • add concrete Markdown/Rust/PDF/session schemas;
  • store actual project entities inside schemas;
  • require canonical reverse edges;
  • add agent/UI/server behavior.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] canonical schema crate was reused/created at the workspace-prescribed location;
  • [ ] property schemas and value shapes exist;
  • [ ] cardinality is explicit;
  • [ ] relation endpoint constraints exist;
  • [ ] collection order semantics are explicit;
  • [ ] domain schema container exists;
  • [ ] validation-subject/context traits avoid a graph dependency cycle;
  • [ ] validation issues are structured and machine-readable;
  • [ ] schema-level validation covers required structural cases;
  • [ ] no production domain schema is hard-coded;
  • [ ] workspace checks and tests pass.

docs.title: Scaffold Rust Application and Product Layers
Objective
docs.text:
Extend the Rust workspace created by 001. initialize rust foundation workspace.md with the application, transport, agent, native UI, CLI, and final executable crates prescribed by design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md.

This task creates dependency boundaries only. Do not implement application operations, wire payloads, HTTP endpoints, agent tools, TUI screens, or CLI commands beyond the minimum required for the workspace to compile.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/001. vision and principles.md
  2. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  3. design/level-3/001. initialize rust foundation workspace.md

The important architectural rules are:

  • product surfaces consume shared application capabilities;
  • the server is an adapter, not the owner of semantics;
  • agents are consumers of the same application capabilities;
  • foundation crates must never depend on these higher layers;
  • the final executable contains composition, not business logic.

docs.text:
Create:

crates/scriberig-app/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-client/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-client/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-core/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-agent-core/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-agent-runtime/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-server/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-server/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-tui/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-tui/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-cli/Cargo.toml
crates/scriberig-cli/src/lib.rs
apps/scriberig/Cargo.toml
apps/scriberig/src/main.rs

Also update the root Cargo.toml workspace member list to include all of these packages.

Do not remove or rename foundation members created by Level 3 task 001.

docs.title: Package Names
docs.text:
Use these package names exactly:

scriberig-app
scriberig-protocol
scriberig-client
scriberig-agent-core
scriberig-agent-runtime
scriberig-server
scriberig-tui
scriberig-cli
scriberig

apps/scriberig is the package named scriberig and contains the product executable.

Use the workspace version and edition already defined in the root workspace.

docs.title: Internal Dependency Direction
docs.text:
Declare only the internal dependencies needed to represent this architecture:

scriberig-app
├── scriberig-core
├── scriberig-graph
├── scriberig-query
├── scriberig-migration
├── scriberig-projection
└── scriberig-session

scriberig-protocol
└── scriberig-core

scriberig-client
└── scriberig-protocol

scriberig-agent-core
├── scriberig-app
└── scriberig-session

scriberig-agent-runtime
└── scriberig-agent-core

scriberig-server
├── scriberig-app
└── scriberig-protocol

scriberig-tui
└── scriberig-app

scriberig-cli
├── scriberig-app
├── scriberig-server
├── scriberig-tui
└── scriberig-agent-runtime

scriberig executable
└── scriberig-cli

Use relative path dependencies.

Do not add a dependency from scriberig-app to scriberig-protocol.

Do not add a dependency from any foundation crate to any crate created in this task.

Do not add a dependency from scriberig-protocol to the server or application implementation.

docs.title: Source File Content
docs.text:
Every library src/lib.rs should contain crate-level documentation only.

Document the role accurately:

  • scriberig-app: shared application-operation boundary used by all surfaces;
  • scriberig-protocol: serializable external transport contract boundary;
  • scriberig-client: reusable Rust client boundary for a remote server;
  • scriberig-agent-core: reusable agent-facing abstractions over application/session capabilities;
  • scriberig-agent-runtime: integrated agent execution/orchestration boundary;
  • scriberig-server: remote adapter over scriberig-app plus scriberig-protocol;
  • scriberig-tui: terminal UI adapter over application capabilities;
  • scriberig-cli: command parsing/dispatch boundary for the product executable.

Do not create speculative public functions, DTOs, command enums, HTTP server setup, model provider abstractions, or terminal components.

docs.title: Product main.rs
docs.text:
apps/scriberig/src/main.rs must remain minimal.

It may contain an empty main function and a short comment saying product composition will be added by later designs.

Do not invent CLI flags or runtime modes in this task.

The scriberig package should depend on scriberig-cli so the intended composition edge exists in the manifest even if no runtime invocation is implemented yet.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

All must succeed after extending the workspace.

Inspect the dependency graph and verify manually that:

  • scriberig-core has no Scriberig dependency;
  • no foundation crate depends on an agent/product crate;
  • scriberig-server depends on scriberig-app, not vice versa;
  • the product executable sits at the top of the dependency graph.

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement HTTP or WebSocket endpoints.
  • Do not choose a web server framework.
  • Do not define the transport schema.
  • Do not implement a remote client.
  • Do not create actual agent tools.
  • Do not integrate an LLM provider.
  • Do not implement TUI widgets.
  • Do not invent CLI syntax.
  • Do not add domain adapters.
  • Do not move business logic into scriberig-server, scriberig-cli, scriberig-tui, or the binary.
  • Do not edit Level 1 or Level 2 design documents.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Root workspace contains every foundation and product Rust member prescribed by Level 2.
  • [ ] All new package names match this document.
  • [ ] Dependency direction matches the prescribed graph.
  • [ ] Every library contains only accurate crate-level documentation.
  • [ ] apps/scriberig/src/main.rs is minimal.
  • [ ] No product behavior was invented.
  • [ ] No lower layer depends on a higher layer.
  • [ ] cargo fmt --all -- --check succeeds.
  • [ ] cargo check --workspace succeeds.
  • [ ] cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings succeeds.

docs.title: Implement Derived Selection, Freshness, Failure, and Retention Policies
Objective
docs.text:
Implement policy types for choosing among immutable derived results and deciding whether a result is fresh enough or retained long enough to satisfy a request.

This task must keep four concerns separate:

identity
selection
freshness
retention

A result's immutable identity must never change because it becomes preferred, stale for a current-information request, or eligible for eviction.

Do not implement reverse-dependency invalidation, protocol events, domain registration, background scheduling, agents, or a durable backend in this task.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/008. derived knowledge caching and incrementality.md
  2. design/level-2/001. derived knowledge runtime and cache design.md
  3. Level 3 tasks 001 and 002 from this derived-knowledge sequence.

Inspect the actual derivation crate and reuse all types already created there.

Do not rename or duplicate the profile, key, result, or repository abstractions merely because this task would prefer another representation.

docs.title: Files to Create or Modify
docs.text:
Inside the canonical derivation crate:

src/selection.rs
src/freshness.rs
src/retention.rs
src/result.rs      # only for narrowly required status/failure extensions
src/lib.rs

Do not create backend-specific files.

docs.title: 1. Selection Is Not Identity
docs.text:
In selection.rs, define policy/request types for choosing among already stored immutable result records.

Exact lookup by DerivationKey remains the strongest path and is not replaced by selection.

Selection should support policy dimensions conceptually equivalent to:

exact profile required
preferred profile
successful results only
fresh results only
newest compatible result
cheapest compatible result when cost metadata exists
trusted/allowed producer filter when caller supplies one

Do not hard-code one global selection policy.

A caller should be able to request a specific policy.

Selection must return the chosen exact result handle/record plus enough structured reason metadata to explain the choice later.

Do not mutate old results to mark one as current.

docs.title: 2. Preferred Result Metadata
docs.text:
The architecture allows convenience pointers such as:

preferred_summary(F@R7) -> Summary S3

If this task introduces preferred-result metadata, represent it as derived selection state outside canonical snapshots.

Changing a preferred pointer must not:

  • change a canonical SnapshotId;
  • rewrite the immutable result record;
  • delete older results;
  • change the DerivationKey.

If the existing repository contract does not yet have a place to persist preferred metadata, define the policy/value type now and leave persistence to a later backend integration.

Do not distort the repository trait simply to force persistence into this task.

docs.title: 3. Freshness Model
docs.text:
In freshness.rs, define a domain-neutral freshness model.

The model must distinguish local immutable derivations from external/time-varying observations.

Local exact-state results should normally support:

Freshness::Immutable

or an equivalent concept meaning that passage of time alone does not make them invalid.

External observations should be able to record conceptually:

source identity
observed_at
optional valid_until / max_age policy
optional source revision / validator token
optional revalidation metadata

Use the repository's established time type if one exists. Do not introduce a second timestamp library without need.

The API must be able to answer:

Fresh
Stale
RequiresRevalidation
NotApplicable

or equivalent structured outcomes.

Do not encode freshness only as a boolean if the policy needs to explain why revalidation is required.

docs.title: 4. Historical Truth vs Current Suitability
docs.text:
A stale external observation is still an exact historical artifact.

Tests and API docs must preserve this distinction:

observed at T1: value X

can remain permanently true as an observation even when:

X is the current value

can no longer be asserted.

Therefore freshness evaluation must not delete or mutate the historical record.

It only decides whether that record satisfies a request with a freshness requirement.

docs.title: 5. Failure Policy
docs.text:
Extend result/failure policy only as needed to classify reuse/retry behavior.

At minimum support clear policy for:

deterministic failure for immutable inputs
transient/retryable failure
cancelled/incomplete work

Examples:

  • parser rejects immutable invalid syntax -> deterministic and cacheable;
  • network timeout -> transient and normally retryable;
  • model request cancelled -> incomplete, not a successful reusable result.

Do not infer these categories from error-message text.

Selection policy must be able to exclude failures unless a caller explicitly asks to inspect them.

docs.title: 6. Retention Policy
docs.text:
In retention.rs, define retention categories equivalent to:

Disposable
ReusableExpensive
HistoricalEvidence
Pinned

Names may differ if repository conventions suggest better terminology.

Retention answers:

Should this artifact be kept when storage pressure or garbage collection policy runs?

It does not answer:

Is this result still valid for a derivation request?

Keep these concepts separate in types and documentation.

docs.title: Reference strength
docs.text:
Represent whether a retained derived artifact should preserve its canonical inputs strongly enough for historical interpretation.

At minimum distinguish:

WeakDependency
StrongPinnedDependency

or an equivalent mechanism.

Disposable cache dependencies must not automatically pin canonical history forever.

Pinned historical evidence may intentionally preserve required inputs.

Do not implement canonical garbage collection in this task.

docs.title: 7. Selection Evaluation
docs.text:
Implement a pure selection function or service that can evaluate a collection of immutable candidate records against a SelectionPolicy.

The function should:

  1. filter incompatible profiles;
  2. filter unusable status categories;
  3. evaluate freshness when requested;
  4. apply explicit producer/trust filter supplied by caller, if present;
  5. rank remaining candidates according to requested preference;
  6. return the exact selected result plus a structured reason;
  7. return a structured no-match reason when nothing qualifies.

Do not query network sources or run derivations here.

Selection evaluates existing candidates only.

docs.title: 8. Public API
docs.text:
Expose equivalents of:

SelectionPolicy
SelectionOutcome
SelectionReason
FreshnessPolicy
FreshnessState
RetentionPolicy
RetentionStrength

Reuse the existing result status/failure types rather than duplicating them.

Public docs must state that none of these operations modify canonical snapshots.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for at least:

  1. exact-profile selection;
  2. preferred-profile selection among two immutable results;
  3. newest-result selection without mutating older results;
  4. failed result excluded from normal success selection;
  5. deterministic failure remains inspectable;
  6. transient failure remains retryable by policy;
  7. immutable local result never expires only because time passes;
  8. external observation is fresh before its policy deadline;
  9. same observation is stale after the deadline but remains historically retrievable;
  10. revalidation-required outcome is representable;
  11. disposable retention is distinct from validity;
  12. pinned retention is representable;
  13. weak cache dependency does not imply canonical-history retention;
  14. changing preferred selection does not call or modify canonical snapshot APIs.

Tests must use test-domain profile names only.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

Run clippy if already standard for the repository.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
Do not:

  • add network clients;
  • fetch external data;
  • implement garbage collection;
  • implement invalidation;
  • mutate result identity when freshness changes;
  • add global mutable current result state;
  • advance canonical snapshots;
  • add agent/server/UI dependencies;
  • hard-code domain-specific selection rules.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] selection policy is separate from exact lookup identity;
  • [ ] multiple historical results remain immutable;
  • [ ] freshness distinguishes immutable local state from external observations;
  • [ ] stale observations remain historical artifacts;
  • [ ] deterministic and transient failures are distinguishable;
  • [ ] retention is separate from validity;
  • [ ] weak and strong retention semantics are representable;
  • [ ] structured selection/no-match reasons exist;
  • [ ] tests cover preference, freshness, failure, and retention;
  • [ ] no canonical snapshot mutation is introduced.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/client as the framework-independent client for shared Scriberig application operations and events.

The package must be usable from browser code, Node-based tooling, tests, and non-React applications.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  4. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  5. design/level-3/002. implement protocol package boundary.md

Prerequisite: @scriberig/protocol compiles and exposes the authoritative public protocol shapes.

Do not guess server endpoint paths if the server protocol has not defined them. In that case implement the transport abstraction and client operation mapping first, and keep HTTP endpoint mapping isolated behind the transport implementation.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/client/src/client.ts
web/packages/client/src/transport.ts
web/packages/client/src/http-transport.ts
web/packages/client/src/event-stream.ts
web/packages/client/src/errors.ts
web/packages/client/test/client.test.ts
web/packages/client/test/fake-transport.ts

Update:

web/packages/client/src/index.ts
web/packages/client/package.json

docs.title: Transport Abstraction
docs.text:
Define a small transport contract that supports:

  • typed request/response operations;
  • cancellation through AbortSignal or equivalent;
  • transport-level failures separate from semantic protocol errors;
  • event subscription or a companion event transport;
  • authentication metadata injection without coupling the client to one auth system.

The transport contract must not expose React concepts.

Tests must be able to provide an in-memory fake transport.

docs.title: Public Client
docs.text:
Implement one public client class or factory that maps shared application capabilities to typed methods.

Required conceptual method groups:

inspect
list/follow
query/search
diff/history
branch/change/migration
validate
render/projection
session/branch operations
agent operations
operation inspection/cancellation
event subscription
capability discovery

Use protocol types for inputs and outputs.

Do not duplicate protocol interfaces inside the client package.

Do not return raw Response objects from public semantic methods.

docs.title: HTTP Transport
docs.text:
http-transport.ts owns HTTP-specific behavior only.

It should handle concerns such as:

  • base URL;
  • request headers;
  • authentication header callback/provider;
  • JSON encoding/decoding;
  • abort/cancellation;
  • structured protocol error decoding;
  • network/HTTP error normalization.

Endpoint paths and HTTP verbs must follow the canonical server protocol if present.

If that contract is not yet implemented, centralize provisional endpoint mapping in one private table or function and mark it as blocked on the server protocol design. Do not scatter guessed URLs throughout client methods.

docs.title: Event Stream
docs.text:
Implement an event subscription abstraction in event-stream.ts.

Requirements:

  • expose typed protocol events;
  • expose connected/disconnected/resuming state when available;
  • allow consumers to unsubscribe/close;
  • support cancellation;
  • isolate WebSocket/SSE details from semantic consumers;
  • preserve resume/cursor metadata if the server protocol provides it.

Do not build a React hook here.

Do not automatically mutate semantic caches; that belongs to @scriberig/model.

docs.title: Error Model
docs.text:
Separate at least:

TransportError
ProtocolError
Structured server/application error

Protocol/application errors from @scriberig/protocol should remain inspectable by callers.

Do not turn stale-base, conflict, capability-denied, or validation errors into generic Error("request failed") values.

docs.title: Fake Transport Tests
docs.text:
The tests must verify that client methods:

  • send the expected operation and payload through the transport abstraction;
  • return typed protocol results;
  • propagate structured application errors;
  • pass cancellation signals;
  • do not require DOM or React globals for non-browser tests.

Also test event subscription wiring with a fake event source.

docs.title: Public Exports
docs.text:
Export from src/index.ts:

  • the public client;
  • transport interfaces needed by alternate implementations;
  • HTTP transport;
  • event subscription interfaces;
  • client/transport error classes that callers must distinguish.

Do not export private endpoint tables or internal codecs unless they are intentionally part of the compatibility contract.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
From web/ run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/client typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/client test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/client build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add React.
  • Do not add MUI.
  • Do not add entity/revision caches.
  • Do not add selection state.
  • Do not add route or component logic.
  • Do not implement optimistic editing.
  • Do not bypass public protocol types with unknown/any to make calls compile.
  • Do not access SQLite or filesystem state.
  • Do not hide semantic errors behind transport-only errors.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] A framework-independent transport abstraction exists.
  • [ ] A typed public Scriberig client exists.
  • [ ] HTTP-specific logic is isolated.
  • [ ] Event subscription is isolated and typed.
  • [ ] Structured errors survive client boundaries.
  • [ ] Cancellation is supported.
  • [ ] Tests use a fake transport rather than a real server.
  • [ ] No React or MUI dependency exists.
  • [ ] Client tests and workspace typecheck pass.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement History Topology and Lineage
Goal
docs.text:
Implement explicit change-history topology for sr-change so history is represented as a DAG of immutable snapshots and migrations rather than inferred from write order.

This task does not implement branch promotion, merge algorithms, or domain-specific history views.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 3, 12, 13, 28, 33, 34, 40, 41, 42, and 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. The completed migration/provenance implementation from Level 3 task 002.
  4. sr-store ancestry/history capabilities.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
Primary files:

crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/migration.rs
crates/sr-change/src/query.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs

Tests may be placed beside the code or in crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs following repository convention.

docs.title: Required concepts
docs.text:
Implement explicit representations for:

  • a committed migration reference;
  • migration parent relationships;
  • base and result snapshot relationships;
  • merge history with more than one parent line;
  • lineage of an entity revision through migrations;
  • semantic replacement lineage such as replaces, split_into, merged_from, supersedes, or extracted_from when represented by higher layers.

Do not encode topology using timestamps or integer insertion order.

docs.title: History access abstraction
docs.text:
If migration persistence is not already part of sr-store, define a backend-independent read abstraction in sr-change for history records.

It must be possible for query/merge code to request:

migration by id/reference
migrations producing a snapshot
migrations touching an entity
parents of a historical transition
children/descendants where the implementation can provide them

Do not add SQL or concrete memory-store internals to sr-change.

If durable persistence of migration objects requires a new generic storage capability, add the smallest backend-independent trait extension and conformance requirements. Do not bypass sr-store.

docs.title: Snapshot ancestry
docs.text:
Implement reusable helpers for ancestry operations required later by merge:

is_ancestor(candidate, descendant)
ancestors(snapshot)
common_ancestor(left, right)

Prefer storage-provided ancestry indexes when exposed, but keep correctness independent of optional acceleration indexes.

If multiple common ancestors are possible, document and implement the deterministic rule for choosing the merge base or return enough information for the merge layer to decide. Do not silently pick based on timestamp.

docs.title: Entity lineage
docs.text:
Provide a queryable lineage model for one EntityId across migrations.

It should expose facts such as:

revision before
revision after
migration that introduced the transition
snapshot where the new revision became visible
branch/workspace provenance if available

Do not treat moving an entity as creating unrelated identity when migration data says continuity is preserved.

docs.title: State equality versus history equality
docs.text:
Add helpers or documentation that preserve this distinction:

  • equal SnapshotId means equal canonical state;
  • equal snapshot state does not imply identical historical path.

Tests must include two histories that converge to the same snapshot state through different transitions.

docs.title: Creation and removal
docs.text:
History traversal must preserve the difference between:

entity absent in result snapshot

and:

physical revision destroyed

Never assume semantic removal makes old revisions unreadable.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • linear history S1 -> S2 -> S3;
  • sibling history S1 -> S2 and S1 -> S3;
  • merge topology with two parent lines;
  • common ancestor discovery;
  • history queries unaffected by insertion order;
  • entity lineage across multiple revision replacements;
  • semantic removal while old snapshot still resolves the old revision;
  • two distinct histories converging to the same current snapshot;
  • move/replacement lineage retaining semantic continuity when explicitly recorded.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• No timestamps as authoritative topology.
  • No backend-specific queries.
  • No textual file history assumptions.
  • No mutation of committed migration records.
  • Do not implement merge resolution in this task.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] History topology is explicit and DAG-capable.
  • [ ] Common ancestor logic exists.
  • [ ] Entity lineage is queryable.
  • [ ] Creation/removal semantics preserve historical readability.
  • [ ] State equality is not confused with history equality.
  • [ ] Tests do not rely on insertion order.
  • [ ] No backend-specific code is present.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: List the history abstractions added, how common ancestry is determined, what storage capability was required, and the tests proving DAG behavior.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Create the first sr-store crate and implement immutable canonical revision values plus an in-memory revision store.

This task proves content-addressed revision storage independently from snapshot logic.

Do not implement snapshots, roots, migrations, SQLite, or agents in this task.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/001. bootstrap workspace and identity types.md
design/level-3/002. implement canonical encoding and revision hashing.md

Assume Level 3 tasks 001 and 002 are complete.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify:

Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/revision.rs
crates/sr-store/src/revision_store.rs
crates/sr-store/tests/revisions.rs

The root workspace Cargo.toml may be modified only to add crates/sr-store as a workspace member if needed.

docs.title: Revision Value
docs.text:
Implement a public immutable Revision value containing exactly the canonical fields needed by this stage:

EncodingVersion
TypeId
canonical payload bytes
RevisionId

The RevisionId must be computed by sr-core revision hashing from:

revision domain tag
encoding version
type ID
payload

Do not accept an arbitrary caller-provided RevisionId in the normal constructor.

The constructor must compute the ID itself.

The revision must not contain:

  • [ ] EntityId;
  • [ ] parent identity;
  • [ ] child position;
  • [ ] mutable root name;
  • [ ] current snapshot;
  • [ ] cache data;
  • [ ] derived summary data;
  • [ ] incidental timestamps.

Expose read-only accessors.

docs.title: Revision Store Trait
docs.text:
Define a small backend-independent trait with behavior equivalent to:

put(revision) -> Result<RevisionId, StoreError>
get(id) -> Result<Option<Revision>, StoreError>
contains(id) -> Result<bool, StoreError>

The exact ownership form may use Arc<Revision> if useful, but do not expose internal map locks.

put must be idempotent.

Putting an already present exact revision returns the same RevisionId and does not create a logically distinct record.

docs.title: In-Memory Implementation
docs.text:
Implement MemoryRevisionStore using an internal map keyed by RevisionId.
