  • explicit transaction rollback leaves old root visible;
  • unsupported newer backend schema version fails with a typed error;
  • failure before root promotion does not expose attempted new root.

Where possible, run tests against temporary database files rather than only SQLite :memory:.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not expose a raw SQLite connection through the public sr-store interface.
  • Do not add agent/session/domain tables.
  • Do not rely on SQLite row order for canonical identity.
  • Do not mutate existing canonical revision rows.
  • Do not implement semantic merges.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] SQLite backend implements the existing revision/snapshot/root interfaces.
  • [ ] Fresh initialization and reopen work.
  • [ ] Named-root promotion is transactional and compare-and-set based.
  • [ ] Previous snapshots remain readable.
  • [ ] Backend schema versioning is explicit.
  • [ ] Crash/reopen semantics expose only committed roots.
  • [ ] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Scaffold Web UI Packages and Editor Shell
Objective
docs.text:
Extend the web workspace created by 003. initialize web workspace and headless packages.md with reusable UI packages and the integrated Scriberig editor shell prescribed by design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md.

This task creates package boundaries and a minimal application shell only. Do not implement semantic browsers, editors, agent panels, MUI widgets, routing, server communication, or application state behavior.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/001. vision and principles.md
  2. design/level-2/001. workspace and package layout.md
  3. design/level-3/003. initialize web workspace and headless packages.md

The important architectural rules are:

  • the integrated editor is a consumer of public packages;
  • low-level database/revision views and high-level semantic/agent views must eventually resolve through the same public model;
  • reusable components must not depend on the private integrated editor app;
  • MUI-specific code belongs only in the MUI package or integrated app;
  • product behavior must not bypass @scriberig/client, @scriberig/model, and the public editor abstractions.

Create:

web/packages/components/package.json
web/packages/components/src/index.ts
web/packages/components-mui/package.json
web/packages/components-mui/src/index.ts
web/packages/agent-ui/package.json
web/packages/agent-ui/src/index.ts

web/apps/editor/package.json
web/apps/editor/src/main.tsx

docs.title: Package Names and Roles

web/packages/components      -> @scriberig/components
web/packages/components-mui  -> @scriberig/components-mui
web/packages/agent-ui        -> @scriberig/agent-ui
web/apps/editor              -> @scriberig/editor-app

Use version 0.1.0 for the reusable packages.

Mark the integrated editor app private.

At this stage the reusable packages may also remain private to avoid accidental publication before release design exists.

@scriberig/components

@scriberig/components-mui

No public package may depend on @scriberig/editor-app.

docs.title: MUI Boundary
docs.text:
This task reserves the MUI-specific package boundary but does not need to install or implement MUI yet.

If MUI dependencies are added while performing this task, they are allowed only in:

web/packages/components-mui

They must not appear in:

@scriberig/protocol
@scriberig/client
@scriberig/model
@scriberig/editor-core
@scriberig/react

docs.title: Reusable Package Source Files

Each reusable package src/index.ts should contain only documentation comments and an empty module export.

Document the intended roles accurately:

  • @scriberig/components: reusable style-neutral or styleable Scriberig component boundary;
  • @scriberig/components-mui: opinionated MUI implementation over public editor/React primitives;
  • @scriberig/agent-ui: reusable UI primitives for sessions, branches, agent operations, and agent-scoped semantic selections.

docs.title: Integrated Editor main.tsx
docs.text:
Create a compileable placeholder module only.

It may contain a comment explaining that the integrated editor will compose public Scriberig packages and an empty export:

export {};

Do not create a private semantic model in the app.

Do not create a raw database API client in the app.

Do not add direct server fetches.

Do not add placeholder UI that would establish accidental product architecture before the editor design exists.

docs.title: Editor App Manifest
docs.text:
The editor app manifest must express dependencies on the public packages listed above using pnpm workspace references.

Do not add a production framework, router, state library, or build system unless a later design explicitly selects it.

This means the app may not yet have a runnable browser bundle. That is acceptable: this task establishes the dependency boundary, not the final web runtime.

pnpm install
pnpm list -r --depth -1

Verify that the three new packages and editor app are discovered.

Inspect package manifests and verify:

  • no package imports the editor app;
  • only the MUI package/editor may contain MUI dependencies;
  • the editor depends on reusable packages rather than private source paths;
  • workspace dependencies resolve without cycles.

Do not introduce a framework just to create a build command for this scaffold.

  • [ ] @scriberig/components-mui exists with the correct dependencies.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Complete the first universal knowledge model implementation with cross-crate conformance tests and public API documentation.

The tests must prove that the shared core, schema, and graph layers satisfy the semantic rules in design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md without relying on an agent runtime, UI, parser, or specific database backend.

This task should primarily add tests and documentation. Only make small implementation fixes needed to satisfy explicit invariants.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-2/001. universal knowledge model rust libraries.md
  3. design/level-3/001. extend shared core with knowledge values and provenance.md
  4. design/level-3/002. implement universal schema contracts.md
  5. design/level-3/003. implement universal graph semantic records.md
  6. the identity/revision/snapshot design used by the implemented workspace.

Inspect the actual crate names and APIs before writing tests. Reuse the canonical shared crates; do not create alternate versions of them.

docs.title: Primary Test File
docs.text:
Create or fill the universal graph crate's integration test:

tests/universal_model.rs

Use the path inside the canonical graph crate already registered in the workspace.

You may also improve public documentation in the shared core/schema/graph modules when the tests reveal unclear contracts.

docs.title: 1. Define a Test-Only Domain Schema
docs.text:
Inside the integration test, define a small schema using names such as:

Document
Section
Paragraph

These are test fixtures only.

Suggested test structure:

Document --sections--> Section       ordered collection
Section  --blocks----> Paragraph     ordered collection
Section  --related---> Section       typed relation
Paragraph.text                       required string property
Section.title                        optional string property

Use schema/type IDs created through the normal public API.

Do not add Document, Section, or Paragraph as variants or production structs in the universal crates.

docs.title: 2. Entity Continuity vs Exact Revision
docs.text:
Create one paragraph entity and represent two exact revisions for it.

The test must demonstrate:

same EntityId
+ different RevisionId
= same conceptual entity at different exact states

Use the identity/storage APIs already defined by prerequisite work.

Do not invent a second ID implementation in the test.

Assert that EntityId and RevisionId are distinct public types.

docs.title: 3. Snapshot-Bound Interpretation
docs.text:
Use the existing in-memory snapshot/store implementation if one exists; otherwise implement a tiny test double for the graph-view trait.

Create two snapshots:

S1: Paragraph P -> Revision R1
S2: Paragraph P -> Revision R2

Assert that resolving P in S1 and S2 returns the different expected revisions.

This test must fail if the graph API silently uses an implicit global current revision instead of the requested snapshot.

docs.title: 4. Ordered Collection Semantics
docs.text:
Construct an ordered collection containing:

[P1, P2, P3]

Assert order is preserved.

Construct another ordered collection:

[P2, P1, P3]

Assert the values differ.

The entities P1, P2, and P3 must keep the same identities in both collections.

This proves that position belongs to the parent collection rather than the child entity.

docs.title: 5. Unordered Collection Semantics
docs.text:
Construct two unordered collections containing the same members supplied in different input orders.

Assert they have identical semantic membership/equality according to the public API.

The test must show that callers cannot infer semantic order from insertion or storage order.

docs.title: 6. No Canonical Parent Requirement
docs.text:
Construct a paragraph revision containing only its own type/property state.

Construct a section revision whose collection contains the paragraph entity.

Assert that the paragraph revision does not require a parent ID or position.

If reverse navigation exists in the graph view, use a test/mock reverse index to find the parent and demonstrate that reverse lookup is a derived/view concern.

docs.title: 7. Typed Relation Validation
docs.text:
Using the test schema, validate:

Section A --related--> Section B

as valid.

Then validate an invalid target type such as:

Section A --related--> Paragraph P

Assert the invalid case produces a structured validation issue with a stable machine-readable code.

Do not determine validity by matching the human-readable message string.

docs.title: 8. Property Validation
docs.text:
Validate at least:

  1. a paragraph with required string text;
  2. a paragraph missing text;
  3. a paragraph with text set to the wrong value shape.

Assert:

  • the valid subject has no error-severity issues;
  • invalid subjects have error-severity issues;
  • issues contain semantic locations where practical;
  • validation does not panic for ordinary invalid input.

docs.title: 9. Provenance
docs.text:
Create provenance examples for:

user-authored knowledge
parser-produced knowledge
model-generated description

Assert source kinds remain distinguishable.

Create provenance with exact entity/revision dependencies and assert those dependencies can be inspected directly.

Do not add trust ranking assertions. Provenance records origin only.

docs.title: 10. Derived Description
docs.text:
Create a description for one exact paragraph revision.

It must contain:

exact entity/revision reference
description profile
text
provenance

Use model-generated provenance for this test.

Assert that the description remains a separate derived object and is not automatically inserted into the canonical revision record.

docs.title: 11. Derived Artifact Dependencies
docs.text:
Create a generic derived artifact with at least two exact immutable input dependencies.

Example concept:

Section S@R1 summary depends on:
  Section S@R1
  Paragraph P@R3

Assert that exact dependency revision IDs remain inspectable.

This proves the future incremental-cache contract: an unrelated global snapshot change need not invalidate a derived result whose declared inputs are unchanged.

Do not implement a cache in this task.

docs.title: 12. Cross-Domain Neutrality
docs.text:
Search the production universal crates before completing the task.

They must not hard-code production variants/types such as:

MarkdownSection
RustFunction
PdfPage
SessionBranch

Documentation may mention these as examples.

Runtime schemas/domain crates must supply those names later.

Add a test or compile-time usage pattern showing that test domain entity types are represented through schema IDs/definitions rather than universal enum variants.

docs.title: 13. Reverse Navigation Contract
docs.text:
If the graph-view API exposes reverse relation lookup, verify that:

  • forward canonical relation exists only in the owning source revision;
  • target revision does not need a duplicate reverse edge;
  • reverse lookup can still return the source through the view/index abstraction.

If reverse lookup is not yet implemented because it belongs to a later index design, test the type-level contract as far as currently possible and document the deferred behavior clearly.

Do not add backend-specific indexing solely for this test.

docs.title: 14. Public Documentation Review
docs.text:
Review public API docs across the three layers.

Ensure they clearly communicate:

EntityId   = conceptual continuity
RevisionId = exact immutable state
SnapshotId = exact consistent graph view

Also document:

  • property values are not a substitute for semantic relations;
  • relations are typed;
  • ordered/unordered collections differ semantically;
  • child entities do not own parent position;
  • canonical and derived knowledge differ;
  • descriptions/derived artifacts carry provenance and dependencies;
  • graph reads that depend on state are snapshot-bound;
  • universal libraries do not depend on the agent runtime.

Keep API docs concise; do not copy whole design documents into Rust comments.

docs.title: 15. Validation Commands
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace

If available:

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

If clippy reports pre-existing unrelated warnings, do not broadly rewrite unrelated code; report them separately.

docs.title: 16. Final Scope Audit
docs.text:
Before completing, verify this universal-model work did not accidentally add:

  • a second core/store crate;
  • a new identity/hash algorithm;
  • a second snapshot implementation;
  • SQLite-specific semantic APIs;
  • parser libraries;
  • renderers;
  • migrations;
  • agent runtime;
  • HTTP server/client behavior;
  • CLI/TUI behavior;
  • UI components;
  • hard-coded production domain schemas.

The result must remain a reusable semantic model layer.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] test-only domain schema works through universal schema APIs;
  • [ ] entity continuity vs revision exactness is demonstrated;
  • [ ] snapshot-bound resolution is demonstrated;
  • [ ] ordered collection behavior is tested;
  • [ ] unordered collection behavior is tested;
  • [ ] children need no canonical parent pointer;
  • [ ] typed relation endpoint validation is tested;
  • [ ] property shape/required validation is tested;
  • [ ] validation issues are machine-readable;
  • [ ] provenance source and dependencies are tested;
  • [ ] descriptions remain separate derived knowledge;
  • [ ] derived artifacts preserve exact dependencies;
  • [ ] production universal crates remain domain-neutral;
  • [ ] public docs state the key semantic contracts;
  • [ ] workspace checks and tests pass;
  • [ ] no deferred subsystem was introduced.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/editor-core as the framework-independent interaction layer for semantic selection, knowledge-tree navigation, commands, history, diffs, branches, migration review, and projection coordination.

This package contains behavior and state transitions only. It must not render JSX and must not depend on React or MUI.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/010. universal query and operation model.md
  2. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  4. design/level-3/004. implement client semantic model and incremental events.md

Prerequisite: @scriberig/model compiles and exposes framework-independent subscriptions/state access.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/editor-core/src/selection.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/commands.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/knowledge-tree.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/navigation.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/history.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/diff.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/branches.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/migration-review.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/projection-session.ts
web/packages/editor-core/src/extensions.ts
web/packages/editor-core/test/selection.test.ts
web/packages/editor-core/test/commands.test.ts
web/packages/editor-core/test/knowledge-tree.test.ts
web/packages/editor-core/test/navigation.test.ts

Update:

web/packages/editor-core/src/index.ts
web/packages/editor-core/package.json

docs.title: Universal Selection
docs.text:
Implement one semantic selection type/model capable of representing:

entity
optional exact revision
snapshot
optional relation/path context
optional projection location

Requirements:

  • support current-resolution selection and exact historical selection;
  • preserve snapshot identity;
  • allow projection views to attach location metadata without changing semantic identity;
  • support equality/comparison helpers based on semantic meaning;
  • avoid file-path/line-number assumptions in the core representation.

Selection is local interaction state, not canonical knowledge.

docs.title: Selection Controller
docs.text:
Implement a small controller/state object for active selection.

It must support:

  • get current selection;
  • set/clear selection;
  • subscribe/unsubscribe;
  • update projection/path context while retaining semantic entity where appropriate;
  • preserve historical exact revisions when current snapshot advances.

Do not couple selection to browser URL routing in this package.

docs.title: Command Model
docs.text:
Implement a command descriptor model with at least:

id
title
read-only or mutating classification
applicability predicate/capability requirements
execute descriptor or operation factory
optional keyboard/menu metadata
optional domain metadata

Commands must resolve to public application/client operations, not frontend-only database mutations.

Implement command discovery given:

  • current semantic selection;
  • server/client capability set;
  • registered domain extensions.

The same command descriptor must be usable later from palettes, menus, buttons, and agent-oriented action surfaces.

Do not embed JSX or MUI icons in the core descriptor. Use semantic icon keys/metadata if necessary.

docs.title: Knowledge Tree
docs.text:
Implement a headless expandable semantic tree controller.

It must support:

  • a root semantic reference;
  • lazy child loading by relation/collection;
  • expand/collapse;
  • loading/error state per node;
  • child counts or summary metadata where supplied;
  • stable semantic node handles;
  • selection integration;
  • pagination/cursor continuation for large child sets;
  • refreshing a loaded branch when current resolution changes.

It must not recursively load all descendants.

The controller should work for raw knowledge, domain trees, sessions, PDFs, and other relation-driven structures.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Implement reusable navigation state for semantic history such as:

back
forward
open selection
reveal related entity

Navigation entries must preserve enough snapshot/revision context to revisit exact historical state.

Do not assume URL routing or one fixed panel layout.

docs.title: History and Diff Controllers
docs.text:
Provide headless coordination models for:

  • loading entity/snapshot history;
  • selecting two comparable revisions/snapshots;
  • requesting semantic diff;
  • tracking raw/projection diff availability when provided;
  • navigating changed semantic entities.

Do not implement visual diff rendering here.

docs.title: Branch Navigation
docs.text:
Provide a controller/model for session/project branches that can:

  • list child branches lazily;
  • expose branch description/purpose/outcome;
  • select/open a branch;
  • resolve result references such as migrations or snapshots;
  • preserve branch semantic identity independently of chat transcript rendering.

docs.title: Migration Review
docs.text:
Implement local review state around a protocol migration proposal/detail.

It should support:

  • current proposal/base snapshot;
  • list of affected semantic objects;
  • selected change;
  • validation status reference;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • accept/apply command creation through the public client operation;
  • reject/close local review without mutating canonical state.

Do not directly apply database updates.

docs.title: Projection Session
docs.text:
Implement reusable state for coordinating a semantic object with a projection editor/view.

It should carry:

  • semantic selection;
  • projection identity;
  • snapshot/base state;
  • candidate/draft state when present;
  • semantic location mapping when available;
  • stale/conflict markers.

Do not implement Monaco, CodeMirror, PDF rendering, or Markdown editing in this task.

docs.title: Domain Extension Registry
docs.text:
Implement a minimal public extension registry supporting descriptors for:

  • inspectors;
  • projection handlers;
  • diff handlers;
  • relation views;
  • command providers;
  • labels/icons metadata;
  • validation presentation metadata.

The registry stores descriptors/handlers, not React components in the core package. React/component packages may interpret view keys or adapters later.

Keep the API small and typed.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests:

  1. one selection can retain entity identity while projection location changes;
  2. historical exact selection does not silently resolve to a newer revision;
  3. command discovery filters by capabilities and applicability;
  4. knowledge tree loads only expanded children;
  5. pagination adds children without losing stable node state;
  6. navigation back/forward preserves snapshot context;
  7. migration review exposes stale/conflict state without mutating canonical model;
  8. extension registration cannot overwrite an existing extension silently unless explicitly allowed.

Use fake model/client objects.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/editor-core typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/editor-core test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/editor-core build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add React.
  • Do not add JSX.
  • Do not add MUI.
  • Do not add routing.
  • Do not implement visual components.
  • Do not hard-code source-code-specific tree behavior.
  • Do not use line numbers as semantic identity.
  • Do not create private mutation paths.
  • Do not duplicate model caches.
  • Do not persist panel layout into canonical state.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Universal selection is implemented and snapshot-aware.
  • [ ] Command descriptors and discovery are implemented without visual dependencies.
  • [ ] Lazy semantic tree behavior is implemented.
  • [ ] Navigation preserves historical context.
  • [ ] History/diff controllers are headless.
  • [ ] Branch navigation is semantic rather than chat-only.
  • [ ] Migration review is local state over public migration operations.
  • [ ] Projection coordination is domain-neutral.
  • [ ] A minimal domain extension registry exists.
  • [ ] No React/MUI dependency exists.
  • [ ] Required tests pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the language-independent source-code vocabulary described by design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md in scriberig-domain-code.

This crate defines broad concepts that are genuinely shared across programming languages. It must not pretend that all languages have the same AST and must not absorb Rust-specific syntax.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/001. scaffold domain adapter crates.md
  4. current public APIs of scriberig-core, scriberig-schema, scriberig-graph, and scriberig-migration

If required shared schema APIs are not yet available, stop and report the prerequisite rather than implementing a private substitute.

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/code/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/types.rs
src/comment.rs
src/code_group.rs
src/classification.rs

Add tests under:

tests/schema.rs
tests/code_groups.rs

Do not add a parser in this crate. Language-specific adapters own parsing.

docs.title: Shared Code Vocabulary
docs.text:
Define broad entity concepts for:

CodeProject
Module
Type
Function
Parameter
CodeGroup
Statement
Expression
Comment
Symbol
Reference

These types exist only to support operations and navigation that genuinely overlap across languages.

Do not define Rust-specific constructs such as:

match arm
Rust pattern kinds
attribute syntax
macro invocation details
token trees
trait-specific syntax

Those belong to the Rust specialization.

docs.title: Core Structural Relations
docs.text:
Make the schema capable of representing at least:

CodeProject --contains--> Module
Module --contains--> Type/Function/other declarations
Function --parameters--> Parameter
Function --code_groups--> CodeGroup
CodeGroup --contains--> Statement
Statement/Expression --contains--> language-specific syntax children where specialized schemas allow it
Comment --attached_to--> semantic code entity
Reference --targets--> Symbol or semantic entity

Where order is meaningful, collections must preserve order.

Do not store reverse parents as canonical child properties solely for navigation.

docs.title: Canonical and Derived Boundaries
docs.text:
The shared code domain must distinguish broad canonical source structure from derived compiler analysis.

Canonical-capable concepts include:

author-chosen declarations
parameters
statement/expression structure
comments intentionally preserved
meaningful ordering
code groups when they reflect intentionally preserved source grouping

Derived concepts include by default:

resolved symbol targets
inferred types
call graph
control-flow graph
data-flow graph
compiler diagnostics
lint diagnostics
model-generated code-group descriptions

Do not mark compiler or model output canonical merely because it is stored in the same graph.

docs.title: Comment Model
docs.text:
Comments must be first-class where the language adapter preserves them.

Support a shared classification vocabulary at least broad enough for:

ordinary
documentation
explanation
invariant
safety
todo
directive
generated

Language adapters may extend or refine this classification.

A source-authored comment and a generated description must remain distinguishable.

docs.title: Code Groups
docs.text:
Define CodeGroup as an explicit semantic navigation layer between a function and its statements.

A code group must be able to carry or reference:

ordered statement membership
optional source-authored leading comment or grouping evidence
optional derived description/purpose
provenance/classification indicating which parts are canonical vs inferred

The shared domain must not require every function to have generated descriptions.

A function should remain inspectable even when code-group descriptions have not been produced.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
The schema must support this navigation shape:

Project
  -> Module
     -> Function/Type
        -> CodeGroup
           -> Statement
              -> Expression

The model must allow consumers to inspect counts, identifiers, names/signatures where available, and descriptions before loading fine-grained syntax.

Do not flatten a function body into one opaque text property.

docs.title: Semantic Handles
docs.text:
Every important code entity should be referenceable through normal universal entity handles.

The code domain must not use these as primary identity:

file path + line number
byte range
parser node pointer
compiler-internal transient ID

External coordinates may be attached as projection/adapter metadata.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
Expose the minimum stable domain API needed for:

register/obtain the code schema
refer to shared code type/relation identifiers
classify shared comment kinds
construct or inspect CodeGroup metadata through universal graph primitives

Do not invent a second graph API.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests proving:

  • every required shared code type is registered;
  • ordered parameters, groups, and statements are representable;
  • comments are separate semantic entities;
  • generated descriptions remain derived;
  • language-specific extension points can add specialized entity/relation types without modifying the shared store;
  • obvious invalid relation endpoints are rejected if supported by the shared schema layer;
  • no file coordinate is required for code identity.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-code
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-code --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not create a universal AST for every language.
  • Do not add Rust syntax here.
  • Do not choose a parser.
  • Do not implement compiler analysis.
  • Do not create source-file persistence tables.
  • Do not make generated descriptions canonical.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.
  • Do not store code only as raw source text.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Shared code vocabulary is implemented through the universal schema system.
  • [ ] Language-specific extension remains possible.
  • [ ] Code groups and comments are first-class semantic concepts.
  • [ ] Canonical vs derived boundaries are explicit.
  • [ ] Progressive disclosure is structurally supported.
  • [ ] No parser or language-specific syntax leaked into this crate.
  • [ ] No alternate persistence architecture exists.
  • [ ] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Implement mutable named roots that point to immutable SnapshotId values.

Named roots provide familiar moving names such as main while preserving the rule that snapshots themselves never change.

This task adds the only mutable coordination primitive required by the initial identity subsystem.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/004. implement persistent snapshots and diffs.md

Assume Level 3 tasks 001 through 004 are complete.

docs.title: Files You Own
docs.text:
Create or modify:

crates/sr-store/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-store/src/roots.rs
crates/sr-store/tests/roots.rs

Do not change the snapshot hashing or revision hashing rules in this task.

docs.title: Root Name
docs.text:
Define a small validated root-name type or an equivalent checked string wrapper.

Requirements:

  • [ ] non-empty;
  • [ ] deterministic textual representation;
  • [ ] no hidden normalization;
  • [ ] suitable for names such as main, active-workspace, and current-project;
  • [ ] validation failure uses a typed error.

Keep validation conservative and simple. Do not invent a complex path hierarchy in this task.

docs.title: Root Store Contract
docs.text:
Define a backend-independent public trait with behavior equivalent to:

get(name) -> Option<SnapshotId>
set(name, snapshot) -> Result<...>
compare_and_swap(name, expected, new) -> Result<CasOutcome, ...>

The exact signatures may return owned values or references as appropriate, but callers must not receive mutable access to internal storage.

docs.title: get
docs.text: Returns the exact snapshot currently referenced by the name, or None if the root does not exist.

docs.title: set
docs.text:
Unconditionally points the name at the supplied immutable snapshot ID.

This changes only the mutable root pointer. It does not change either snapshot.

docs.title: compare_and_swap
docs.text:
This is the concurrency-sensitive operation.

It succeeds only when the currently stored value equals expected.

Support both cases if practical:

expected = Some(snapshot)   # update an existing root only if still at this snapshot
expected = None             # create only if the root is currently absent

Return an explicit outcome containing enough information for a caller to distinguish success from stale expectation.

Do not silently retry inside the store.

docs.title: In-Memory Implementation
docs.text:
Create MemoryRootStore backed by an RwLock-protected map or an equivalent standard synchronization primitive.

The compare-and-swap check and update must happen while holding one exclusive critical section so another writer cannot change the root between them.

Do not expose the lock through the trait.

docs.title: Required Tests
docs.text:
In crates/sr-store/tests/roots.rs, test at least:

  • [ ] missing root returns None;
  • [ ] set creates a root;
  • [ ] set can move a root from S1 to S2;
  • [ ] moving a root does not change S1 or S2;
  • [ ] CAS succeeds when expected value matches;
  • [ ] CAS fails when expected value is stale;
  • [ ] failed CAS leaves the current root unchanged;
  • [ ] CAS with expected = None can create a missing root;
  • [ ] CAS with expected = None fails when root already exists;
  • [ ] two independent root names may point to the same snapshot;
  • [ ] one root moving does not affect another root.

Add one concurrency test using two threads if it can be written deterministically enough to avoid flaky timing assumptions. Prefer barriers/channels over sleeps.

The test should demonstrate that only one writer can successfully advance a root when both use the same old expected snapshot.

docs.title: Error and Outcome Types
docs.text:
Keep storage failures distinct from compare-and-swap conflicts.

A stale expectation is not an exceptional storage failure; it is a normal concurrency outcome.

A caller must be able to inspect the actual current snapshot after a failed CAS, either in the outcome or with a subsequent get.

docs.title: Public API Rule
docs.text:
Named roots are mutable aliases.

They must never be accepted where an exact SnapshotId is required without first resolving the name.

Do not create an API such as:

SnapshotId::from_root_name(...)

A name and a snapshot ID are fundamentally different concepts.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not mutate a Snapshot when moving a root.
  • Do not put root names into snapshot hashes.
  • Do not turn root names into snapshot identities.
  • Do not silently overwrite after a failed compare-and-swap.
  • Do not add SQLite or network coordination yet.
  • Do not add retry loops that hide conflicts from higher layers.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Root-name validation exists.
  • [ ] Backend-independent root-store trait exists.
  • [ ] In-memory implementation exists.
  • [ ] Compare-and-swap is atomic within the in-memory store.
  • [ ] Stale CAS is an explicit normal outcome.
  • [ ] Roots point to snapshots without mutating them.
  • [ ] Tests, formatting, and clippy all pass.

docs.title: Implement: Reachability, Garbage Collection, and Integrity
Objective
docs.text:
Implement storage maintenance features required by the Level 1 persistence model without changing canonical semantics.

This task adds backend-neutral reachability and integrity reporting plus SQLite garbage-collection support.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/005. indexes reachability gc and integrity.md
  3. Level 3 tasks 001 through 004.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
In sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── reachability.rs
└── integrity.rs

In sr-store-sqlite:

crates/sr-store-sqlite/src/
├── indexes.rs
├── reachability.rs
├── gc.rs
└── integrity.rs

Update lib.rs exports only as needed.

Add corresponding support to sr-store-memory if required by shared public traits/tests.

docs.title: Reachability API
docs.text:
Define backend-neutral types for:

  • protected roots;
  • reachable canonical object enumeration;
  • unreachable candidate reporting.

Reachability must begin from an explicit stable set of protected roots/snapshots.

Traversal must retain every immutable storage object required to read a protected snapshot completely, including snapshot-map structure, revisions, and persistent collection/storage nodes.

Do not automatically retain rebuildable caches merely because they mention a protected object.

docs.title: Integrity report
docs.text:
Define a structured IntegrityReport or equivalent with machine-readable issues.

At minimum detect/report:

  • revision ID does not match stored canonical content;
  • referenced persistent node missing;
  • invalid snapshot-map structure;
  • named root points to missing/invalid snapshot;
  • protected snapshot cannot be read completely;
  • persistent collection invariant violation;
  • derived/backend index points to missing authoritative data;
  • unreachable but otherwise valid immutable object.

Keep unreachable separate from corrupt.

docs.title: Index rebuild
docs.text:
Implement rebuilding of any backend-derived indexes introduced so far.

A rebuild must derive results from authoritative persisted data and must not modify canonical revision bytes or snapshot meaning.

docs.title: Garbage collection
docs.text:
Implement conservative mark-and-sweep for SQLite.

Required API behavior:

gc_dry_run(protected_roots) -> report
gc_sweep(protected_roots) -> report

Rules:

  • capture a stable protected-root set before marking;
  • dry run deletes nothing;
  • sweep deletes only objects proven unreachable under the captured root set and retention policy supported so far;
  • sweep must not make any protected snapshot unreadable;
  • when uncertain, retain rather than delete.

The first implementation does not need concurrent online GC. It may require exclusive/serialized maintenance access if documented internally.

docs.title: Integrity repair policy
docs.text:
Safe automatic repair is limited to rebuildable derived indexes.

Do not silently rewrite or synthesize canonical revisions to repair corruption.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create tests for:

  • reachability from one root marks all required canonical storage;
  • two protected roots preserve the union of their reachable state;
  • abandoned branch becomes a GC candidate only after no protected root reaches it;
  • dry run reports candidates and deletes nothing;
  • sweep removes an unreachable candidate;
  • sweep preserves all data required by protected snapshots;
  • altered stored canonical revision bytes are reported as corruption;
  • missing snapshot-map node is corruption;
  • unreachable valid record is not categorized as corrupt;
  • derived index can be deleted and rebuilt without changing canonical IDs.

After destructive GC tests, run integrity verification against every protected snapshot.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add retention policy UI or CLI.
  • Do not implement distributed GC.
  • Do not compact or rewrite canonical identities.
  • Do not automatically repair canonical corruption.
  • Do not make GC dependent on an agent runtime.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Reachability API exists.
  • [ ] Structured integrity report exists.
  • [ ] SQLite dry-run GC works.
  • [ ] SQLite sweep preserves protected snapshots.
  • [ ] Derived index rebuild works.
  • [ ] Corruption and unreachability are distinguished.
  • [ ] Memory and SQLite behavior remain consistent where public APIs overlap.
  • [ ] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Universal Semantic Diff
Goal
docs.text:
Implement backend-independent comparison of two exact snapshots.

A diff answers what differs between states. It must work whether the snapshots are directly related, distant ancestors, siblings, or historically unrelated but available in the same store.

Do not implement merge resolution in this task.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 10 through 13, 21, 23, 24, 29, 30, 42, 43, 44, and 48.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Existing sr-store snapshot enumeration/diff capabilities.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/diff.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Extend sr-store only if a generic efficient snapshot-mapping comparison capability is missing and cannot be implemented correctly through the existing public API.

docs.title: Universal diff result
docs.text:
Implement a result containing, at minimum:

left SnapshotId
right SnapshotId
entity deltas

Reuse the universal EntityDelta model rather than defining another incompatible changed-entity type.

The diff must classify:

introduced entities
removed entities
modified entities

Do not include unchanged entities in the main result.

docs.title: No ancestry requirement
docs.text:
The API must accept arbitrary snapshots.

Do not require one snapshot to be an ancestor of the other.

Add tests for:

S1 -> S2 -> S3: diff(S1, S3)

       S1
      /  \
    S2    S3: diff(S2, S3)

docs.title: Snapshot-level optimization
docs.text:
If left == right, return an empty diff immediately.

If storage provides a persistent-map structural diff, use it through the backend-independent interface.

Correctness must not depend on a specific Merkle/trie implementation.

docs.title: Relation and collection details
docs.text:
If generic relation/collection state is available through universal graph/storage APIs, define optional detail structures for:

relation added/removed
collection member inserted/removed
collection order changed

These details must be subordinate to the authoritative revision/entity delta.

Do not parse domain-specific payloads in the generic diff engine.

docs.title: Domain enrichment interface
docs.text:
Expose a narrow extension point that allows a domain crate to turn a universal diff into richer meaning.

The generic crate must remain useful without any domain adapter installed.

The extension point should receive exact entity/revision references and return additional interpretation without mutating the universal diff.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
Diff output must have deterministic ordering independent of backend iteration order.

Choose and document a stable ordering for entity deltas using canonical identifier ordering.

Do not use timestamps or insertion sequence for ordering.

docs.title: Summary support
docs.text:
Implement a compact deterministic summary containing at least:

introduced count
removed count
modified count
total changed entities

This summary should be obtainable without rendering textual source or opening domain-specific details.

docs.title: Large diffs
docs.text:
Design the API so it can later support pagination/streaming without changing semantic meaning.

Do not prematurely implement a complex streaming framework unless the storage API already supports one. Avoid forcing all higher layers to rely on a giant formatted string.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • identical snapshots produce empty diff;
  • one modified entity;
  • one introduced entity;
  • one removed entity;
  • multiple changes sorted deterministically;
  • ancestor-to-descendant comparison;
  • sibling comparison;
  • same final revision reached through different histories still compares as state, not history;
  • unrelated unchanged entities are absent from result;
  • summary counts exactly match deltas;
  • generic diff requires no domain adapter.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Diff is not migration.
  • Diff is not textual file diff.
  • Do not infer historical intent.
  • Do not declare conflicts; merge owns that.
  • Do not mark all entities changed because SnapshotId differs.
  • No concrete backend dependency.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

Run shared store conformance tests if the storage API changed.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Arbitrary snapshots can be compared.
  • [ ] Entity changes use EntityDelta.
  • [ ] No unchanged entities are emitted.
  • [ ] Result ordering is deterministic.
  • [ ] Compact summary exists.
  • [ ] Sibling snapshot tests pass.
  • [ ] Domain enrichment is optional and dependency-safe.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the diff API, any storage capability added, deterministic ordering rule, performance shortcut used for equal snapshots, and tests added.

docs.title: Persist Projection Conflicts and Captured Evidence
Objective
docs.text: Preserve ambiguous or failed projection reconciliation as structured knowledge so an external edit is never reduced to a transient watcher event or silently guessed into canonical history.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 20–23, 44–45, 51 and 60.
  2. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md.
  3. Existing projection/reconciliation Level 2 and Level 3 designs.
  4. Existing provenance/core task.

If projection state, captured projection bytes/text, or candidate reconciliation does not exist yet, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Work primarily in the projection layer and its schema/graph integration. Typical modules:

crates/scriberig-projection/src/conflict.rs
crates/scriberig-projection/src/reconcile.rs
crates/scriberig-projection/src/lib.rs

Use existing graph/schema facilities for persistence. Do not create an unrelated logging database.

docs.title: Captured Observation
docs.text:
When a managed projection changes externally, capture an immutable observation before attempting destructive normalization. It must retain enough data to identify:

projection identity
previous rendered projection/revision
observed external content or blob reference
observation metadata/time if supported
current semantic snapshot
parser/adapter identity and version

The original observation must remain distinguishable from any parsed candidate.

docs.title: Conflict Object
docs.text:
Define a structured conflict capable of representing at least:

base projection/reference
current canonical snapshot
observed external evidence
candidate parse/revision if one exists
ambiguous mappings
conflicting entities/relations
conflict kind
status

Support unresolved and resolved states through immutable history/operations rather than by erasing the original conflict.

docs.title: Reconciliation Behavior
docs.text:
When matching is confident, normal reconciliation may continue.

When matching is ambiguous, the reconciler must return/persist an explicit conflict or candidate alternatives. It must not choose an uncertain lineage silently.

The canonical root remains unchanged until a later resolution produces a normal migration that passes the standard validation/promotion path.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
Provide an application-facing resolution input that references the exact conflict and selected interpretation. The result should produce a normal migration/candidate plus provenance linking back to the conflict and captured observation.

Do not make conflict resolution a privileged direct storage mutation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Create fixtures for:

  1. clean external edit -> no conflict;
  2. ambiguous paragraph merge/split -> conflict persisted;
  3. conflicting concurrent canonical change -> conflict references both states;
  4. original observed content remains accessible after parse failure;
  5. parser output is distinguishable from original evidence;
  6. unresolved conflict does not change canonical root;
  7. resolution creates migration provenance back to conflict;
  8. resolving stale conflict against changed canonical state requires re-evaluation;
  9. conflict history preserves the original competing states.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. Use deterministic small projection fixtures.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not insert textual conflict markers into canonical semantic objects as the primary conflict representation. Do not discard the external observation after parsing. Do not auto-promote a parser's best guess when the matcher reports ambiguity.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] external observations are immutable evidence;
  • [ ] ambiguity becomes a first-class conflict;
  • [ ] canonical state is unchanged by unresolved conflicts;
  • [ ] conflict resolution creates a normal migration/candidate;
  • [ ] provenance reaches back to original observation;
  • [ ] tests cover ambiguity and concurrent changes.

docs.title: Implement External Effect Receipts and Reconciliation
Objective
docs.text:
Create the application-level record and state machine for side-effecting external operations so retries, failures, and local/external disagreement remain explicit.

This task provides reusable external-effect semantics. It does not implement any specific GitHub, email, cloud, or messaging connector.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 27–30 and 61.
  2. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  3. Existing application operation/event designs.
  4. Existing session/tool invocation designs if they are already implemented.

If application operations and capability checks are not implemented, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Typical modules:

crates/scriberig-app/src/external_effect.rs
crates/scriberig-app/src/lib.rs

Protocol exposure is handled by a later task. Connector-specific code must remain outside this module.

docs.title: External Effect Intent
docs.text:
Represent an immutable intent containing at least:

principal
operation kind
external destination identifier
request fingerprint or idempotency key when available
input semantic snapshot/revisions
capability reference/context
created operation id

Do not store reusable credentials in the semantic object.

docs.title: State Model
docs.text:
Represent explicit states equivalent to:

Requested
Attempted
ConfirmedExternally
ReflectedLocally
Failed
Unknown

A local exception after sending a remote request must not be reported as definitely failed when the external outcome is unknown.

State transitions must preserve history/provenance. Do not overwrite a single mutable status without retaining the operation chain.

docs.title: Receipt
docs.text:
Provide a durable receipt/result representation capable of storing non-secret evidence such as:

external operation id
remote resource reference
response/status metadata
confirmation observation
time if supported by existing history model
request fingerprint/idempotency key

Keep raw secrets and credential material out of receipts.

docs.title: Execution Boundary
docs.text:
The application operation must verify InvokeExternal authority for the exact destination before calling connector code.

A local ModifyBranch or Promote capability must not imply external invocation authority.

Run all applicable local validation and approval checks before irreversible invocation where the operation permits it.

docs.title: Retry Semantics
docs.text:
Expose enough state for connector adapters to make safe retry decisions:

  • confirmed success: do not resend blindly;
  • definite failure before remote acceptance: retry may be safe according to connector policy;
  • unknown outcome: require reconciliation/lookup when supported;
  • idempotency key available: reuse it for the same semantic intent.

Do not pretend all external systems are transactional or idempotent.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: Provide an operation to record a later external observation and reconcile it with the pending intent. The result must state whether the effect is confirmed externally and whether local semantic state reflects that confirmation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use a fake connector and test:

  1. external invocation without destination capability is denied;
  2. local write capability alone cannot invoke remote effect;
  3. confirmed success records a receipt;
  4. timeout after send becomes Unknown, not definite failure;
  5. unknown outcome can be reconciled by later observation;
  6. repeated confirmed operation is not blindly resent;
  7. idempotency key is stable for retry of the same intent where configured;
  8. credentials are absent from persisted intent/receipt fixtures;
  9. external success plus local persistence failure remains recoverable/inspectable;
  10. all transitions retain operation provenance.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run workspace formatting, check, tests, and lint. No live external service is required.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not implement a generic secret vault. Do not add a universal network client. Do not claim local database transactions make remote services atomic. Do not log credential values for debugging.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] external authority is destination-specific;
  • [ ] intent and receipt are durable structured objects;
  • [ ] unknown outcome is representable;
  • [ ] retry behavior can use idempotency/reconciliation;
  • [ ] local and external state remain distinguishable;
  • [ ] no connector-specific policy leaks into the universal model.

docs.title: Implement: Observability and Shared Store Conformance
Objective
docs.text:
Create one backend-neutral conformance suite and one backend-neutral observability/error model, then run the same behavior tests against the in-memory and SQLite backends.

This task proves that higher layers can depend on sr-store rather than on a particular backend.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. design/level-2/006. persistence observability and conformance.md
  3. All earlier Level 3 persistence tasks.

docs.title: Files to create or update
docs.text:
In sr-store:

crates/sr-store/src/
├── error.rs
├── stats.rs
└── conformance.rs

Add or update:

crates/sr-store/tests/conformance.rs

Backend crates may add small test adapters, but expected behavior must live in shared conformance logic rather than duplicated test bodies.

docs.title: Error model
docs.text:
Ensure storage errors have machine-readable categories for at least:

  • not found;
  • invalid identifier or encoding;
  • unsupported encoding/storage version;
  • stale named-root compare-and-set;
  • integrity failure;
  • invalid operation;
  • backend transaction/I/O failure.

Backend-specific errors may be retained as sources, but callers must not need to parse backend-specific strings to determine category.

docs.title: Observability types
docs.text:
Implement backend-neutral data types equivalent to:

StoreStats
RootStatus
IntegrityReport
GcReport
IndexStatus

Do not require every backend to provide every numeric statistic. Use optional values when a metric cannot be determined cheaply or meaningfully.

At minimum, expose where possible:

  • revision count;
  • snapshot count;
  • named-root count;
  • reachable/unreachable counts after reachability analysis;
  • backend storage byte count if meaningful;
  • integrity issue counts;
  • GC candidate/deleted counts.

Observability values must not participate in canonical revision or snapshot identity.

docs.title: Shared conformance harness
docs.text:
Build reusable test functions that accept a backend factory or test-store instance implementing the public storage traits.

The suite must verify at least:

  1. put/get immutable revision;
  2. duplicate revision insertion is idempotent;
  3. create/read snapshot;
  4. historical base snapshot remains readable after descendant creation;
  5. branch two snapshots from one base;
  6. deterministic snapshot identity for equivalent maps;
  7. named-root compare-and-set success;
  8. stale compare-and-set conflict and unchanged root;
  9. reopen/durability test when backend declares durable capability;
  10. reachability from protected roots;
  11. integrity verification of healthy data.

Use backend capabilities to skip only behavior that is genuinely inapplicable, such as reopening an in-memory-only store. Core semantic behavior must not be skipped.

docs.title: Cross-backend fixtures
docs.text:
Create deterministic fixture histories such as:

S1: A -> R1, B -> R1
S2: A -> R2, B -> R1
S3: A -> R1, B -> R2

Run the same fixture against memory and SQLite.

Assert that logical RevisionId and SnapshotId values are identical across backends for the same canonical content and complete mapping.

This test is critical: a backend must not influence semantic identity.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• memory backend passes shared suite;
  • SQLite in-memory database passes shared suite;
  • SQLite temporary file database passes durable parts of suite;
  • fixture IDs match across memory and SQLite;
  • error categories match for equivalent failures;
  • observability calls do not change snapshots or roots.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace

Run any stricter lint command already established by the repository. Do not introduce a new CI system in this task.

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add HTTP/CLI observability surfaces.
  • Do not add Prometheus or telemetry dependencies yet.
  • Do not let conformance tests import SQLite internals.
  • Do not loosen semantics merely to make both backends pass.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Shared conformance suite exists.
  • [ ] Memory backend passes it.
  • [ ] SQLite backend passes it.
  • [ ] Cross-backend logical IDs match.
  • [ ] Error categories are backend-neutral.
  • [ ] Observability models are backend-neutral.
  • [ ] Statistics do not affect canonical identity.
  • [ ] Entire workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/react as a thin React integration over @scriberig/client, @scriberig/model, and @scriberig/editor-core.

The package must expose providers and hooks that subscribe React components to reusable model/controller state without moving semantic logic into hooks.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/004. implement client semantic model and incremental events.md
  4. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md

Prerequisite: model and editor-core packages compile and provide framework-independent subscription interfaces.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/react/src/provider.tsx
web/packages/react/src/use-object.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-children.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-snapshot.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-operation.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-session.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-selection.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-commands.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-knowledge-tree.ts
web/packages/react/src/use-migration-review.ts
web/packages/react/test/provider.test.tsx
web/packages/react/test/hooks.test.tsx

Update:

web/packages/react/src/index.ts
web/packages/react/package.json

docs.title: Provider
docs.text:
Create a public React provider that supplies the reusable runtime objects needed by hooks.

The provider should accept already-created objects rather than constructing hidden global singletons.

Expected dependencies include equivalents of:

ScriberigClient
WorkspaceModel
SelectionController
CommandRegistry/ExtensionRegistry as required

The provider must support tests with fake objects.

Do not couple provider creation to one server URL or authentication mechanism.

docs.title: Subscription Strategy
docs.text:
Hooks must subscribe to reusable model/controller state using React-compatible external-store subscription patterns.

Prefer useSyncExternalStore or an equivalent correct React mechanism for framework-external stores.

Do not duplicate model state into per-component React state merely to trigger renders.

Do not introduce Redux or another React state framework.

docs.title: Object Hook
docs.text:
use-object.ts should expose the state needed to inspect a semantic object/reference.

It should distinguish where possible:

not requested/loading
loaded
not found/error
stale relative to current snapshot
historical exact state

Loading must go through WorkspaceModel/client APIs.

Do not silently replace an exact historical revision with a current revision.

docs.title: Children Hook
docs.text:
use-children.ts should bind relation/collection loading to React.

Support:

  • initial page load;
  • loading state;
  • error state;
  • loaded children;
  • child counts when known;
  • load-more/cursor behavior;
  • snapshot-aware cache reuse.

Do not recursively load descendants.

docs.title: Snapshot Hook
docs.text:
use-snapshot.ts should expose at least:

  • current canonical snapshot known by the model;
  • viewed snapshot when supplied by context/controller;
  • whether the view is current, historical, candidate, or stale.

Do not reduce snapshot awareness to a boolean if the model exposes richer state.

docs.title: Operation Hook
docs.text:
use-operation.ts observes one long-running operation by OperationId.

Expose lifecycle, progress, result references, error information, and cancellation capability when available.

Do not tie an operation to the lifecycle of the initiating component.

Unmounting a view must not implicitly cancel a server operation.

docs.title: Session Hook
docs.text:
use-session.ts exposes loaded session/branch semantic summaries and loading operations.

It must not reinterpret sessions as only chat message arrays.

Preserve branch IDs, descriptions, outcomes, decisions, tasks, and migration/result references exposed by protocol/model.

docs.title: Selection Hook
docs.text:
use-selection.ts binds the shared SelectionController to React.

Expose:

selection
setSelection
clearSelection

plus any small helper required to update relation/projection context.

All editor views must be able to share the same controller instance.

docs.title: Commands Hook
docs.text:
use-commands.ts returns command descriptors applicable to the current or supplied selection/capability context.

It must use editor-core command discovery.

Do not hard-code command lists in the hook.

Execution should invoke the operation descriptor/client path defined by editor-core.

docs.title: Knowledge Tree Hook
docs.text:
Wrap the headless knowledge tree controller for React consumption.

Expose rows/nodes and actions such as:

expand
collapse
select
loadMore
refresh

Do not implement tree markup in this package.

docs.title: Migration Review Hook
docs.text:
Bind the headless migration review controller to React.

Expose selected change, affected objects, validation/stale/conflict state, and public apply/reject actions.

Do not perform direct state mutation outside controller/client APIs.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use React Testing Library or hook test utilities compatible with the workspace.

Required cases:

  1. provider can use fake client/model/controller objects;
  2. one model subscription updates multiple consumers consistently;
  3. selection changed by one consumer is observed by another;
  4. historical snapshot state remains exact after current snapshot advances;
  5. operation hook survives initiating component removal when observed elsewhere;
  6. commands update when capabilities or selection change;
  7. no hook requires MUI context.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/react typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/react test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/react build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add MUI.
  • Do not create visual components.
  • Do not hard-code app routes.
  • Do not create a global singleton client/model.
  • Do not duplicate cache logic from @scriberig/model.
  • Do not duplicate selection/tree/command state machines from @scriberig/editor-core.
  • Do not treat sessions as only message arrays.
  • Do not cancel server operations automatically on component unmount.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] A configurable public provider exists.
  • [ ] Hooks subscribe to external model/controller state correctly.
  • [ ] Object/children/snapshot/operation/session hooks exist.
  • [ ] Selection and commands use shared editor-core controllers.
  • [ ] Knowledge tree and migration review have headless React bindings.
  • [ ] No MUI dependency exists.
  • [ ] Tests demonstrate shared selection and snapshot correctness.
  • [ ] Package and workspace checks pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the Rust-specific source syntax specialization and adapter in scriberig-domain-rust on top of scriberig-domain-code.

This task represents Rust source syntax faithfully enough for semantic inspection, editing, and later projection reconciliation. It does not implement compiler-derived analysis; that is a separate task.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  2. design/level-3/005. implement language independent code domain.md
  3. current public APIs of scriberig-schema, scriberig-graph, scriberig-migration, and scriberig-projection

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/rust/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/syntax.rs
src/parse.rs
src/render.rs
src/mapping.rs
src/comments.rs
src/code_groups.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/parse_render.rs
tests/schema.rs
tests/comments_and_groups.rs

Do not create compiler-analysis modules in this task.

docs.title: Parser Dependency
docs.text:
Choose one mature Rust parser that preserves source-level syntax needed for round-trip semantics, including attributes, patterns, macros/token trees, comments or source ranges sufficient to recover comments, and nested expressions/statements.

Prefer an already-selected workspace dependency if one exists. Do not introduce multiple competing Rust syntax parsers.

Parser-specific types must remain private to the adapter.

docs.title: Rust Schema Specialization
docs.text:
Extend the language-independent code domain with Rust-specific constructs needed for the supported syntax slice.

At minimum represent:

functions
parameters
patterns
type syntax
let statements
expression statements
path expressions
call/method-call expressions
binary/unary expressions
blocks
if expressions
match expressions and arms
return/break/continue where relevant
structs/enums where needed for module inspection
impl blocks
attributes
macro invocations
token trees or equivalent concrete syntax for macros
comments

Use language-independent Module, Function, Parameter, CodeGroup, Statement, Expression, and Comment concepts where appropriate, and Rust-specific types where semantics differ.

Do not normalize Rust into a generic compiler IR.

docs.title: Canonical Syntax Rules
docs.text:
Canonical state must preserve author-chosen syntax that matters to source-level meaning or faithful reconstruction.

Preserve at least:

  • declaration structure and order;
  • parameter patterns and type syntax;
  • statement/expression structure;
  • attributes;
  • macro invocation syntax and token trees where normalization would lose information;
  • source-authored comments that can be reliably attached;
  • meaningful grouping and ordering.

Do not make ordinary indentation, line wrapping, or spacing semantic identity.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Recover comments from source and represent them through the shared code-domain comment model.

Attach comments to the nearest domain object only when the attachment is deterministic enough to preserve author intent.

When attachment is ambiguous, preserve source-location metadata and avoid inventing a false semantic attachment.

Distinguish source-authored comments from future generated descriptions.

docs.title: Code Groups
docs.text:
Create initial deterministic code groups from source evidence only.

Use signals such as:

blank-line boundaries
leading explanatory comments
explicit block boundaries
statement sequence

Do not call a model to name groups.

A group may have no human-readable purpose description yet. Preserve the group boundary/provenance separately from any later derived summary.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
Implement deterministic source rendering for the supported canonical syntax.

The renderer may use an existing pretty-print/formatting library if compatible with the projection architecture, but must render from Scriberig semantic state rather than retaining the original source file as the authoritative representation.

Macros/token structures that cannot be safely normalized must round-trip without semantic loss.

Do not silently replace unsupported constructs with placeholders.

docs.title: Source Coordinates
docs.text:
Parser source spans, filenames, line numbers, and byte positions are adapter/projection metadata.

They may support diagnostics, external editing, and UI highlighting, but they must not be the primary semantic identities of functions, statements, expressions, or comments.

docs.title: Adapter API
docs.text:
Expose syntax-domain operations through existing domain/projection abstractions where available:

parse/import Rust source -> candidate semantic objects
render Rust semantic scope -> source text

Do not expose parser AST types publicly.

Do not write directly to persistence from parse/render operations.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Include fixtures covering at least:

simple functions
patterns and typed parameters
nested expressions
if/match
attributes
impl blocks
macros
comments
blank-line/comment code grouping

Test:

  • parse produces expected semantic structure;
  • shared code-domain concepts are reused;
  • Rust-specific syntax remains specialized;
  • comments are preserved without becoming parser trivia;
  • macro/token syntax survives round trip;
  • parse -> render -> parse preserves equivalent canonical syntax for supported fixtures;
  • formatting-only differences do not change canonical semantics;
  • no semantic identity depends on line numbers.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-rust
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-rust --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement symbol resolution or type inference.
  • Do not implement call/CFG/data-flow graphs.
  • Do not use rustc IR as canonical storage.
  • Do not flatten macros into expanded compiler syntax as the only representation.
  • Do not add agent dependencies.
  • Do not create Rust-specific persistence tables.
  • Do not make formatting whitespace canonical.
  • Do not silently discard unsupported syntax.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Rust-specific schema extends the shared code domain.
  • [ ] Source syntax is represented semantically rather than as one text blob.
  • [ ] Comments are preserved as first-class knowledge where deterministic.
  • [ ] Initial code groups come from source evidence only.
  • [ ] Macros/token trees preserve author syntax.
  • [ ] Rendering is deterministic for supported syntax.
  • [ ] Parser implementation details remain private.
  • [ ] No compiler-derived analysis is mixed into canonical syntax.
  • [ ] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Three-Way Merge and Structured Conflicts
Goal
docs.text:
Implement the universal three-way merge engine and structured conflict model for sr-change.

This task consumes exact snapshots and universal diffs. It must merge independent changes automatically and preserve ambiguity as semantic conflicts.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 21 through 30 and 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Level 3 task 005 implementation of universal semantic diff.
  4. Existing history/common-ancestor APIs.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/conflict.rs
crates/sr-change/src/merge.rs
crates/sr-change/src/diff.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

docs.title: Merge input
docs.text:
Expose a public merge request equivalent in meaning to:

MergeInput {
    base: SnapshotId,
    left: SnapshotId,
    right: SnapshotId,
}

The caller may supply the base explicitly. If a convenience API derives it, use explicit history topology and common-ancestor logic rather than timestamps.

docs.title: Base validation
docs.text:
When the merge API is given an explicit base, verify that it is a valid ancestry base when the operation requires ancestry.

Return a typed error for an invalid base rather than silently substituting another snapshot.

docs.title: Universal merge rules
docs.text:
Apply these rules in order:

  1. Compute base -> left and base -> right diffs.
  2. If an entity changed on only one side, adopt that side.
  3. If both sides resolve an entity to the same exact revision, converge without conflict.
  4. If neither side changes an entity, omit it from the merge change set.
  5. If both sides make different changes to the same entity, attempt deeper generic merge only when the available structure proves it is safe.
  6. If safe resolution is not possible, create a structured conflict.

Do not choose left or right by default.

docs.title: Structured conflict model
docs.text:
Implement a universal conflict type with at least:

entity: EntityId
base: Option<RevisionId>
left: Option<RevisionId>
right: Option<RevisionId>
kind: ConflictKind

Initial ConflictKind values must cover:

BothModified
DeleteModify
CompetingCreate
RelationConflict
CollectionConflict
DomainConflict

Allow optional structured detail for an affected generic field/relation/collection path and optional domain detail.

Do not store textual conflict markers as the canonical conflict.

docs.title: Minimal conflict scope
docs.text:
If only one entity conflicts, preserve all other automatically resolved entity changes in the merge result.

The result should separate:

resolved entity deltas
unresolved conflicts

A conflict must not erase unrelated successful merge work.

docs.title: Merge result
docs.text:
Return a structure equivalent in meaning to:

MergeResult {
    base,
    left,
    right,
    resolved_deltas,
    conflicts,
}

Do not automatically promote the result to a named root.

If creating a provisional result snapshot is supported, it must be a new immutable snapshot and must clearly remain provisional when unresolved conflicts exist.

docs.title: Domain merge strategy
docs.text:
Implement the extension point prescribed by Level 2.

A domain strategy receives exact base/left/right state for one conflicted semantic area and may return either:

Resolved(delta or revision)
Conflict(domain detail)
NotApplicable

Domain strategies must not mutate input snapshots.

The generic merge engine must work with zero registered domain strategies.

docs.title: Generic collection merge
docs.text:
Only implement generic collection resolution where the intent is mechanically unambiguous.

Examples that may be safe:

  • independent insertion at distinct stable positions;
  • identical insertion by both sides;
  • independent changes to different members when identity and order are unambiguous.

If ordering intent is ambiguous, emit CollectionConflict.

Do not implement a large domain-specific list algorithm in this task.

docs.title: Merge provenance
docs.text:
Provide enough output for a later migration record to retain:

merge base
left input
right input
automatically resolved entities
explicit/domain resolutions
unresolved conflicts

Do not require history persistence to be performed inside the pure merge algorithm.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • left-only change merges;
  • right-only change merges;
  • disjoint changes to two entities merge;
  • both sides produce same revision and converge;
  • different edits to same entity produce BothModified;
  • left delete/right modify produces DeleteModify;
  • competing creation of same semantic entity produces CompetingCreate when revisions differ;
  • one conflict does not discard unrelated resolved changes;
  • domain strategy can resolve one same-entity change;
  • no domain strategy still returns structured conflict;
  • ambiguous collection order produces CollectionConflict;
  • merge does not mutate base/left/right snapshots.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• No textual merge as the canonical algorithm.
  • No left-wins/right-wins fallback.
  • No timestamp-based base selection.
  • No automatic named-root promotion.
  • Domain-specific code must stay outside sr-change.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Merge is explicitly three-way.
  • [ ] Disjoint changes merge automatically.
  • [ ] Equal revisions converge.
  • [ ] Ambiguity becomes structured conflict.
  • [ ] Conflict scope is minimal.
  • [ ] Domain strategy extension is optional.
  • [ ] Inputs remain immutable.
  • [ ] Tests cover delete/modify and competing edits.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the merge stages, conflict kinds, domain strategy interface, automatic-resolution cases, and tests proving unresolved conflicts preserve unrelated merged work.

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Review the completed sr-core and sr-store identity subsystem as one integrated unit, add any missing conformance coverage, and fix only defects that violate the Level 1 or Level 2 identity contracts.

This task is not an opportunity to add new product features. Its purpose is to prove that the implementation created by Level 3 tasks 001 through 005 actually satisfies the architecture before higher layers depend on it.

docs.title: Read Before Editing
docs.text:
Read completely:

design/level-1/003. identity revisions and snapshots.md
design/level-2/001. identity revision snapshot implementation.md
design/level-3/001. bootstrap workspace and identity types.md
design/level-3/002. implement canonical encoding and revision hashing.md
design/level-3/003. implement immutable revision store.md
design/level-3/004. implement persistent snapshots and diffs.md
design/level-3/005. implement named roots and compare and swap.md

Then inspect all source and tests under:

crates/sr-core/
crates/sr-store/

docs.title: Files You May Modify
docs.text:
Prefer adding integration coverage in:

crates/sr-store/tests/identity_conformance.rs

You may fix defects in existing sr-core or sr-store files when a test demonstrates that they violate the design.

Do not redesign APIs merely for style preference.

docs.title: Required End-to-End Scenario
docs.text: Add an integration test that performs this exact logical sequence.
