docs.title: Step 1: Create entities
docs.text:
Create stable entities:

F
P1
P2
B

Create canonical revisions:

FR7
PR3
PR8
BR2

Store all revisions.

docs.title: Step 2: Build snapshot S1
docs.text:
Build a snapshot containing:

F  -> FR7
P1 -> PR3
P2 -> PR8
B  -> BR2

Record S1 and its SnapshotId.

docs.title: Step 3: Change only P2
docs.text:
Create a new revision for the same entity P2:

PR9

The EntityId of P2 must stay unchanged.

Create successor snapshot S2 with only:

P2 -> PR9

changed.

docs.title: Step 4: Assert local stability
docs.text:
Verify:

  • [ ] F still resolves to FR7 in S2;
  • [ ] P1 still resolves to PR3 in S2;
  • [ ] B still resolves to BR2 in S2;
  • [ ] P2 resolves to PR8 in S1;
  • [ ] P2 resolves to PR9 in S2;
  • [ ] no semantic parent revision was manufactured merely because P2 changed.

docs.title: Step 5: Assert global certainty
docs.text:
Verify:

  • [ ] S1.id() != S2.id();
  • [ ] rebuilding S1 in another insertion order produces the same SnapshotId;
  • [ ] rebuilding S2 in another insertion order produces the same SnapshotId.

docs.title: Step 6: Assert exact history
docs.text:
Verify that S1 remains readable after S2 exists and still resolves every entity to the original revisions.

No operation may retarget S1.

docs.title: Step 7: Assert semantic snapshot diff
docs.text:
Verify S1.diff(S2) contains exactly one change:

Changed {
  entity: P2,
  from: PR8,
  to: PR9
}

No unchanged entity may appear.

docs.title: Step 8: Assert named-root concurrency semantics
docs.text:
Set:

main -> S1

Advance it with compare-and-swap:

expected S1
new S2

Verify success.

Then try another update still expecting S1.

Verify:

  • [ ] it fails as stale;
  • [ ] main remains at S2;
  • [ ] neither S1 nor S2 changed.

docs.title: Additional Invariant Audit
docs.text: Check the implementation manually and with tests for every item below.

docs.title: Identity separation
docs.text:
• [ ] EntityId, RevisionId, and SnapshotId are distinct Rust types.
  • [ ] An EntityId is not computed from current content.
  • [ ] A RevisionId is content-derived.
  • [ ] A SnapshotId is content-derived from global mapping state.

docs.title: Historical exactness
docs.text:
• [ ] Revisions have no mutable update method.
  • [ ] Snapshots have no mutable update method that changes an existing value in place.
  • [ ] Named roots are pointers, not snapshot identities.

docs.title: Canonical hashing
docs.text:
• [ ] Encoding version is included in revision hashes.
  • [ ] Type ID is included in revision hashes.
  • [ ] Entity ID is not included in revision hashes.
  • [ ] Snapshot internal node hashes use domain separation.
  • [ ] Snapshot root hash uses separate root domain separation.
  • [ ] No unordered map iteration participates in canonical identity.

docs.title: Change propagation
docs.text:
• [ ] One entity update does not copy the full entity-to-revision mapping.
  • [ ] An update copies only the bounded trie path plus the new leaf/state required.
  • [ ] Unaffected branches are structurally shared.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
• [ ] Equivalent revision values have equivalent IDs.
  • [ ] Equivalent snapshot mappings have equivalent IDs regardless of insertion order.
  • [ ] Diff order is deterministic.
  • [ ] ID textual forms round-trip exactly.

docs.title: Dependency direction
docs.text:
• [ ] sr-core does not depend on sr-store.
  • [ ] Neither crate depends on agent, server, UI, domain, filesystem watcher, or database-driver crates.

docs.title: Test Organization
docs.text:
If existing tests already prove an invariant clearly, do not duplicate them unnecessarily.

The new conformance test should focus on cross-module behavior that individual unit tests cannot prove alone.

Use fixed EntityId::from_bytes(...) values for most deterministic tests. Use EntityId::new() only when testing fresh identity generation.

docs.title: Documentation Check
docs.text:
Ensure the public APIs make these distinctions understandable without reading implementation internals:

EntityId = conceptual continuity
RevisionId = exact immutable local state
SnapshotId = exact immutable global state
named root = mutable pointer to SnapshotId

Add short rustdoc where the distinction is unclear.

Do not add long architectural essays to source files; the design documents remain authoritative.

docs.title: Commands to Run
docs.text:
Run all of the following successfully:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps

If rustdoc warnings are enabled by the workspace, fix warnings introduced by these crates.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text:
• Do not add SQLite.
  • Do not add migrations.
  • Do not add domain schemas.
  • Do not add projection rendering.
  • Do not add agent APIs.
  • Do not optimize snapshot diff unless correctness requires a fix.
  • Do not change identity semantics to make tests easier.
  • Do not replace the persistent trie with a full copied HashMap.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Cross-module conformance scenario exists and passes.
  • [ ] Local entity stability is demonstrated.
  • [ ] Immutable historical revisions are demonstrated.
  • [ ] Global snapshot change is demonstrated.
  • [ ] Snapshot diff identifies only the changed entity resolution.
  • [ ] Named-root CAS behavior is demonstrated.
  • [ ] Structural sharing is still covered.
  • [ ] All workspace tests pass.
  • [ ] cargo fmt --check passes.
  • [ ] clippy with warnings denied passes.
  • [ ] docs build successfully.

When this task is complete, the identity subsystem is ready for later Level 2 designs covering durable persistence, migrations, domains, projections, sessions, and agents.

docs.title: Expose Trust State Through Protocol and Events
Objective
docs.text:
Expose trust-relevant application results through the shared Rust/wire protocol so server, remote clients, web libraries, TUI, CLI adapters, and agent tooling can observe the same semantics.

This task is transport representation only. It must not reimplement authorization, validation, promotion, or external-effect logic inside the protocol/server.

docs.title: Read First
docs.text:
1. design/level-1/013. trust validation capabilities and provenance.md, especially sections 30, 32, 37–39, 49, 52–54.
  2. design/level-1/011. runtime libraries protocol and product surfaces.md.
  3. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md.
  4. design/level-3/001. implement principal and capability model.md.
  5. design/level-3/003. implement validation evidence and exact input binding.md.
  6. design/level-3/004. implement candidate promotion and approval pipeline.md.
  7. design/level-3/006. implement external effect receipts and reconciliation.md.

If the shared protocol crate or application operations do not exist, stop and report the prerequisite.

docs.title: Expected Area
docs.text:
Typical files/modules:

crates/scriberig-protocol/src/trust.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/event.rs
crates/scriberig-protocol/src/lib.rs
crates/scriberig-server/... application-to-protocol adapters
web/packages/protocol/... generated/shared representations if that path already exists

Follow the repository's established schema generation approach. Do not maintain unrelated Rust and TypeScript wire models manually if generation already exists.

docs.title: Protocol Types
docs.text:
Expose serializable representations for at least:

CapabilityDenied
TrustSummary / provenance summary
ValidationSummary
ValidationDiagnostic
PolicyEvaluationSummary
ApprovalSummary
PromotionResult
ConflictSummary
ExternalEffectSummary / ReceiptSummary

Use stable IDs/references to inspect full underlying knowledge objects rather than embedding entire graphs into every response.

A compact trust summary should be able to say things equivalent to:

source kind
current validation state
last accepted migration/promotion
whether generated vs authored/observed
links/handles for deeper provenance

Do not invent one global trust score.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Add event variants for at least:

CandidateCreated
ValidationStarted
ValidationCompleted
ApprovalRecorded
ConflictDetected
CapabilityDenied
ExternalEffectUpdated
SnapshotPromoted

Events must carry operation/candidate/snapshot handles sufficient for a client to fetch current details.

Do not duplicate full validation output into every event when a result object can be referenced.

docs.title: Server Adapter
docs.text:
Map application results/errors to protocol types. The server must not reinterpret policy or retry denied operations with broader authority.

A capability denial must remain a denial, not become a generic 500/error string.

A stale/conflict promotion result must remain distinguishable from validation failure.

docs.title: TypeScript Parity
docs.text: If the TypeScript protocol package exists, update the generated/shared type surface and add compile-time tests/examples proving the trust/event variants are available to web clients.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  1. structured capability denial round-trip;
  2. validation result with diagnostics round-trip;
  3. promotion allowed/rejected/stale states remain distinct;
  4. conflict summary contains resolvable handles;
  5. external-effect unknown state survives serialization;
  6. events reference exact candidate/snapshot/operation IDs;
  7. no secret/credential field exists in trust protocol objects;
  8. Rust and TypeScript protocol representations stay in sync using the repository's normal conformance test.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Run Rust workspace checks and web/type generation checks already defined by the repository.

docs.title: Do Not
docs.text: Do not add server-only business rules. Do not flatten all trust state into strings. Do not leak restricted payloads inside denials/events. Do not expose reusable credentials.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] trust outcomes have stable protocol representations;
  • [ ] denial/validation/conflict/promotion states remain distinct;
  • [ ] trust events use the common event model;
  • [ ] server is an adapter, not policy owner;
  • [ ] TypeScript consumers receive the same contract;
  • [ ] no sensitive material is serialized.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/components as a reusable React component library over @scriberig/react and @scriberig/editor-core with minimal visual assumptions and no MUI dependency.

The components provide ready-made semantic views while preserving replaceability and styling freedom for third-party applications.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement react bindings.md

Prerequisite: React bindings and headless controllers compile.

docs.title: Styling Rules
docs.text:
The package must not depend on MUI or another application design system.

Allowed styling mechanisms:

  • semantic class names;
  • data attributes;
  • minimal package CSS if needed for structural layout/accessibility;
  • render props/slots for caller-owned rendering;
  • standard HTML attributes and ARIA roles.

Do not hard-code Scriberig product colors, typography, spacing system, or panel layout.

Components should accept className and relevant standard DOM props where practical.

docs.title: ObjectTree
docs.text:
Render the headless knowledge tree state.

Requirements:

  • lazy expanded children only;
  • expandable/collapsible rows;
  • loading and error state per node;
  • semantic labels/descriptions where present;
  • selection integration;
  • load-more behavior;
  • keyboard navigation provided through shared interaction behavior;
  • accessible tree/treeitem semantics where appropriate.

Do not fetch descendants independently from editor-core/model logic.

docs.title: ObjectInspector
docs.text:
Render semantic object information in a domain-neutral form.

Support at least:

  • semantic identity/reference;
  • type/schema label;
  • description/provenance where supplied;
  • current/exact revision information;
  • properties/summary values;
  • available relations;
  • stale/historical indicators.

Allow domain extensions or caller slots to replace sections.

docs.title: RelationBrowser
docs.text:
Render one selected relation/collection with pagination and semantic child selection.

Do not treat relation contents as a flat static array if the model exposes paging/count metadata.

docs.title: HistoryView and SemanticDiffView
docs.text:
HistoryView renders semantic history/lineage summaries and allows selection of revisions/snapshots for comparison.

SemanticDiffView renders structured semantic diff data rather than computing diffs itself.

Support caller/domain rendering overrides for specialized diff entries.

Do not implement source-text diffing algorithms in this package.

docs.title: MigrationPreview
docs.text:
Render a migration proposal/detail including:

  • base snapshot;
  • affected objects;
  • selected semantic changes;
  • validation status;
  • stale/conflict state;
  • apply/accept action when capability permits;
  • reject/close local review action.

Use the migration review controller/hook.

Do not directly mutate server/database state.

docs.title: SessionTree and BranchView
docs.text:
Represent sessions as structured semantic objects.

SessionTree must expose branches and nested branch structure progressively.

BranchView should show, where available:

  • title/description;
  • purpose;
  • status;
  • outcome;
  • touched objects;
  • decisions/tasks;
  • resulting migrations/snapshots;
  • links to detailed turn/chat projection when requested.

Do not reduce the session model to one chronological chat list.

docs.title: ValidationResults and OperationView
docs.text:
ValidationResults renders structured validation results and preserves distinctions among checks, diagnostics, pass/fail states, and references.

OperationView renders one durable operation lifecycle and progress/result references.

Closing/unmounting the component must not cancel the operation automatically.

docs.title: ProjectionHost
docs.text:
ProjectionHost is a domain-neutral host for registered projection view/editor implementations.

Responsibilities:

  • receive projection identity and semantic selection context;
  • locate the applicable registered projection handler;
  • display unsupported/readonly states explicitly;
  • pass semantic location selection callbacks between projection handler and shared selection model;
  • surface stale/candidate/conflict state.

Do not hard-code Monaco, CodeMirror, PDF.js, or Markdown editors in this task.

docs.title: AgentOperationView
docs.text:
Render agent operation state and semantic result links.

It may show streamed text/output when protocol exposes it, but semantic links to branch, migration, validation, and affected objects are first-class.

Do not make plain chat output the only result representation.

docs.title: Slots and Domain Extension
docs.text:
Where domain-specific rendering is expected, accept typed render callbacks/registered view descriptors rather than importing every domain package directly.

The neutral package should be able to render a useful fallback when no specialized extension exists.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Required shared behavior:

  • keyboard-operable tree and command controls;
  • semantic button labels;
  • focusable interactive rows where appropriate;
  • ARIA roles for trees, lists, status, progress, dialogs/panels when applicable;
  • no interaction that is pointer-only.

Do not duplicate complex focus logic if editor-core already provides it.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests:

  1. ObjectTree renders only loaded/expanded children;
  2. selection changes through a tree row update shared selection;
  3. keyboard navigation works for the primary tree interaction;
  4. historical/stale state is visible in ObjectInspector;
  5. MigrationPreview shows conflict/stale state distinctly from validation failure;
  6. SessionTree renders branch summaries without loading every branch transcript;
  7. unmounting OperationView does not cancel the underlying operation;
  8. package tests run without MUI context/theme.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/components typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add MUI.
  • Do not add a product theme.
  • Do not implement app routing or panel layout.
  • Do not duplicate transport/model/editor-core state machines.
  • Do not implement source-specific projection editors.
  • Do not query the server directly from visual components when a hook/controller exists.
  • Do not create frontend-only mutation semantics.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All prescribed neutral components exist.
  • [ ] No MUI dependency exists.
  • [ ] Components consume public hooks/controllers rather than private state.
  • [ ] ObjectTree is lazy and keyboard accessible.
  • [ ] History/diff/migration/session/operation views preserve semantic structure.
  • [ ] ProjectionHost supports registered domain handlers.
  • [ ] AgentOperationView preserves semantic result links.
  • [ ] Components expose styling/slot extension points.
  • [ ] Required tests and workspace typecheck pass.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Rebase and Semantic Replay
Goal
docs.text:
Implement rebase as creation of new history by replaying existing semantic work onto a different base snapshot.

The implementation must preserve original history and prefer recorded semantic intent over textual or positional patching.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 31 through 35 and 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. The completed migration, history, diff, and conflict models.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/rebase.rs
crates/sr-change/src/operation.rs
crates/sr-change/src/conflict.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

docs.title: Rebase model
docs.text:
A rebase takes:

original base snapshot
original result snapshot or migration sequence
new base snapshot

and attempts to produce a new descendant of the new base.

Conceptually:

S1 -> S2
 \
  -> S3

rebase S1->S2 onto S3

S3 -> S4

S2 and its migration history remain unchanged.

docs.title: Replay order
docs.text:
For each original migration, replay in historical order.

For each change, use this preference order:

  1. recorded domain semantic operation through a registered domain replay strategy;
  2. recorded universal generic semantic operation;
  3. exact entity delta only when it can be applied safely against the new base;
  4. structured conflict when intent cannot be preserved safely.

Never fall back to byte offsets, line numbers, or rendered text patches in the universal engine.

docs.title: Domain replay strategy
docs.text:
Implement the Level 2 extension point for domain replay.

A domain strategy should receive:

  • the semantic operation;
  • old base/result references needed to understand it;
  • current target snapshot/context.

It should return an equivalent of:

Applied(changes)
Conflict(detail)
NotApplicable

The strategy must not mutate historical input state.

docs.title: Generic replay
docs.text:
Support replay for universal operations whose semantics remain unambiguous, such as:

  • replace entity revision when the target still resolves to the expected old revision;
  • insert/remove relation when the precondition still holds;
  • collection insertion/removal/move when stable entity identities and anchors still resolve unambiguously.

If a precondition does not hold, return a structured replay conflict instead of guessing.

docs.title: Replay preconditions
docs.text:
Each generic operation should define the semantic condition under which it can be safely replayed.

Examples:

ReplaceRevision(E, old, new)
requires target snapshot resolves E -> old

RemoveRelation(A, R, B)
requires relation exists

InsertCollectionMember(after X, Y)
requires X still identifies an unambiguous anchor

Do not silently adapt a failed precondition unless a domain strategy explicitly understands the change.

docs.title: Rebase result
docs.text:
Return a structure containing at least:

original base
original work/result
new base
new result snapshot if fully applied
new migration records or proposals
conflicts

Do not promote the rebased result automatically.

docs.title: History preservation
docs.text:
Tests must prove:

  • original snapshots and migrations remain readable;
  • rebased work receives new result snapshots;
  • rebased migration base references the new line of history;
  • original and rebased histories are distinguishable even if they converge to the same final state.

docs.title: Multi-migration replay
docs.text:
Support replaying a sequence, not only one migration.

Stop or continue after a conflict according to a documented deterministic policy. Prefer stopping at the first unresolved migration unless the implementation can safely isolate independent later work.

Do not partially claim a complete rebase when conflicts remain.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • clean replay of one ReplaceRevision onto an unchanged entity;
  • replay conflict when the new base already changed that entity differently;
  • generic relation operation replay;
  • replay of two sequential migrations preserves order;
  • domain replay strategy resolves an operation unknown to the generic engine;
  • missing domain strategy yields conflict rather than discarded intent;
  • original history remains unchanged;
  • rebased state is a descendant of the new base;
  • same final state through rebase still has distinct history provenance.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Rebase never rewrites old history.
  • Do not use textual patch application.
  • Do not silently ignore failed operations.
  • Do not automatically promote rebased work.
  • Do not introduce domain-specific code into sr-change.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Rebase creates new history.
  • [ ] Semantic operations are preferred for replay.
  • [ ] Generic operation preconditions are explicit.
  • [ ] Failed preconditions become conflicts.
  • [ ] Domain replay is optional and dependency-safe.
  • [ ] Original history remains exact.
  • [ ] Multi-migration replay is tested.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the replay order, precondition rules, conflict behavior, domain extension interface, and tests proving original history is unchanged.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Add Rust compiler/static-analysis integration as derived knowledge over canonical Rust syntax.

This task must keep compiler facts separate from canonical source syntax. The same canonical Rust entities remain authoritative even when compiler/toolchain-derived analysis is absent, stale, or rebuilt.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  2. design/level-3/005. implement language independent code domain.md
  3. design/level-3/006. implement rust syntax domain adapter.md
  4. the current derived-knowledge/provenance APIs in shared crates

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/rust/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/analysis.rs
src/analysis_profile.rs
src/analysis_mapping.rs
src/diagnostics.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/derived_analysis.rs

If the project has already standardized on a separate crate for compiler integration, place the files there instead and preserve the boundaries in this task.

docs.title: Analysis Boundary
docs.text:
Implement analysis as a producer of derived knowledge.

The derived output must identify enough provenance to answer:

which canonical entities/revisions were inputs?
which analyzer/tool produced the result?
which tool version/profile/configuration was used?
which project/build settings affected the result?

Do not write compiler facts into canonical Rust syntax revisions.

docs.title: Initial Derived Facts
docs.text:
Support an initial useful subset such as:

resolved symbol references
function callers/callees where available
resolved/inferred type information where available
compiler diagnostics
lint diagnostics

If the chosen analysis integration naturally provides additional facts, keep them behind explicit derived-analysis types rather than promoting them into canonical state.

Control-flow and data-flow graphs may be deferred unless already straightforward with the chosen integration.

docs.title: Tool/Library Choice
docs.text:
Prefer an analysis API already selected elsewhere in the repository.

If none exists, choose one Rust analysis integration suitable for library use and document why it is used. Do not integrate multiple competing analyzer stacks in this task.

The external analyzer's transient IDs must not become Scriberig semantic identity.

Map analyzer references back to canonical Scriberig entities using source/syntax correspondence and store the result as derived relations with provenance.

docs.title: Dependency Tracking
docs.text:
Derived results may depend on more than one source entity.

Track exact or sufficiently precise dependencies for each analysis result so unchanged inputs can reuse cached analysis and changed dependencies can invalidate it.

Include relevant environment/profile inputs when they change semantics, including as applicable:

toolchain/compiler version
target
features
workspace/dependency state
configuration

Do not key validity only by the global current snapshot if a narrower dependency set is available.

docs.title: Queryability
docs.text:
Make the resulting facts available through shared graph/query abstractions where those APIs exist.

A future caller should be able to support operations equivalent to:

find references to symbol/function
find callers
inspect resolved type
list diagnostics affecting an entity

Do not create an agent-specific query API.

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text:
Compiler analysis may fail because source is incomplete, dependencies are unavailable, or the environment is invalid.

Represent failures explicitly as derived analysis/diagnostic results when useful.

A failed analysis must not corrupt or invalidate canonical source knowledge.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use a small Rust fixture workspace and test at least:

  • a function reference resolves to the intended canonical function entity;
  • caller/callee relation can be queried;
  • one type fact is mapped to the correct source entity;
  • diagnostics are derived objects with provenance;
  • changing a relevant source revision invalidates/recomputes dependent analysis;
  • changing an unrelated entity does not force unrelated analysis to become semantically different when dependencies are unchanged;
  • compiler/analyzer transient IDs are not exposed as Scriberig identities.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-rust
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-rust --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not store compiler IR as the canonical program.
  • Do not overwrite canonical syntax with inferred types or resolved symbols.
  • Do not use analyzer IDs as semantic IDs.
  • Do not require an agent runtime.
  • Do not make failed analysis delete source entities.
  • Do not create a separate analysis persistence database.
  • Do not implement model-generated code descriptions in this task.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Compiler/static-analysis facts are explicitly derived.
  • [ ] Provenance includes producer/profile/version information.
  • [ ] Dependencies are recorded precisely enough for safe reuse/invalidation.
  • [ ] Symbol/reference or caller relationships are queryable.
  • [ ] Diagnostics remain derived knowledge.
  • [ ] Canonical Rust syntax remains unchanged by analysis.
  • [ ] Analysis failure does not damage canonical state.
  • [ ] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Perform the final integration pass for the persistence work derived from Level 1 document 004.

This task should not add a new subsystem. It verifies that the implemented storage slice behaves as one coherent backend-independent platform capability.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/004. persistence and storage model.md
  2. all design/level-2/00*.md persistence documents created from it;
  3. Level 3 tasks 001 through 006.

Inspect the current implementation before making changes. Prefer small corrective changes over redesign.

docs.title: Acceptance scenario
docs.text: Construct the following history through the public sr-store API.

docs.title: Step 1: canonical revisions
docs.text:
Create entities A, B, and C at revisions:

A -> A1
B -> B1
C -> C1

Create snapshot S1 containing those mappings.

Promote named root main to S1.

docs.title: Step 2: local content change
docs.text:
Create A2 while keeping B1 and C1 unchanged.

Create S2 from S1:

A -> A2
B -> B1
C -> C1

Verify:

  • S1 is still readable;
  • S2 differs from S1;
  • B1 and C1 keep the same RevisionId values;
  • no unrelated entity revision was recreated;
  • main advances from S1 to S2 using compare-and-set.

docs.title: Step 3: branch
docs.text:
Starting from S1, create S3 by changing only B:

A -> A1
B -> B2
C -> C1

Keep S2 and S3 simultaneously readable.

Do not implement semantic merge. This step only proves branch storage.

docs.title: Step 4: stale promotion
docs.text:
Attempt to promote main from expected S1 to S3 after it already points at S2.

Verify:

  • operation fails with the typed stale-root conflict;
  • main still points to S2;
  • S3 remains readable as an immutable snapshot.

docs.title: Step 5: durability
docs.text:
Run the scenario using a temporary SQLite database.

Close and reopen it.

Verify:

  • main still resolves to S2;
  • S1, S2, and S3 remain readable;
  • all revision and snapshot IDs match those created before reopen.

docs.title: Step 6: cross-backend identity
docs.text:
Run the same logical scenario against the in-memory backend.

Verify the memory and SQLite implementations produce identical logical revision and snapshot IDs for identical canonical content and mappings.

docs.title: Step 7: reachability and GC
docs.text:
Treat main -> S2 as protected and leave S3 unprotected.

Run GC dry-run.

Verify it identifies only storage that is genuinely unreachable under the implemented retention rules.

If the ancestry/history policy used by the implementation retains S1, confirm the report reflects that policy.

Run destructive GC only after recording the dry-run result.

After GC, every protected snapshot must pass integrity verification.

docs.title: Implementation corrections allowed
docs.text:
If the scenario exposes a problem, fix it in the owning crate.

Allowed corrections include:

  • missing trait methods required by existing Level 2 designs;
  • inconsistent error categories;
  • backend identity divergence;
  • failure to preserve historical snapshots;
  • unsafe root promotion;
  • structural-sharing implementation bugs;
  • integrity or reachability bugs;
  • missing tests.

Do not introduce unrelated product features.

docs.title: Documentation checks
docs.text:
Ensure public Rust modules have concise documentation explaining:

  • entity versus revision versus snapshot;
  • immutable revisions;
  • named-root compare-and-set behavior;
  • backend independence.

Do not duplicate the design documents into API docs; link concepts through concise explanations.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
At minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

If the repository has established additional checks by the time this task runs, run them too.

docs.title: Final checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Workspace compiles without higher-level agent/domain dependencies.
  • [ ] Memory and SQLite stores implement the same public persistence contract.
  • [ ] Immutable historical snapshots remain readable.
  • [ ] Deep/local changes preserve unrelated revision identities.
  • [ ] Any canonical map change creates a different snapshot identity.
  • [ ] Equivalent canonical state produces the same IDs across backends.
  • [ ] Named-root promotion is compare-and-set and atomic.
  • [ ] SQLite state survives reopen.
  • [ ] Reachability and GC preserve protected state.
  • [ ] Integrity verification passes on retained state.
  • [ ] Formatting, tests, and clippy pass.

When every item is satisfied, stop. Do not proceed into migrations, domain adapters, agents, CLI, server, or web implementation; those belong to later design documents.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement Change Queries and Progressive Summaries
Goal
docs.text:
Implement the backend-independent query and compact-inspection layer for change history.

The result must let database-only applications, CLI/API surfaces, and future agents ask useful questions without loading full migration bodies or domain-specific representations.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially sections 36, 42, 43, 45 through 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. Existing migration, history, branch, diff, conflict, and merge types.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/src/query.rs
crates/sr-change/src/summary.rs
crates/sr-change/src/history.rs
crates/sr-change/src/branch.rs
crates/sr-change/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

docs.title: Query service
docs.text:
Provide a backend-independent service or set of functions capable of answering at least:

what changed between snapshots A and B?
what migration introduced revision R?
what is the history of entity E?
which migrations touched entity E?
what branches descend from snapshot S?
what is the common ancestor of A and B?
what conflicts prevent merging A and B?
which changes came from branch/workspace W?

Use existing store/history abstractions. Do not reach into backend tables.

docs.title: Query result types
docs.text:
Return structured data, not formatted prose.

Each result should contain stable identifiers/handles that callers can use for deeper queries.

For example, entity history results should carry:

EntityId
RevisionId before/after
Migration reference
SnapshotId where visible
optional branch/workspace provenance

Do not return only filenames, line numbers, or free-form descriptions.

docs.title: Pagination and bounded results
docs.text:
For potentially large queries, design result types so pagination or cursors can be added or used without changing meaning.

If the existing store/query conventions already provide cursors, use them.

Do not force every call to materialize all descendants or all migrations in memory when a bounded form is possible.

docs.title: Structural summaries
docs.text: Implement deterministic compact summaries for:

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
At minimum:

base snapshot
result snapshot
source category
introduced count
removed count
modified count
semantic operation count
validation reference count

docs.title: Diff
docs.text:
At minimum:

left/right snapshots
introduced count
removed count
modified count

docs.title: Branch/workspace
docs.text:
At minimum:

branch/workspace reference
base snapshot
current snapshot
status
short title/description if present
resulting migration if present

docs.title: Merge result
docs.text:
At minimum:

base/left/right
resolved entity count
conflict count
conflict kinds by count

These are structural facts. Do not invoke an LLM or create generated prose in sr-change.

docs.title: Progressive disclosure
docs.text:
Support at least three conceptual levels through APIs/types:

summary
structured detail
exact referenced revisions/operations

A caller should be able to list many migrations/branches using summaries and then inspect one item deeply.

Do not make full migration payload loading mandatory for branch lists if storage can provide summary metadata separately.

docs.title: Branch descriptions
docs.text:
Expose authored or already-derived title/purpose/description/outcome fields when available.

Preserve their provenance/reference rather than pretending structural summaries generated them.

The query layer should not synthesize semantic conclusions.

docs.title: Generic operation without domain adapter
docs.text:
Every query in this task must remain meaningful if no domain adapter is loaded.

Domain-aware callers may enrich returned identifiers later.

For example, generic history must still say:

Entity E changed R1 -> R2

without knowing that E is a function or paragraph.

docs.title: Cross-domain migration
docs.text:
Add tests where one migration changes entities from different domain/type categories.

The generic query/summary layer must return all changes in one migration without assuming one file, one language, or one adapter.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
When a query returns an ordered collection without semantic order, sort using stable canonical identifiers.

Do not rely on hash-map, database, or insertion order.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Add tests for:

  • changed-between query delegates to semantic diff and returns stable handles;
  • migration that introduced a revision can be found;
  • entity history returns correct ordered transitions;
  • migrations touching an entity are returned deterministically;
  • descendant branch query uses explicit ancestry;
  • common ancestor query returns topology result, not timestamp result;
  • workspace provenance query filters correctly;
  • migration summary counts match exact deltas;
  • merge summary reports conflict kinds correctly;
  • branch list can use compact metadata;
  • cross-domain migration is fully visible without adapters;
  • queries remain valid when descriptions are absent.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• No prose-generation model calls.
  • No concrete backend SQL.
  • No domain-specific assumptions.
  • No physical write-order semantics.
  • No hidden full-object reads solely to render a one-line list when structured summary data is available.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo check --workspace

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Required history/change questions have structured APIs.
  • [ ] Results expose stable handles.
  • [ ] Structural summaries exist for migration, diff, branch/workspace, and merge.
  • [ ] Progressive disclosure is possible.
  • [ ] Cross-domain changes remain understandable generically.
  • [ ] Ordering is deterministic.
  • [ ] No agent/domain/backend dependency was introduced.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text: Report the query methods/types added, how large result sets are bounded, which structural summaries were implemented, and the cross-domain tests added.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement @scriberig/components-mui as the opinionated Material UI interpretation of Scriberig's public web model and interaction primitives.

The package may make strong visual and composition choices, but it must not reimplement protocol access, caching, selection, command discovery, migration semantics, or event processing.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement react bindings.md
  5. design/level-3/007. implement neutral reusable components.md

Prerequisite: public React bindings and neutral components compile.

docs.text:
Create:

web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiObjectTree.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiObjectInspector.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiRelationBrowser.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiHistoryView.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiSemanticDiffView.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiMigrationPreview.tsx
web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiSessionTree.tsx

web/packages/components-mui/src/MuiCommandPalette.tsx

web/packages/components-mui/test/components-mui.test.tsx

Update:

web/packages/components-mui/src/index.ts
web/packages/components-mui/package.json

docs.title: MUI Boundary
docs.text:
MUI is allowed only in this package and consuming applications.

Do not modify lower reusable packages to accept MUI-specific props, theme types, icons, or component instances.

Where a lower component already provides sufficient structure, wrap or compose it.

Where an MUI implementation needs different markup for quality, consume the same hooks/controllers directly rather than copying their state logic.

docs.title: Theme Contract
docs.text:
Provide a small optional Scriberig theme helper in theme.ts.

It may define component defaults and semantic tokens for concepts such as:

  • current/historical/stale state;
  • success/warning/error/conflict;
  • selected semantic objects;
  • agent/operation status.

Do not create a hard requirement that consumers use the provided theme.

Components must work within an existing host MUI theme.

docs.title: Tree and Inspector
docs.text:
MuiObjectTree must use MUI controls/layout while preserving lazy loading, semantic selection, pagination, and keyboard behavior from the reusable layers.

MuiObjectInspector should use application-ready sections/cards/tables where appropriate for identity, revision, description, properties, relations, and stale/historical state.

Do not query the client directly if a public hook/controller already exposes the required data.

docs.title: Relation, History, and Diff Views
docs.text:
Implement MUI versions of relation browsing, history navigation, and semantic diff display.

The semantic diff renderer must clearly distinguish:

  • added;
  • removed;
  • changed;
  • moved/structural changes when protocol supports them;
  • conflicts/ambiguous states where relevant.

Do not compute semantic diffs in the UI package.

docs.title: Migration Preview
docs.text:
MuiMigrationPreview should provide a review-oriented composition suitable for accepting or rejecting a proposed migration.

Display:

  • base/candidate snapshot context;
  • affected objects;
  • semantic changes;
  • validation result;
  • stale/conflict warnings;
  • permitted apply/reject actions.

Mutating actions must use public command/client operations.

docs.title: Session and Agent Components
docs.text:
MuiSessionTree and MuiBranchView preserve the structured session model.

MuiAgentPanel should combine:

  • active session/branch context;
  • current semantic selection/scope;
  • command input;
  • durable operation progress;
  • streamed agent output if available;
  • resulting branch/migration/validation/snapshot references.

The panel must not construct line-number-oriented prompts from source text when semantic selection is available.

Do not make the agent panel a private transport client; use public agent operations.

docs.title: Command Palette
docs.text:
Implement MuiCommandPalette over the universal command descriptors from editor-core/React bindings.

It should:

  • show commands applicable to current semantic selection and capabilities;
  • support keyboard invocation/search;
  • distinguish mutating commands where useful;
  • invoke the same command descriptor used by other controls.

Do not maintain a separate hard-coded list of application commands.

docs.title: Projection Host
docs.text:
MuiProjectionHost provides MUI framing around registered domain projection handlers.

It may add toolbars, status indicators, snapshot/stale banners, and command access, but domain rendering/editing remains supplied through public extension handlers.

Do not hard-code one source editor implementation in this task.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Use MUI accessibility support but preserve explicit semantic labels and keyboard operation.

Required:

  • keyboard-accessible tree and command palette;
  • visible focus;
  • labeled icon-only controls;
  • status messages that are not communicated by color alone;
  • stale/conflict states exposed textually and semantically.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Required tests:

  1. components render under a normal external MUI theme;
  2. components also render under the optional Scriberig theme helper;
  3. selection propagates through MuiObjectTree to shared selection state;
  4. command palette uses editor-core command discovery;
  5. migration preview invokes public apply operation rather than local mutation;
  6. agent panel sends structured semantic scope with commands;
  7. no import reaches into another package's private src path;
  8. stale/conflict state is visible without relying only on color.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run:

pnpm --filter @scriberig/components-mui typecheck
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components-mui test
pnpm --filter @scriberig/components-mui build
pnpm typecheck

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not add semantic caches.
  • Do not reimplement event handling.
  • Do not hard-code server endpoint URLs.
  • Do not import database/server internals.
  • Do not modify lower packages to require MUI.
  • Do not make agent commands textual/file-line based when semantic selection exists.
  • Do not implement the reference app's routing/layout here.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All prescribed MUI components exist.
  • [ ] Lower packages remain MUI-free.
  • [ ] MUI components consume public hooks/controllers.
  • [ ] A reusable command palette exists.
  • [ ] Agent panel sends structured scope and exposes semantic results.
  • [ ] Migration review uses public operations.
  • [ ] Theme helper is optional.
  • [ ] Accessibility states are explicit.
  • [ ] Required tests and workspace typecheck pass.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the first PDF domain/import adapter in scriberig-domain-pdf.

PDFs are treated primarily as imported source artifacts whose exact bytes are preserved, while extracted text, layout, tables, figures, and semantic structure are represented as derived knowledge with explicit provenance.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/002. universal knowledge model.md
  2. design/level-1/007. domain modeling and adapters.md
  3. design/level-3/001. scaffold domain adapter crates.md
  4. current blob/artifact and provenance APIs in the shared knowledge model

docs.title: Files to Create or Update
docs.text:
Inside crates/domains/pdf/, create or update:

src/lib.rs
src/schema.rs
src/import.rs
src/extract.rs
src/geometry.rs
src/provenance.rs
src/error.rs

Add tests under:

tests/import.rs
tests/extraction.rs

If exact binary/blob storage is owned by another shared crate, call that API rather than implementing binary storage locally.

docs.title: Domain Vocabulary
docs.text:
Define or register PDF-domain entities needed for the first implementation slice:

PDFDocument
PDFPage
TextRegion
Paragraph
Table
TableRow
TableCell
Figure
Annotation

The extracted Paragraph, Table, TableRow, and TableCell concepts may reuse compatible universal/document concepts where the shared schema model supports cross-domain reuse. Do not duplicate concepts merely because they came from a PDF.

docs.title: Source Artifact
docs.text:
The original PDF bytes must be preservable as an exact imported source artifact.

The PDF document/domain entity must be able to reference that source artifact with provenance.

The exact source bytes are distinct from extracted semantic structure.

Do not treat extracted text as an exact replacement for the PDF.

docs.title: Extraction Dependency
docs.text:
Choose one mature PDF parsing/extraction library suitable for the first implementation slice, unless one is already selected elsewhere.

Do not add OCR in this task unless the selected parser requires it for all text extraction. OCR should remain a later optional producer because it has different confidence and dependency characteristics.

Parser/extractor private object IDs must not become Scriberig semantic identity.

docs.title: Pages and Geometry
docs.text:
Represent page-level geometry needed to map semantic entities back to the source.

At minimum support:

page number
page dimensions
bounding region/rectangle for extracted region entities where available

Geometry is source/projection metadata used for source highlighting and provenance.

Coordinates must not replace semantic identity.

docs.title: Extraction Provenance
docs.text:
Every extracted or inferred entity must record enough provenance to identify:

source PDF artifact
source page
extractor/producer
extractor version/profile where relevant
source region/geometry where available
confidence where the producer supplies a meaningful confidence value

Do not fabricate confidence values when the extractor does not provide a meaningful score.

docs.title: Canonical vs Derived Rules
docs.text:
Treat the exact imported source artifact and explicit import relationship as authoritative imported evidence.

Treat these as derived unless a later design explicitly promotes them:

extracted text regions
paragraph segmentation
reading order
table detection
row/cell segmentation
figure classification
semantic summaries
OCR output

The store may contain several extraction results from different producers at the same time.

Do not overwrite an older extraction merely because a new extractor produces a better result.

docs.title: Initial Import API
docs.text:
Expose an API usable without agents that can conceptually:

import PDF bytes/file reference -> PDFDocument/source artifact
run extractor -> derived page/region entities and relations

Use universal graph/provenance APIs.

Do not create a PDF-specific persistence database.

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
The produced structure should support navigation:

PDFDocument
  -> PDFPage
     -> TextRegion/Paragraph/Table/Figure
        -> TableRow
           -> TableCell

A caller should be able to list pages and page child counts without loading all extracted text.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Use small checked-in PDF fixtures with known content where repository policy permits binary test fixtures; otherwise generate deterministic fixtures during tests.

Test at least:

  • original source artifact is preserved/referenced;
  • document exposes ordered pages;
  • extracted paragraph/region has page provenance;
  • region geometry maps back to the source page where available;
  • a table extraction produces row/cell structure when supported by the chosen extractor;
  • extracted facts are marked derived rather than canonical source bytes;
  • two producer profiles can coexist without overwriting each other's derived output;
  • semantic identity does not depend on page byte offsets or extractor-private IDs.

Run:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p scriberig-domain-pdf
cargo clippy -p scriberig-domain-pdf --all-targets -- -D warnings

docs.title: Do Not Do
docs.text:
• Do not implement a PDF editor.
  • Do not treat extracted text as authoritative exact content.
  • Do not add model summaries.
  • Do not add OCR unless unavoidable for the selected baseline extractor.
  • Do not invent confidence values.
  • Do not use page coordinates as semantic IDs.
  • Do not create private SQL tables for PDF structure.
  • Do not depend on agent crates.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] PDF source artifact can be preserved and referenced.
  • [ ] PDFDocument/PDFPage structure uses the universal graph.
  • [ ] Extracted regions and semantic structures are derived with provenance.
  • [ ] Geometry is available as source mapping metadata where possible.
  • [ ] Page/region hierarchy supports progressive disclosure.
  • [ ] Multiple extractor outputs can coexist.
  • [ ] No PDF-specific persistence architecture exists.
  • [ ] Tests, formatting, and clippy pass.

docs.title: Implement: Projection Specifications, Rendering, and Adapter API
Objective
docs.text:
Complete the domain-independent sr-projection API so higher layers can define persistent projection specifications, render deterministic outputs, and plug in editable domain adapters without depending on filesystem or agent code.

This task builds on the projection scaffolding task and should leave sr-projection usable by a non-agent embedding application.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  3. design/level-3/007. bootstrap projection crates and core contracts.md

Also inspect existing public APIs in sr-core, sr-store, and sr-change before adding types.

docs.title: Files to modify
docs.text:
Primarily:

crates/sr-projection/src/model.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/style.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/render.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/adapter.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/reconcile.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/diagnostic.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection/tests/projection_conformance.rs

Create focused extra modules only if a responsibility cannot remain clear in the prescribed files.

docs.title: Projection specification
docs.text:
Implement a public projection specification structure that can express:

  • stable projection/spec identity or entity reference;
  • semantic scope to render;
  • ProjectionKind;
  • ProjectionClass;
  • exact style revision/reference;
  • adapter identity/version;
  • renderer version;
  • ownership policy at the generic level;
  • adapter/domain configuration through a typed/opaque extension mechanism.

Do not store runtime dirty state inside the immutable user-meaningful specification.

Do not use a path as the projection ID.

docs.title: Deterministic render request
docs.text:
Create a request type that contains every generic input needed to reproduce output:

projection specification/reference
semantic scope
exact snapshot or exact resolved revisions
style revision
renderer version
rendering context

The API should make it obvious when a caller supplies only a moving/current reference rather than an exact snapshot. Deterministic render/cache paths should use exact inputs.

docs.title: Rendered output
docs.text:
Create a result type containing:

  • bytes or an adapter-neutral payload capable of text/binary representation;
  • media/projection kind metadata;
  • exact output digest/hash;
  • exact semantic/style/renderer inputs used;
  • optional fragment/cache metadata owned by the adapter;
  • deterministic/non-deterministic marker if the API supports non-reproducible renderers.

For the first implementation, deterministic renderers are the default and preferred case.

Use a stable digest mechanism already selected by the project; do not invent a different hash family unless necessary.

docs.title: Style reference behavior
docs.text:
Style used for deterministic output must resolve to exact immutable configuration.

If the system supports aliases such as user-default, resolve the alias before constructing the final render-cache identity. The alias itself must not be treated as immutable input if it can move.

Add tests proving two style revisions can produce distinct cache/input identities without changing the semantic object revision.

docs.title: Adapter trait
docs.text:
Implement the adapter trait so one domain adapter can provide:

capabilities()
render(...)
parse(...)
reconcile(...)
validate(...)

Requirements:

  • parsing and reconciliation are separate calls/responsibilities;
  • candidate parsed structures remain adapter-owned;
  • the generic trait does not require Markdown/source AST types;
  • reconciliation can return no-op, migration proposal, ambiguity, conflict, or invalid state;
  • validation can return structured diagnostics;
  • read-only adapters are not forced to implement meaningful parse/reconcile behavior beyond an explicit unsupported result.

Prefer compile-time separation/associated types where practical over Any downcasting.

docs.title: Reconciliation context
docs.text:
Provide a context type containing references needed for bidirectional editing:

  • last synchronization base snapshot/state;
  • current canonical snapshot/state;
  • semantic scope;
  • projection specification;
  • adapter/domain metadata needed to interpret the candidate.

Do not include filesystem watcher events in this type.

docs.title: Error model
docs.text:
Use structured error enums with sources.

At minimum distinguish:

  • unsupported operation;
  • bad projection configuration;
  • rendering failure;
  • parse failure;
  • reconciliation ambiguity/conflict;
  • validation failure;
  • stale/missing synchronization base;
  • storage/change-layer failure where propagated.

Do not use panics for malformed external content or unsupported adapter capabilities.

docs.title: Conformance tests
docs.text:
Add fake adapters in tests rather than using Markdown yet.

Cover:

  • deterministic render call returns exact input metadata;
  • exact same render request can produce identical digest;
  • different style revision is visible in render identity;
  • read-only adapter rejects edit import cleanly;
  • editable fake adapter performs parse then reconciliation as distinct operations;
  • NoSemanticChange carries no migration;
  • conflict/ambiguity remains structured;
  • no agent/server/filesystem dependency appears in sr-projection.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add actual filesystem synchronization.
  • Do not add Markdown parsing.
  • Do not define HTTP types.
  • Do not add model/provider or agent dependencies.
  • Do not bypass sr-change with an independent commit mechanism.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Projection specs separate immutable configuration from runtime state.
  • [ ] Render requests use exact reproducible inputs.
  • [ ] Output digest and input metadata are available.
  • [ ] Style aliases are resolved before exact render identity is formed.
  • [ ] Adapter parse/reconcile lifecycle is explicit.
  • [ ] Structured outcomes/errors are tested.
  • [ ] Workspace tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Agent Task: Implement the Change Subsystem Conformance Suite
Goal
docs.text:
Complete crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs as an end-to-end executable specification of the architectural invariants from design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md.

This task should add tests and only the minimal production fixes required to make already-designed behavior conform. Do not redesign public APIs opportunistically from the test task.

docs.title: Read before editing
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/005. changes migrations branches and merge.md, especially section 49.
  2. design/level-2/002. change history and merge crate design.md.
  3. All Level 3 tasks 001 through 008 and the resulting implementations.
  4. The in-memory store conformance API from sr-store-memory.

docs.title: Primary file
docs.text:
crates/sr-change/tests/change_conformance.rs

Production files may be modified only when a test reveals a real mismatch with the approved designs.

docs.title: Test environment
docs.text:
Use sr-store-memory as the default backend for this suite.

Build small fixtures through public APIs only. Do not reach into internal hash maps or private store fields to construct states.

Create helper functions for:

empty/base snapshot creation
entity/revision creation
snapshot descendant creation
migration creation
branch/workspace setup
named-root setup

Keep helpers deterministic and small.

docs.title: Required scenario 1: exact direct migration
docs.text:
Create S1 containing entity E -> R1.

Create S2 containing E -> R2.

Record migration M1 from S1 to S2.

Verify:

  • S1 still resolves E -> R1;
  • S2 resolves E -> R2;
  • migration base/result are exact;
  • delta is exactly R1 -> R2;
  • history query finds M1 as touching E.

docs.title: Required scenario 2: creation and semantic removal
docs.text:
From one base:

  • introduce entity A;
  • remove entity B from the next canonical state.

Verify creation/removal delta classification and that historical snapshots still resolve retained old state.

Do not assert physical garbage collection.

docs.title: Required scenario 3: branches are cheap lines of work
docs.text:
Create two branches/workspaces from the same base snapshot.

Advance each independently.

Verify:

  • shared base remains unchanged;
  • each branch points to its own descendant;
  • branch creation did not duplicate semantic entities/revisions;
  • both results remain queryable.

Use public store metrics only if such metrics exist. Otherwise prove sharing through identical snapshot/revision identities rather than backend internals.

docs.title: Required scenario 4: optimistic promotion
docs.text:
Set:

main -> S1

Create workspaces producing S2 and S3 from S1.

Promote S2 with expected S1; it must succeed.

Attempt to promote S3 with expected S1; it must fail as stale and report actual S2.

Verify S3 remains available and no work was overwritten.

docs.title: Required scenario 5: arbitrary semantic diff
docs.text:
Build:

S1 -> S2 -> S4
 \
  -> S3

Compare:

  • S1 with S4;
  • S2 with S3;
  • a snapshot with itself.

Verify diff correctness without requiring direct ancestry.

docs.title: Required scenario 6: disjoint merge
docs.text:
Base contains entities A@A1 and B@B1.

Left changes only A.

Right changes only B.

Three-way merge must resolve both automatically with zero conflicts.

Verify base, left, and right remain unchanged.

docs.title: Required scenario 7: convergent merge
docs.text:
Both descendants independently produce the same exact revision for one entity.

Merge must converge to that revision without conflict.

History may remain distinct even though resulting state is equal.

docs.title: Required scenario 8: competing edit conflict
docs.text:
Both sides modify the same entity to different revisions.

Verify:

  • conflict kind is BothModified or the approved equivalent;
  • base/left/right revision handles are present;
  • no side is silently selected;
  • unrelated disjoint changes remain in resolved output.

docs.title: Required scenario 9: delete/modify conflict
docs.text:
One side removes an entity while the other modifies it.

Verify a structured DeleteModify conflict and no textual conflict-marker dependency.

docs.title: Required scenario 10: rebase preserves original history
docs.text:
Create original work S1 -> S2.

Create newer base S1 -> S3 affecting unrelated state.

Rebase original work onto S3 to produce S4.

Verify:

  • S2 and its migration still exist unchanged;
  • S4 descends from S3;
  • semantic intent was replayed;
  • history query can distinguish original and rebased paths.

docs.title: Required scenario 11: rebase conflict
docs.text:
Create original work modifying E.

Create new base modifying the same E differently.

Rebase must return a structured conflict rather than overwrite the new base.

docs.title: Required scenario 12: history topology ignores insertion order
docs.text:
Persist migration/history records in an order different from logical ancestry where the test infrastructure permits it.

Verify ancestry/common-ancestor/entity-history queries use explicit references and still return correct topology.

docs.title: Required scenario 13: move preserves entity continuity
docs.text:
Represent a structural move of one existing entity between generic collections/owners.

Verify:

  • the moved entity retains its EntityId;
  • structural owners change as required;
  • history describes a move/structural change rather than unrelated delete/create when continuity is known.

docs.title: Required scenario 14: cross-domain universal migration
docs.text:
Create entities with at least two different generic type/domain identities.

Change them atomically in one migration/snapshot transition.

Without loading any domain adapter, verify:

  • all entity deltas are visible;
  • summary counts are correct;
  • query APIs do not assume one file or language;
  • provenance is preserved.

docs.title: Required scenario 15: representation-only change creates no migration
docs.text:
Simulate or construct the highest-level available representation/style change that leaves canonical entity revisions identical.

Verify:

  • canonical snapshot identity remains equal where the underlying snapshot model says state is identical;
  • no semantic migration is manufactured;
  • derived/render artifacts may change independently if those APIs are available.

Do not create a fake empty migration to satisfy this test.

docs.title: Required scenario 16: compact navigation summaries
docs.text:
Create a migration with several changes and a branch/workspace with description metadata.

Verify summary APIs return:

  • exact handles;
  • counts;
  • branch status/base/current snapshots;
  • short metadata where present;

without requiring domain adapters.

docs.title: Determinism checks
docs.text:
Repeat relevant diff/query construction with different insertion order.

Verify public result ordering remains deterministic.

Do not snapshot-test unstable debug formatting unless repository convention explicitly uses it.

docs.title: Backend independence check
docs.text:
Inspect sr-change dependencies as part of review.

The library must not depend on:

sr-store-memory
sr-store-sqlite

except that sr-store-memory may appear under dev-dependencies for tests.

No production source file may import concrete backend implementation types.

docs.title: No domain leakage check
docs.text:
Search sr-change production code for domain-specific types.

The universal crate must not contain special cases for:

Rust AST
Markdown
PDF
session agent behavior
filesystem line offsets

Generic extension traits are allowed.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run at minimum:

cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-change
cargo test -p sr-store-memory
cargo test --workspace
cargo check --workspace

Run clippy if it is part of repository CI.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All 16 scenarios are implemented as real tests.
  • [ ] Direct migration preserves old state.
  • [ ] Branching and stale promotion are covered.
  • [ ] Arbitrary diff is covered.
  • [ ] Disjoint and convergent merge are covered.
  • [ ] Both-modified and delete/modify conflicts are covered.
  • [ ] Rebase success and conflict are covered.
  • [ ] History is independent of insertion order.
  • [ ] Move continuity is covered.
  • [ ] Cross-domain migration works without adapters.
  • [ ] Representation-only change does not create semantic history.
  • [ ] Compact summaries are covered.
  • [ ] Production crate has no concrete backend dependency.
  • [ ] Workspace tests pass.

docs.title: Final response from implementing agent
docs.text:
Provide:

  1. the list of conformance scenarios implemented;
  2. any production defects discovered and fixed;
  3. exact commands run and outcomes;
  4. any Level 1 invariant that could not be tested because another subsystem is not implemented yet.

Do not weaken or skip a required invariant silently. If a dependency is genuinely missing, leave the test as a clearly documented blocked scenario rather than fabricating behavior.

docs.title: Implement: Filesystem Projection Ownership, Hashing, and Atomic IO
Objective
docs.text:
Implement the low-level filesystem primitives required by managed file projections without adding watcher integration or domain parsing yet.

This task establishes explicit ownership, normalized locations, exact-byte hashing, and safe writes in sr-projection-fs.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
Read:

  1. design/level-1/006. projections and bidirectional editing.md
  2. design/level-2/008. filesystem projection synchronization.md
  3. design/level-2/007. projection crate boundaries and core model.md
  4. design/level-3/008. implement projection specifications rendering and adapter api.md

docs.title: Files to create/modify
docs.text:
crates/sr-projection-fs/Cargo.toml
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/lib.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/location.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/ownership.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/hash.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/io.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/src/state.rs
crates/sr-projection-fs/tests/sync_conformance.rs

Do not create watcher-specific modules in this task beyond placeholders already required by lib.rs.

docs.title: location.rs
docs.text:
Define a filesystem projection location type around a path.

Requirements:

  • path is not a semantic EntityId;
  • preserve enough information to access the exact file;
  • define normalization/comparison behavior explicitly and conservatively;
  • avoid canonicalizing through filesystem IO as part of ordinary equality if it would make missing paths impossible to represent;
  • expose path accessors without leaking platform-specific watcher types.

Add tests for relative/absolute handling according to the chosen project-root policy.

docs.title: ownership.rs
docs.text:
Implement:

ManagedEditable
ManagedReadOnly
Unmanaged
ImportedExternal

Represent ownership separately from existence/dirty state.

Add helpers answering at least:

  • Scriberig may render/write this file;
  • external changes may be imported;
  • Scriberig must never rewrite it automatically.

Unmanaged must always reject automatic write/import ownership operations.

docs.title: hash.rs
docs.text:
Implement exact-byte digesting for file content and rendered output.

Requirements:

  • reuse project-standard digest/hash implementation if available;
  • hash exact bytes for the initial design;
  • expose a strongly typed file-content digest if appropriate;
  • support hashing bytes already in memory and file contents read from disk;
  • errors are returned, not panicked.

Add tests proving byte differences, including newline/spacing changes, change the file digest even though later domain reconciliation may find no semantic change.

docs.title: io.rs
docs.text:
Implement a small filesystem IO abstraction used by synchronization code.

It must support:

read(path) -> exact bytes
metadata/existence(path)
write_atomic(path, bytes)
remove/rename inspection helpers only if needed by later sync code

Provide a concrete local-filesystem implementation and a trait/interface that tests can replace if useful.

docs.title: Atomic write behavior
docs.text:
For write_atomic:

  1. create a temporary sibling file where practical;
  2. write all bytes;
  3. flush/close as required for correctness of the chosen guarantee;
  4. replace target atomically where supported;
  5. clean up failed temporary artifacts best-effort;
  6. return the digest of exact bytes known to have been written or enough data for the caller to compute/verify it.

Do not claim stronger crash-durability guarantees than implemented. The requirement is to avoid exposing half-written projection content during a normal process write.

Preserve reasonable file permissions where the implementation can do so safely; document limitations in code comments/tests rather than inventing a complex permission system here.

docs.title: state.rs
docs.text:
Add the filesystem-facing runtime sync-state value needed by later tasks.

It should be able to carry:

  • projection/spec reference;
  • location;
  • ownership;
  • last synchronized snapshot/base reference;
  • last rendered digest;
  • optional last observed digest;
  • projection lifecycle state from sr-projection;
  • adapter/style/renderer exact references needed to interpret the base.

Do not implement persistence backend tables in this task. Make the state serializable only if the workspace already has a standard serialization dependency and doing so does not couple it to a concrete backend.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Using a temporary directory, cover:

  • atomic write creates expected exact bytes;
  • returned/computed digest matches file bytes;
  • subsequent replacement produces the new exact bytes;
  • failed target path returns a structured error;
  • unmanaged ownership denies automatic writes through any high-level helper added here;
  • exact-byte formatting changes change digest;
  • semantic IDs are not derived from path text.

docs.title: Commands to run
docs.text:
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p sr-projection-fs
cargo test --workspace

docs.title: Do not do
docs.text:
• Do not add filesystem watcher library integration.
  • Do not parse or reconcile Markdown.
  • Do not treat a digest difference as a semantic migration.
  • Do not create SQL storage tables.
  • Do not import an unmanaged file automatically.
  • Do not implement agent or UI APIs.

docs.title: Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Ownership model is explicit and tested.
  • [ ] File locations are separate from semantic identity.
  • [ ] Exact-byte hashing works.
  • [ ] Atomic replacement works in normal local filesystem tests.
  • [ ] Runtime sync-state type can carry the required synchronization base metadata.
  • [ ] No watcher/domain/agent code was introduced.
  • [ ] Tests pass.

Stop after these conditions are met.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Implement the full Scriberig reference web application under web/apps/scriberig using only public web packages.

The application must demonstrate that the public web platform is sufficient to build the complete editor described by Level 1. It combines low-level knowledge browsing, semantic/domain views, projections, history/diffs, sessions/agents, migrations, validation, and long-running operations around one shared semantic selection.

Read before editing:

  1. design/level-1/012. web platform and integrated editor.md
  2. design/level-2/001. web workspace packages and integrated editor.md
  3. design/level-3/005. implement headless editor core primitives.md
  4. design/level-3/006. implement react bindings.md
  5. design/level-3/007. implement neutral reusable components.md
  6. design/level-3/008. implement material ui component package.md

Prerequisites:

  • all public web packages compile;
  • the runtime/server exposes enough of the public protocol to connect the app;
  • if some server capability is not yet available, the app must show an explicit unsupported state rather than use a private workaround.

The controlling rule is:

If this application needs a private server call, direct database access, or private package import, fix the public abstraction instead of bypassing it.

docs.title: Files to Create or Replace
docs.text:
Create:

web/apps/scriberig/src/app-shell.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/routes.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/runtime.ts
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/RawKnowledgeView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/SemanticView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/ProjectionView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/HistoryView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/SessionAgentView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/OperationsView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/views/MigrationReviewView.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/SnapshotStatus.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/SelectionSummary.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/components/UnsupportedCapability.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/test/app-public-boundary.test.ts

Update:

web/apps/scriberig/src/main.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/src/App.tsx
web/apps/scriberig/package.json
web/apps/scriberig/vite.config.ts

Do not create semantic logic in apps/scriberig that belongs in reusable packages.

docs.title: Runtime Composition
docs.text:
runtime.ts creates the application runtime from public packages.

It should construct/configure equivalents of:

public transport
Scriberig client
WorkspaceModel
SelectionController
extension/command registry

Configuration such as API base URL and authentication provider must enter through application configuration/environment, not hard-coded source constants.

The runtime should be injectable or replaceable enough for application tests.

docs.title: Application Provider Composition
docs.text:
App.tsx should compose:

  • MUI theme/provider;
  • @scriberig/react provider;
  • application routing/shell;
  • one shared selection controller/runtime;
  • connection/snapshot status.

Do not create a separate model/client instance per view.

docs.title: App Shell
docs.text:
Create a simple, maintainable workbench layout.

The first implementation does not need docking or persistent layouts.

It should expose navigation to these main surfaces:

Raw Knowledge
Semantic
Projection
History / Diff
Session / Agent
Operations
Migration Review when active

A practical initial layout may use:

  • top application bar with current snapshot/connection state;
  • left navigation or semantic tree area;
  • central active view;
  • optional right inspector/agent area.

The exact arrangement is less important than shared selection and public-package use.

docs.title: Universal Selection Integration
docs.text:
All major views must consume the same SelectionController through @scriberig/react.

Required behavior:

  • selecting an entity in Raw Knowledge updates Semantic and History views;
  • selecting an object in Semantic view updates inspector/agent scope;
  • selecting a mapped semantic region in Projection view updates global selection;
  • agent commands receive the active semantic selection;
  • migration review can highlight affected selected entities;
  • historical exact selection remains historical and is visibly marked.

Do not translate selection into file path + line number as the primary internal representation.

docs.title: RawKnowledgeView
docs.text:
Provide the low-level supported database/knowledge browser using public APIs.

It must support progressively inspecting:

  • entities;
  • exact/current revisions;
  • typed properties/summary data;
  • relations/collections;
  • descriptions/provenance;
  • reverse references if public capability exists;
  • snapshot resolution;
  • migration lineage where available.

Use reusable tree/inspector/relation components.

Do not connect directly to SQLite or server-internal database endpoints.

docs.title: SemanticView
docs.text:
Show the selected entity through domain-aware extensions where available.

Fallback to the generic semantic inspector when no domain-specific view is registered.

The view should support progressive disclosure rather than loading an entire project/domain graph.

Examples that may later be supported through extensions:

code module/function/code group
Markdown document/section/paragraph/table
PDF document/page/table/figure
session/branch/decision/task

Do not hard-code each domain into the app shell if extension registration can supply it.

docs.title: ProjectionView
docs.text:
Host the public projection component/handler for the active semantic selection.

Display clearly:

  • projection identity;
  • snapshot/base identity;
  • read-only/editable capability;
  • stale/candidate/conflict state;
  • semantic mapping availability.

When edits are supported, they must produce public semantic operations/migration proposals.

Do not treat the browser text buffer as canonical state.

docs.title: HistoryView
docs.text:
